## Scanned page 006

TWO WORDS ABOUT SECOND EDITION

First part Prasiititantra and second part Striroga of Ayurvediya Prasiititantra
evam Striroga were published respectively twelve and eight years back. In the
intervening period of four years between publication of first and second part, few
important but unquoted references coming to light were presented in Appendix V
of Part HI, indicating relevant heading and page no. of Part I, however the text of
Part [ did not contain any hint of this fact, naturally the reader remained ingorant
about these, till he could read Appendix V of Part II. This difference of hundreds
of pages between exact text and relevant refereuce minimised the utility of these
teferences. Within the period of these eight years after publication of second part,
in the process of teaching, learning and study it was felt that few topics or even
chapters if rearranged will become more intelligible, Certain new references came
to light, few ideas and explanations flashed in mind. As J could not refrain myself
from conveying these references, ideas and explanations to learned readers, thus,
this modified, slightly rearranged / changed and elaborated second edition is pre-

sented with the fond hope that their constructive criticism will make my path of
jearning clearer and easier.

23rd, June 1998 Premvati Tewari

A ngst eight branches of ayurveda—

author says that @yurveda descended from divine or celestial to terrene or terrestrial
stage in its asranga (eight branches) shape. Sugruta has defined very vividly spe-
cific subjects of these eight branches, the clarity is again missing in Astaing-
Sangraha and AstangaHrdaya, which might have come up due to insistance on
comprehensive or summarized description in these classics. KaSyapa has also just
enumerated eight branches, however, Harita has detailed the subjects of these. It
appears, that during the period of Caraka a motion was set-in towards specializa-
tion, which attained maturity and stability during the period of SuSruta, thus all
these eight branches had their specialists. who probably wrote their compendiums.
The motion could not sustain for long, due to various social, political and economic
reasons again study of Gyurveda in its entirety started.

The subject of present book comes under ‘kaumdrabhrtya’, one of the eight
branches of ayurveda. To this particular speciality Caraka has used the term
‘kaumarabrtyaka’,  Susruta  ‘kaumdarabhrtya or  kaumdratantra’, Kasyapa
‘kaumarabhrtya’ and both Vagbhatas and Harita ‘bdlacikitsa’

As stated earlier, only Susruta and Harita have detailed the subjects of these
eight branches of dGyurveda. Cakrapini commenting upon the verse of
CarakaSamhita says that the subject concerned with bharana of kumara comes
under kaumarabhrtya. Laxicons explain the word ‘bharana’ as ‘procuring, carry-
ing, bearing or act of bearing also in womb, bringing, maintaining, supporting and
nourishing’ etc: Accordingly the subject concerned with achievement of concep-
tion, its maintenance and delivery, then its protection, support and nourishment
comes under the perview of kaumdrabhrtya. To know the physiopathologies of
achievement of conception, the knowledge of anatomy and physiology of female
reproductive system, descend of embryo as well as abnormalities of @rtava and
yonivyapad (menstrual and other gynecological disorders) is essential, because in
the presence of menstrual or other gynecoldgical disorders woman may not con-

ceive.

Sugruta says that subject related to bharana (explained “eaglier) of kumara
(child), wet-nurse, disorders of milk and their treatment, diseases: Of the child
caused by consumption of vitiated milk and affliction by grahas alotigwith their
treatment is described under kaum@rabhrtya. In further elaboration he writes that
features of all the nine grahas, treatment of skanda, apasmara (skandapasméra),
Sakuni, rewati, putanad, andha (andhaputana), mandika (mukhamandika),
Sitapitanaé and naigamesa al! balagrahas, gynecological disorders and the subject
described in S@rirasthana are included in kaumarabhrtya. Explaining this Dalhana
says that ‘physiology of menstruation and descend of embryo etc. described in
SGrirasthana also come under kaumdrabhrtya. Cakrapaini says that as antenatal
management, embryology, abortions, normal [abour, management of puerperium
and neonate, wet-nurse, breast milk and certain diseases of children are described

Commentators Indu and Aruuadatta have limited the perview of this branch to
the pediatrics, probably due to use of term ‘bala’ a ‘child’ by principal authors in
Astanga-Sangraha and AstangaHrdaya respectively. Arunadatta has explained that
due to immaturity of deha (body) dhatu and bala of the child, indistinguished state
of its age or Strength and influence of this Specific period of life, the -Management
of. the child is discussed in 4 separate branch, which also includes various measures
adopted to treat a child, qualities of wetnurse and her milk, diseases due to vitiated
milk and their treatment. Both these commentators are silent about the
branch of prasktitantra and striroga (obstetrics and gynecology).

Harita though used the term ‘balacikitsa’ yet has included measures or process
to achieve conception and its maintenance, delivery, puerperium and treatment of
diseases of children under this heading. In the Measures of achievement of con

tion, the knowledge of Synecological disorders 15 essential, which has already
mentioned earlier.

In olden days’ dyurvedika literature was written under monarchism,
birth and Proper brought-up of a son (Kumara) as a heir was very important.
Menstrual and gynecological disorders influence impregnation, non-observance of
regulations Prescribed or negligence during menstrual period, rtukala (optimum
period for fertilization) and Pregnancy as well as improper management during
labour can produce certain abnormalities in the child, similarly improper manage-
ment of puerperal woman can influence nourishment and brought-up of the child.
In other words, to get a physically and Psychologically healthy and handsome son,
knowledge of 8ynecological disorders alongwith their treatment, physio-patholo-
gies of menstrual cycle, pregnancy, labour, Puerperium alongwith their manage-
ment and treatment of disorders of these Stages is essential. I appears that due to
utmost importance of the child, it was made as pivot and entire Physio-pathologies
of woman revolved around it, Hypothesis becomes clearer with discription of
‘garbha, bala and kumdra’ three divisions of age of a child by Kasyapa. Garbha
Or embryo is nourished and maintained by the woman, naturally knowledge of her
Management becomes a Part of the Management of a child.

In manobhavagdra-mukha (vaginal canal) of females there are three n@dis: samirana,
candramukhi and gauri. :
At madanatapatra (clitoris) is mainly samirand, Sukra (semen) falling over it becomes
futile. :
The woman having mainly candramasi in kandarpageha (mid vaginal canal) is easily
satisfied with coitus and delivers female children.

Sexual satisfaction to the woman possessing gauri nadt in upasthagarbha (depth of
vaginal canal) is attained with difficulty and she delivers usually male children.

## Scanned page 031

Ro आयुर्वेदीय प्रसूतितन्त्र एवं स्त्रीरोग

The word yoni in 4yurvedika classics refers to entire reproductive system and also to
individual organs separately. Its shape resembles the mid part of conchshell as it is narrow
at the introitus and very wide at fornices. Its three dvartas are explained as vagina with its
adnexal structures, cervix with adnexa and uterus with adnexa by Dr. Joshi, Dr. Ghanekara
takes these to be mucous membranous folds. Other few explanations can also be given for
these three Gvartas as (A) (i) introitus, (ii) mid canal and (iii) fornices; (B) (i) thick connec-
tive and fibrous layers separating vaginal canal from urinary bladder and urethra anteriorly
and rectum and anus posteriorly, (ii) muscular layer and (iii) mucous membrane (fig.1). (C)
(i) external genitalia, (ii) vagina and (iii) uterus with adnexa. (D) (i) submeatal sulcus, (ii)
transeverse vaginal sulcus (iii) and bladder sulcus. Out of all these four explanations, num-
ber '8' seems to be more logical because Dalhana and Indu have accepted garbhaSaya as
separate from three Gvartas and these dvartas are said to be situated in garbhamarga
(vaginal canal).

Women possess one extra eighth aSaya as garbhaSaya, which is situated in third
avarta of yoni, behind the urinary bladder, in between pittafaya and pakwaSaya; or in
between ‘uipula kundala of srotas’ (multiple coils of intestine), covered with jarayu (perito-
neum). It resembles mouth of rohita fish (fig.2). Dalhana says that it is hollow inside just
‘like mouth of rohita fish; the vasei (urinary bladder) is behind the bhaga (vulva) and uterus
is above this. Vagbhata II has enumerated dimbha amongst the structures of kostha,
Arunadatta says that it is made from essence of rakta and mamsa and is derived from
intestines.

The simile of uterus with mouth of rohita fish might have been given probably due to
two reasons i.e. (1) similarity in shape, as both are triangular and hollow inside; the mouth
of fish is flat below and slightly convex above, similarly anterior wall of uterus is slightly
flat, while posterior wall is slightly convex. (2) the lips of fish are fleshy and hanging, teeth
are not just behind the lips, rather situated slightly behind these giving appearance of a
rounded soft structure, which resembles cervix of uterus.

In the context of situation of uterus the word pittasaya should not be considered as
gallbladder, rather it should be taker: as small intestine, the seat of pittadhara kala,
pakwasaya refers to the place of digested food i.e. large bowel. The uterus is above sigmoid
colon, behind the urinary bladder and multiple coils of small bowel rest upon uterus, it is
covered with peritoneum and is an intratbdominal structure, which has been mentioned by
Kaéyapa and Dalhana.

The word dimbha in not clear, presently it is used to donote ovum. Due to absence of
specific structural description and its presence in male and female both, it is difficult to
equate it with any structure. In Amarakosa it is translated as child, while Vaidyaka
Sabdasindhu book explains it as urinany bladder or uterus, thus, in context of females this
can be considerd as uterus as it is made up of flesh, is good vascular and is situated amongst
the intestines.

In breasts four marmas, two called stanarohita, the mémsa marma of 1 ahgula size
situated above the nipples on both the sides, and two termed stanamiila, the sira marmas of
2 angula size situated below both the breasts are present. All these cause death after some-
times, thus are called 4alantaraprénahara. Death occures by cough and dyspnoea due to
filling of kostha (chest cage) by kapha or rakta as a result of injury to stanamila or
stanarohita marma respectively.

In the chapter of treatment of urinary bladder-stone, Sugruta and Vagbhata I have
cautioned to avoid injury to eight vital parts i.e. mitravaha, Sukravaha, muskasrotas or
phalasrotas, mutrapraseka, sevant, yoni, guda and basti

Amongst these sevani, yoni, phalasrotas, mutrapraseka, guda, basti and miitravaha
etc. seven are important for females. Out of these only guda and vasti have been included in
the enumeration of marmas, it is possible that others are important only during extraction of
stone.

Sevani and yoni

Sevani refers to perineal raphe, while yoni to entire reproductive system also besides
vaginal canal; injury to these causes pain.
Phalasrotas

Phalasrotas refer to ovaries of females, which are counterpart of testicles of males.
Though specific symptoms of injury to these are not described in classics, however, injury
to both these may cause arnenorrhoea, infertility etc.

Mitrapraseka

This refers to urethra. Injury to this causes flow (continuous) of urine.

## Scanned page 036

20 आयुर्वेदीय प्रसूतितन्र एवं स्त्रीरोग

Guda and basti

Guda refers to rectum and basti to urinary bladder. These both are mdamsa marmas of
the size equal to palm, and cause immediate death, if injured.

Mitravaha

Injury to this produces fullness of urinary bladder followed by death.

Generally with mittravaha ureters should be considered, because these fill the bladder
with urine, however, these are two in number, while word miitravaha is a word of singular
number and injury to these can never cause fullness (retention of urine) of bladder, rather
the bladder mill remain empty, if it is taken as internal urethral meatus, it can explain the
fullness of bladder, as its injury may prevent excretion of urine, thus bladder may become
full.

In classics after describing the location of uterus behind the basti, it is advised that for
extracting the urinary bladder-stone in the females, the instrument should be passed direct-
ing it upwards, or else an ulcer discharging urine may be formed. Dalhana says that if the
instrument is insterted forcefully, deeper and directing it downwards instead of upwards,
then, after puncturing the external skin and flesh, it will puncture the bladder, bhaga (va-
gina) and the uterus, situated behind the bladder, thus produce a wound discharging urine
inside the bhaga (vagina). Besides injury to the orifice of uterus, the vagina is also injured.
Though initially continuous discharge of urine due to injury to miitrapraseka of only males
is described, however lateron in this very context the sex differentiation has disappeared.
Mitrapraseka marma refers to urethra which is present in male and females both. Injury to
the bladder with uterus or vagina results in development of utero-vesical or vesicc-vaginal
fistula respectively and injury to the urethra with vagina to urethro-vaginal fistula.

Besides, above structures others i. e. ureters, urinary bladder, urethra, rectum and anus
have to be taken special care during any gynecological surgery, as injury to these may
produce fistula.

Word pesi in ayurveda has been used to denote facia, muscle, tendon and ligaments
etc. in different contexts.

Breasts or even chest of female do not contain any extra muscle than male, thus, it is

The muscles of female reproductive system have been classified under four sub-
groups. These muscles have been explained in following way by previous writers-

स्त्री शरीर-रचना २७

The above explanation of either of the authors can not be accepted in toto due to
following reasons-

(a) The fibres of muscle-coat of vaginal canal are nearly all arranged in criss-cross
fashion, rather than in the outer longitudinal and inner circular pattern; (b) uterine muscle
fibres in most part run obliquely in criss-cross fashion, though most superficial and deepost
fibres are, however, arranged longitudinally, thus layers become three, but it is not easy to
separate these layers; (c) fallopian tubes contain only two muscular layers, not three; (d) if
broad ligaments are to be considered as two separate pesis then uterosacral and cardinal
ligaments being twin ligaments should also be considered as four, which will increase the
number to five of this sub-group; (e) though endometrium can be seen with naked eye yet
mucous membrane of fallopian tubes is not easily discernible, as it is microscopic structure,
thus, to consider this as a separate pest is also not proper.

Considering these facts, other explanations may be given in following way-
i) Outer circular (in orifice of vagina)

Muscle fibres of bulbocavernosus muscles encircling introitus or. sphincter vaginae
may be considered under this heading. Though this muscle is present in both sexes, yet,
these particular groups of fibres are absent in male (page 23; fig 4/1). '

ti) Two spreaded inside (the vaginal canal)

Either anterior and posterior vaginal wall or muscular layer of vagina and connective
tissue layer making pubocervical and rectovaginal facia can be taken ( page 9; fig. 1).
1

iii) Three situated in garbhachidra

Considering twin ligaments as one structure and with ' garbhachidra the cervix uteri,
the pubocervical, cardinal and uterosacral ligaments may be kept in this group. If this is to
be taken as uterus, then fundus, corpus and isthmus may be considered as three pesis ( page
24, 25; fig. 4/2 & 3.) due to following points-- हु

In transeverse section the portion of uterus above the insertion of fallopian tubes i.e.
fundus looks separate from remaining body. Fundus and isthmus are anatomically and
physiologically distinct as fundus has thickest muscular layer, uterus arcuatus etc. congeni-
tal abnormalities involve only fundus, it plays dominant role in expulsion of fetus. Isthmus,
the lowest part of uterus, joins it with cervix, has relatively lowest amount of muscle fibres
specially longitudinal, mucous lining is inbetween endometrium of uterus and endocervix, it
gets softend in early months of pregnancy giving rise to Hegar's sign, it forms lower uterine
segment and does not take active part in expulsion of fetus. Once fundus and isthmus are
isolated remaining portion i. e. corpus automatically becomes third one.

tv) Three responsible for entry of sperms and ovum

Cervix uteri may be taken as responsible for entry of sperms, as it is accepted that
certain conditions of cervix or its mucus can hinder entry of sperms in uterus. Ovum enters

Again ‘phala’ in dual number has appeared in the list of vital parts. Uterus can not be
considered a vital part because injury to this does not produce immediate death ( sadyah
pranahara marma), delayed death (kdlantara pranahara marma), death after removal of
foreign body from this (visalyaghna marma), severe pain (rujakara marma; endometrial
biopsy is performed without much pain to woman) or permanent disability ( vaikalyakara
marma), while injury to ovaries can produce at least permanent disability. With this descrip-
ton it may be concluded that word ‘phala’ in dual number indicates ovaries and in singular
number the uterus.

There is no clear description of various epochs of woman’s life, however, scattered
references present a general picture. Before discussing specific epochs of woman, revision
of general classification of age is essential. ue

The life span is divided into there stages--balawasthd (childhood), madhyamawastha
(adult age) and vrddhawastha (old age). Kasyapa has classified age into three groups,
garbha, bala and kuméra and again into three groups i. 8. yauwana, madhyama and vrddka,
In other words after classifying the age of childhood separately into three, the remaining
span of life is divided into }auwana etc. three stages. Harita has classified age into four
subdividing middle age into two i. e. yauwana and middle.

During this stage energy, potence, strength, working capacity, understanding, retention
power, memory, vocabulary, analysing capacities and all the dhazus are fully developed and
mature, psychology is stable. There is no decline in the qualities of dhadtus. This span is
dominated by pitta.

Caraka and Vagbhata keep the age limit of this span upto sixty years, while Suéruta,
Kasgyapa and Harita to seventy years

Various authors have subdivided this span in following way

(a) Susruta--Vrddhi (developmental stage) upto twenty years; yauwana (adult age)
upto 30 years, sampurrata (full maturity) upto forty years and slight A@ni (decline) upto
seventy years.

(b) Vagbhata- Yawana upto 30 years, sampiirnatd upto forty years. and aparihdni (no
decline) upto sixty years.

(c) KaSyapa-Yuvawastha upto forty years then madkyamawasthd (middle age) upto
seventy years. पे

further classified it on the basis of health and working capacity, as uttama (excellent),
madhyama (average) and adhama (low). Children, young or middle aged and soft persons

Preceding description relates to both sexes, but in females the reproductive capacity
does not last even for the whole middle age, rather menopause ensues. In the last few years
of childhood itself woman is fully mature to achieve conception, this maturity can come
even earlier if she is free from diseases and has good dict. Bhavamisra has mentioned the
woman as faruni (ever young) upto thirtytwo years and adhiriidha (middle aged) upto fifty
years, after which she is vrddha (old lady).

“ Harita has classified the age of female as bala upto five years followed by mugdha for
another six years (upto 11 years) or ba/4 up to twelve years followed by mugdhd for another
seven years (upto 19 years; this difference might be due to individual variation), praudha upto
28 years and pragaibhd upto 41 years. In between twentyfour to thirtyseven she is in best age. .

Paragara smrti has mentioned a girl upto 8 years as gaur7, upto nine as rohint, upto ten
as kanya followed by rajaswala. It seems that this classification is based on the prevalent
socio-religious conditions thus, is not suited to our purpose.

1 As butter melts in contact with fire, similarly woman secrets drtava during coitus with
male. Dalhana has explained that puranartava is excreted during three days of menstrual
blood loss. Navinartava being less and solid can not come out, but due to heat generated
during coitus it is melted, excreted and gets mixed with Sukra, thus, initiates conception.
Further he quotes Vagbhata and says that woman secretes §vkra during coitus which is
useless for conception. Probably Dalhana refers to this Grtava as ovum, which is accepted
by Ghanekara ji.

In human being coitus does not initiate ovulation, thus, it is not advisable to accept
Grtava or gukra excreted during coitus as ovum, this may be.considered only as local
discharges of female reproductive system coming out during coitus.

Explicit description of hormones is not available in ayurvedika classics, however,
indirect inference can be drawn from scattered references such as:-

(i) Vagbhata, Kasyapa and Dalhana accept presence of raja or Sonita from the very
childhood just like fukra, which is not visible due to very minute quantity. Menstrual blood
is not accumulated anywhere in the body, rather it is formed every month in the uterus. If
with this description ovum is accepted due to its presence from embryonic life, then its
explicitness at twelve years of age would be difficult to explain, because it is microscopic
structure. Cakrapani has written that drtava which is explicit at twelve years is formed in
embryonic life. This reference probably indicates description of hormones specially ovarian.

हि (ii) Susruta while describing the formation of dhatus accepts formation of Grtava also
alongwith Sukra in females. Bhavamisra elaborating this, writes that women possess one
extra dhatu just as presence of one extra Saya (garbhasaya), thus, have Grtava as seventh
and Sukra as eighth dhatu. All the functions relating to conception are performed by Grtava,
while energy and complexion etc. are promoted by Sukra. It is also very essential for life.
Here also artava refers to hormones.

(iii) SuSruta accepts the development of breasts, uterus, vagina and vulva etc. during
adolescence due to gradual accumulation of raja, here raja refers to hormones specially
estrogen.

(iv) Sugrota has enumerated amenorrhoea, oligomenorrhoea and pain in vagina etc.
symptoms due to decrease of artava. Cakrapini has explained that these symptoms are
caused by vdyu aggravated due to decrease of drtava responsible for proper nourishment of
reproductive system. This reference also indicates that probably drtava refers to estrogen.

(v) Sugruta and Vagbhata, while describing the formation of placenta write that due to
obstruction to orifices of Grtavavaha srotas by fetus the Grtava goes upwards, gets accumu-
lated and forms placenta, left over Grtava moves further upwards and helps in the develop-
ment of breast and increases black pigmentation of areola and lips etc. After conception the
hormones formed from corpusluteum help in placentation and placental hormones along-
with ovarian and pituitary hormones help in development of breasts and formation of breast
milk. Though excess pigmentation over face or areola is caused by melanin, yet estrogen
plays important role in this process. Since the sex hormones are responsible for all these
changes i.e. amenorrhoea, placenta formation, breast changes and pigmentation, thus this
description can also be taken for hormones.

(vi) For gynecological disorders Grtava and bija are also causative factors, since bija
or ovum is already included, hence, Griava probably refers to hormones.

(vii) While giving indications for basti, Vagbhata has included artavana§a and rajah-
ksaya both. Use of both the words i. e. artava and raja indicates that probably one word
refers to hormones; as ovum is invisible, thus, can not be considered here.

(viii) Harita says that infertile women have more amount of Grtava, because they can
not secrete milk. The hypothalamus has inhibiting factor for prolactine responsible for milk
secretion and releasing factors to all other anterior pituitary hormones. If hypothalamus
becomes hyperactive, then prolactine will not be sccreted, while secretion of more amount
of other pituitary hormones may cause menorrhagia, or in other words this also refers to
hormones.

(ix) Cakrapani says that ailments develop due to disequilibrium of dhatus i.e. vata etc.,
rasa etc. and ‘raja’ etc., this reference may be considered for ovarian hormones responsible
for certain gynecological disorders.

Body is composed of seven dhdtus, Sukra is seventh and is situated in whole body; _

though explicit only after sixteen years of age, it is present from childhood.

Functions of sukra are the following ones:--

(1) Nourishment of subsequent dhdtu or ojas.

(2) Formation of garbha and its scx, capable of producing teratologic abnormalities.

(3) Betterment of complexion and strength alongwith affection and penile erection,

(4) When vitiated by dosas it can not be effective for fertilization.

Sukra though is situated in whole body within sukradharakala, yet its specific location
is bonemarrow and scrotum. Roots of Sukravaha srotas are testes, penis, breasts and
bonemarrow. Though Sukradhara kald is spread over entire body, yet it is specifically
situated laterally to urinary bladder and urethra. During coitus, it is excreted by male, enters
female reproductive system and forms fetus.

With the above description sukra may be correlated with sperms including spermatic
fluid or even testosterone etc. sex hormones and same has been explained by Ganandtha
Sena Ji as antah-Sukra and bahi-Sukra.

ue आयुर्वेदीय प्रसूतितन्त्र एवं स्त्रीरोग

Alike gukra in males, stanya (milk) is said to be present in whole female’s body, but
this milk is a by-product or upadhatu of rasadhatu, while sukra is dhdtu and formed after
majja. Stri-fukra excreted during coitus as per Vagbhata I can also not be considered
parallel to sukra-dhatu as former is useless for conception, while main function of latter
is conception. This very coital discharge has been termed as drtava by Sugruta and retas
by Vagbhata IL. Cakrapani accepting presence of Sukra in women, has clarified that the
garbha is formed from essence part of pure Sukra, not from its by-product; quoting openion
of others, writes that few erudites accept development of mousatche from by-product
(waste) of Sukra which is not accepted by Caraka, had this been the process, even women
would have had thé moustache due to presence of Sukra, moreover, the sukra of female-
body does not take part in fertilization. Achievement of boneless fetus with sexual pleasure
in-between two women is also a pure hypothetical possibility never a reality; probably
considering these points, Bhavamisra advanced the idea of eight dhatus in females i. 6.
Grtava as seventh and §ukra the eighth one, but exact description regarding location,
characteristiscs etc. is lacking there too. Harita has accepted presence of retas in both male
and female in addition to sukra or rajas, predominance of this retas of both partners
alongwith Sukra or rajas and (power of) male and female respectively is said to form sex
of embryo. Commentator Cakrapani has also included rajas in the list of dhatus because
of its capability of getting vitiated.

Even in males to limit the sukra in reproductive system only is not justified; because
Sukra is a dhdtu, essential for sustenance of body and nourishment of subsequent dhdatu.
Complete absence of any specific dhatu will make the life impossible, moreover it is also
included amongst ten prandyatanas i.e. seats of life of the body. Individuals with complete
absence of reproductive system either congenitally or due to surgical excision have a fairly
normal life-span, which should not have been possible because of absence of Sukra
alongwith ojas which is formed or is nourished from Sukra and is said to be its essence,
byproduct or upadhatu,

Considering the importance of sukra for sustenance of life alongwith its, earlier enu-
merated functions and presence in both sexes, it seems to be description of entire endocrine
orchestra specially hypothalamic-pituitary axis. It can also be equated with prostaglandins,
since these are also present in every cell and play important role in reproduction. Human
body possesses seven dhatus and is composed of microscopic cells. Though all these dhatus
have their specific locations in the body, however, in subtle form these are present in each
and every cell. Every cell divides or reproduces itself; reproduction is function of Sukra
dhdatu. It is just possible that with the advancement in the knowledge, we may come across
some such substance within the cell which has specfic function of cell division, then this
substance would be equated with sukradhatu. Sperms alongwith spermatic fluid and male
sex hormones are also one part of sukra, parallel to which females possess Grtava which
has been clearly indicated by Dalhana (fig.5). Stri-sukra excreted during coitus is just
secretion of bartholin’s, cervical and endometrial glands coming out at the end of orgasm.

कार चक्रपाणि ने रज का वैषम्य हो व्याधि उत्पादन की क्षमता के आधार पर इसे धातु-रूप भी माना है!

From rasa (dhatu), the rakta named raja is formed. Rakta reaching uterus and coming
out for three days in every month is called @rtava. The raja is formed from essence patt of
rasa.

There appears some difference of opinion regarding formation of raja (menstrual
blood). Caraka, Suégruta, Vagbhata H, Dalhana and Cakrapini opine that it is formed from
rasa, while Vagbhata I says that blocd accumulated in uterus, then discharged is Grtava, the
raja is derived from essence portion of rasa; actually both these descriptions are indentical,
because rakta either dh@tu-riipa or menstrual blood is always derived from rasa, thus it
appears that Susruta etc. have mentioned the earlier stage of raja formation while
Vagbhata I the later stage. The point has been clarified by Cakrapani that during the process
of formation, the Griava is saumya due to influence of rasa, while at the time of its
excretion due to specific changes it assumes Ggueya character. This alteration is brought due
to change in character caused by dosas in the same way as solid substances are changed into
fume due to action of fire, cane-juice a vitiating factor of kapha is changed after fermenta-
tion into wine which vitiates all the three dosas. Arunadatta opines that this raja is formed
from @hdrarasa and not from rasadhdtu. Sarigadhara and Bhawamisra mention raja as by-
product (upadhatu) of rakta. ‘

Intermenstrual period has been given as of one month by all the writers, however, there
is difference of opinion regarding duration of menstruation as three days (Vagbhata and
Bhawamisra), five days (Caraka) and seven days (Harita and Bhela). Bhawamiéra has fur-
ther said that if flow is exessive it lasts for three days; if average then for five days;
however, if slight flow without any other symptom of abnormality persists even for sixteen
days, it may be considered as normal.

ay आयुर्वेदीय प्रसूतितन्र एवं स्त्रीरोग

The blood collected for whole month by both the dhamanis (uterine vessels and their
endometrial capillaries) assuming slight black colour and specific odour is brought down-
wards to vaginal orifice by vdyu for excretion. Viswamitra has clarified that hair thin vessels
fill the uterus for whole month to receive bija (both set and pumbija or zygote).

परिवर्तनों का परिणाम होता है, जो आधुनिक ग्रम्थों में वर्णित गर्भाशय की श्लेष्मलकला में होने वाले चक्रिक परिवर्तनों
की ओर इंगित करता है। है

Above description clearly indicates that menstruation is a result of changes going on
in vascular apparatus of uterus for whole month, or in other words this refers to cyclic
changes of endometrium.

The normal menstruation is that which has intermenstrual period of one month; dura-
tion of blood loss as five days (this may differ according to opinions of different authors);
is not associated with pain or burning sensation. excreted blood is not unctuous, not very
scanty or excessive in amount; the colour resembles the red juice of lac, red lotus flower,
fruit of jequirity or rabbit’s blood.

Menstrual blood is not bright red in colour as mentioned above, but is of slight
blackish nature, which has been accepted by some authors at different places (page 64).
Bhawatnigra has explained that this difference in colour is due to prakrti (vataja etc.) of
individuals, and vitiated dosas are responsible for symptoms like pain anc burning sensation
etc.

विमर्श (Comments)

आधुनिक काल में किसी भी विशिष्ट रजःस्वलाचर्या का निर्देश नहीं मिलता । संहिताओं में बर्णित निर्देशों की उपादेयता
संदेहास्पद है, फिर भी उस काल को सामाजिक स्थिति को (व्यक्ति को जीविकोपार्जन के लिए कठित परिश्रम करना पड़ता
था) दृष्टिगोचर रखते हुए सम्भवत: इन निर्देशों कौ उपयोगिता को सिद्ध किया जा सकता है।

The utility of all these restrictions is doubtful, however, this reflects the social customs
of that period, in which for earning livelihood hard work was needed, these restrictions
might help in avoiding this hard labour at least for those three days when the lady is
definitely physically and psychologically in some changed status. However, in to-day's
changed social structure, it is not possible to observe these strictly. Consequences due to
non-observance described Jater do not seem to be correct one.

If copulation occurs on first day of menstruation, the life span of husband shortens,
however. if coitus takes place with menstruating woman (on any day) then also the life of
husband shortens, his eye-sight and glory (¢eja) declines, as well as this becomes the act of
uarighteousness. The penetration of bija (sperms) ducing menstrual flow is not good; as a
light article thrown in the flowing river against the current never reaches upwards, similarly
sperms deposited during menstruation do not reach uterus, hence, for three days the lady
should avoid coitus. Effects on the child impregnated during these four days of menstruation
are given here under:

स्वास्थ्य-दृष्ट्या संभोग न करना ही श्रेयस्कर होता है, क्योंकि यह एक सम्भावना हो सकती है कि इस काल में चूँकि

प्रतिक्रिया का अभाव होगा एवं संभोग से प्रविष्ट जीवाणु सीधे गर्भाशयादि अंगों में प्रविष्ट हो ब्याधि उत्पन्न करने में समर्थ

in a month. This raja or Grtava formed in a month may. be considered as ovulation.

Rajahkala—Excretion or movement of any substance from one place to other is the

function of vayu, hence this is dominated by vayu.

Rtukala—The phase is characterized with proliferation of endometrium followed by
ovulation. The reconstruction of tissue or proliferation or regeneration is done by priint
(solid substance) and jala (water or liquid substances), which are the bhautika components
of kapha. Vagbhatal has clarified that in woman having domination of kapha and using
ghrta and milk etc. daily the artava stays for longer period. It is already mentioned earlier
that Grtaya in its stage of formation is sawnya or has characteristics like kapha, thus this

stage is dominated by kapha

the basal body temperature by 0.00 to {.0° F. (thermogenic effect of progesterone hormone
of secretory phase) or this stage is governed by pitta.

यदि १२ वर्ष को GI से Tain वर्ष का पुरुष विवाह करेगा एवं १६ वर्ष की स्त्री में गर्भाधान करायेगा तो उस समय
युरुष की आयु उन्तीस वर्ष की हो जायेगी, परन्तु दोनों ही स्थितियों में पुरुष की पच्चीस वर्ष की ही आयु का वर्णन मिलता
है, अत: यह मान सकते हैं कि सम्भवतः विवाह-योग्य बारह वर्ष की आयु का वर्णन मुद्रण-ब्रुटि हो अर्थात्‌ महर्षि सुश्रुत
के मतानुसार विवाह एवं गर्भाधारण-योग्यता की एक ही आयु है।

Male at the age of twentyfive and female at the age sixteen are fully mature, hence,
they should attempt for achievement of conception.

Since both the pariners are full of valour and vigour at this age, the born child also
possesses these qualities. In one edition of Susruta Samhita twelve and sixteen years-age of
woman for marriage and full maturity respectively is given; while age of the male at both
these places is mentioned as twentyfive, hence, it apperars that reference of twelve years
of age for marriage could be a printing mistake. In Astanga Hrdaya, the age of man is
prescribed as twenty years, Arunadatta explains that this is usual age of man and woman.
Caraka and Kasyapa opine that the man is not fit for coitus before age of sixteen, after this
he is capable of ejaculating semen, however, these authors have not mentioned appropriate
age for impregnation.

विमर्श (Comments)

अष्टागसंग्रह में विवाह तथा गर्भधारण-क्षमता की पृथक्‌-पृथक्‌ आयु-वर्णन का कारण सामाजिक व्यवस्था हो सकता
है | इस पुस्तक के रचनाकाल तक चूँकि देश में विदेशियों का आगमन हो चुका था, अतः परिवार की मर्यादा-रक्षण के
विचार से बाल-विवाह प्रथा का प्रारम्भ हुआ, एवं विवाहोपरांत बालिका मातृ-गृह में ही रहकर ट्विएगमन के समय से सामान्य
दाम्पत्य जीवन व्यतीत करती थी, जो व्यवस्था आज भी देश के अधिकांश प्रदेशों में प्रचलित है । सभी आचार्यो ने गर्भाधारण
के लिए ot की १६ वर्ष की आयु को ही सर्वोत्तम माना है । आधुनिक विज्ञान में भी प्रासविक दृष्टि से १६ वर्ष की आयु
को ही सर्वोत्तम माना गया है।'

The mention of marriageable age and age for conception separately by Vagbhata
indicates the social pattern of that time. By the period of this book the foreign culture has
established its foot firmly, the marriage of girls was ceremonized at a very early age, lest
the girls were forcibly married by the authorities. The girl was sent to her inlaws only after
gaunda (second marriage). The system is prevalent in some parts of the country even to-day.

In all the dyurvedika classics best age for conception is said to be sixteen. This
observation is confirmed by Harris, who after analysing the statistics found that from a
purely obsterical point of view, sixteen was the most favourable age to have a baby.

Coitus should not be done with a woman in her flexed (hump-back) or lateral position.

kapha getting displaced obstructs the garbhdsaya, similarly in left lateral position displaced
pitta burns (vidaha) the rakta (ovum) and Sukra (sperms), hence for reception of dija the
woman should lie in supine position, so that all the dosas remain in their normal locations.
The man should not lie below the woman, because after this postural copulation if woman
delivers a male child, he will have feminine characters and if female child then she will
have masculine habits.

On even days Grtava is less which increases on odd days, thus there is birth of male
and female respectively. A man desirous of having a son should not have sexual relation
even during day time on odd days. If on odd days Sukre is more and on even days it is less,
then the born male child -will have feminine features and would be weak, with less body
parts: and if it is a female, she will be of masculine features, weak and with less body parts.

Only two authors i.e. Caraka and Kagyapa have described the detailed methods of
putresti yajfia which is actually a subject of sociology or religion. The methods of both
these authors differ considerably.

Now the priest should search a space in the north or east direction of the house (court-
yard) which is slopy towards north or east, besmear it with cow-dung and water, rewipe the
same with water and establish an altar. Now the priest should sit on the west side of that
altar over a cushion made with new cloths or over the skin of white ox if the client is
brahmana, lion ot ox if the client is Agatriya, and deer or goat if the client is vaisya. Sitting
over there he should lit the pious fire (in the altar) with the woods of palasa, :irgudi,
udumbara or madhiika, spread all around kuSa, decorate it, and strew laja (parched paddy)
and fragrant white flowers. Now he should place near the altar the sacred water, treated with
mantras (sacred words) and ghrta for oblation and also the horse and other articles of
decoration of the colour desired for the child.

Now the lady anxious to have the desired child, placing the brahmana on the south .
direction of fire should sit alongwith her husband on the west’ side of fire and follow the
instructions of the priest. The priest should start the putresti yajfia for fulfilment of the
desires of the lady by indicating or characterizing prajgpati to the yoni (vagina) of the
woman and reciting “visnuryoni” etc. hymn. Now he should place the caru (oblation pre-
pared with rice, barley etc. mixed with milk and ghrta etc.) in saucepan, mix it with ghrta

There is some difference in the events described by various authors. Caraka says that
when a man copulates with a rtumarT woman (described earlier), then due to excitement and
pleasure the dhaturiipa Sukra situated in various body parts is excreted. This excreted sukra-
dhatu coming out of male’s body, in the form of bija (seed or sperms) enters the uterus
through proper passage (vagina) and gets mixed with drtava or Sonita (ovum). At this very
time, due to association of satwa or mana, the jivavnd comes there in the garbha (zygote).
Due to constant use of congenial diet by the pregnant woman, this. garbha (fetus) grows
normally and gets delivered at appropriate time with all indriyas (sensory and motor or-
gans), complete body parts, bala (energy), varna (complexion), satwa (endurance) and
samhanana (compactness) alongwith mderja (maternal), pitrja (paternal), Gtmaja, satmyaja
and rasaja bhawas (physical and psychological components) having constant association of
mana,

SuSruta opines that teja or heat generated at the time of coitus activates vayu. then the
Sukra excreted due to the action of both vayu and teja reaches uterus, gets mixed with
Grtava, thus formed zygote with the union of agni (artava) and soma (Sukra) stays in uterus.
Then the dima or jiva, known by synonyms of ksetrajfia, vedayita, sprasta, ghrata, drasta,
Srota, rasayitd, purusa, srastda, ganta, sGksi, dhata and vakra etc., inspite of being aksava
(imperishable), avyaya (eternal), acintya (inconceivable) but due to effect of daiva (des-
tiny), associated with bhitta (paitcamahabhiitas), satwa, raja, tama, daiva and asura etc.
bhavas and impelled by vayu reaches the uterus and stays there.

Vagbhata I corroborating the views of Caraka explains that due to effect of raga fiove
or passion) etc. and impelled by deeds of previous life the mana propells jiva to come to
the uterus.

Vagbhata II explaining this very point says further that as fire is generated from the
wood by contrivance, similarly sa¢wa with the association of Sukra and drtava forms zygote.
As the rays emanating from sun or fire being emitted from quartz (sphatikamani} and
reaching wood are not actually seen, but are accepted because of their results i. e. heat of
the sun and fire in the wood, similarly entry of safwa in the uterus is not seen (but is
accepted due to its effect).

११२ आयुर्वेदीय प्रसूतितन्त्र एवं स्त्रीरोग

With the help or companionship of mana, the cetand dhatu 91072ए१५ for taking hold
of guna (sarwa, raja and tama). This very cetand is called as hetu, karanc. aimitta, aksara,
karta, mand, vedita, boddha, drasta, dhata, brahmda, viswakarma. viswariipa, purusa,
prabhava, avyaya, nitya, guni, grahana, pradhana, avyakta, jiva, jiia, pudgala, cetanavana,
vibhu, bhiutdtmd, indriyaétma and antaratma. This atmd at the time of beholding of gunas
first of all creates Gkaéa, in the same way as after complete annihilation of entire universe
the god of creation brakma first of all created akaSa with the assistance of satwa, followed
by gradual creation of more perceptible bhitas as v@yu etc. Similarly in the formation of
embryo also first acquisition of akaga followed by more perceptible other four bhiitas as
vayu etc. occures, In acquiring all the mah&bhitas time taken is very negligible.

Describing transmigration of self, Caraka writes that the self alongwith four subtle
bhittas and with the speed of mind transmigrates from one body to the other on the basis
of past deeds. it can not be seen without divine visual sense. The self is all pervasive,
sustains all bodies, performs all actions, takes all forms; is the source of consciousness,
transcends all senses, is ever united and closely attached.

Harita opines that from akaSa comes vayu, from vaya is prana which is satwaguna
of all the living beings. From akasa comes jala, from jala the prthvi, from prthyi is teja and
from teja is tama.

आदि ) देहान्तर में गमन करती है।

के मन की उत्पत्ति होती है। इस प्रकार जो आकृति एवं बुद्धि में अन्तर होता है उसके कारण रज, तम एवं

के आहार-रसज महाभूत सभी मिलकर क्रम से कुक्षि में गर्भ को वृद्धि करते हैं |

Four mahabhiitas (vayu, teja, jala and prthvt) comming from four sources i. 8. mother
(through Sonita or ovum), father (through Sukra or sperms), Ghdra-rasa (through the rasa
derived from maternal diet for supplying nourishment to the embryo) and atma (encircling
Gtma due to effect of the deeds of previous life) participate in the formation of embryo. The
bom child reflects the bhautika (physical) characteristics of maternal, paternal or dtmaja
etc. factors depending upon their relative predominance; and others (psychological) depend-
ing upon the preponderance of satwa etc. (satwa, raja and tama) in mana; besides, the mana
is also influenced by its left over previous abode, such as comming after leaving the body
of devas or animals etc. it will have some of their characters (daiva or paSu satwa etc.). The
deeds and species are also related, or in other words due to influence of deeds it will be
satwika, rajas and tamas etc. and it is also due to deeds that it comes to human or other
species and acquires similar characters.

In cetana (alive) garbha (embryo) vibhajana (division), pacana (metabolism), kledana
(moistening), samhanana (solidification) and vivardhana (increase in size) are done by
vayu, teja, jala, prthvi and Gkasa respectively. Dalhana clarifying the above verse says that
only because of cetand the garbha remains alive upto the time of delivery, in absence of
this it gets putrified or degenerated. The division of dosa, dhatu, mata (excretas), aga and
pratyanga (major and minor body pasts) is done by vayu. The teja by its function of
metabolism changes the shape, provides general appearance like human structure etc. along
with specific features and complexion. Moistening is done by jala or in other words the
dryness or absorption caused by division and metabolism being done by vayw and teja
respectively is normalized by moistening action of jala. The prthvi solidifies or gives shape
to the embryo already moistened by jala. The increase in size is done by akasa by providing
vacuum with adhmapana (inflating or blowing upon) to the srofasas (channels) running all-
around the body 1.6. in up, down and oblique directions, which are created by vidarana
(splitting or divison) done by vayu and agni.

Bhavamiéra corroborating the earlier views regarding prthvi, vayu and Gkasa explains
that agni or teja stays in the body in the form of pacaka, Glocaka, raitjaka, bhrajaka and

मारुतावाविशत् इति (Ho सं० Mo ६/३)

गर्भ-विज्ञानीय अध्याय ११३

The development of the fetus mainly depends upon the inflation done by vayu and-

nourishment supplied by rasa is the opinion of SuSruta and Bhivamisra. Behind the
umbilicus there is definitely the location of jyotisthdza (the place of light or fire). The vayu
by its blowing action excites or stimulates this fire, which in turn performs development of
body. The vayw associated with this very fire splits the upward, downward and obliquely
running channels, resulting into development of fetus. It also gives specific shape or fea-
tures to the fetus is the opinion of Caraka.

KaSyapa says that finest particles of vayu responsible for union, division and activity
perform flexion and extension etc. actions as well as division of major and minor body
parts, dhatu, cetana (consciousness) and channels due to their specific nature. All this
splitting and dharana (retention) is done by vayu in association with dala (time factor).

Hacita opines that bija (sperms and ovum both together) attains the shape of kalala by
the action of agni situated in all the five 9145. Further this internally situated kalala gets
the shape of budbuda by the action of outside vayu. This budbuda again becoming kalala
gets solidified in the shape of pinda (solid) by the action of paficabhitdgnt; by further
metabolism this mass becomes a heap of solid substance, then vyana vayu, forms the
paficatatwas, arms, legs and head etc. body parts. The same internally situated one vayu
reaching different parts gives this solid mass a shape of body. Udana vayu situated in neck
and heart forms oral cavity and its aperture. Apana vayu situated downwards clarifies the
apaina dwara (anal orifice), similarly internally situated vayu comes out of the body making
different orifices. Thus with the influence of vayu, nine external meatuses i. e. oral, both
nasal, both eyes, both ears, anal and urinary are formed.

Bhela lays equal emphasis on the role of agni and vayu, both these entering the body

form differnt major and minor body parts, as well as initiate activity and growth. When
these come out of the body, the person (fetus) becomes dead due to absence of agni and

vayu. Bharadwaja contradicts this saying that it is not so, because dead body gets inflated _

and dried too. Atreya corroborates the views of Bhela explaining that internal agni and vayu
exist only during life, after death the inflation and desiccation is done by external vayu and
agni which enter the dead body.

of maternal ete. all the components) है

रहता है। माता एवं पिता का शोणित तथा शुक्र किसी सीमा तक उनके सात्म्य सेवन पर आधारित होता है, इसी विचारधारा

Ayurvedic philosophy believes that the human body is composed of five mahabhitas,
sources of these mahabhinas are said to be mother, father, rasa and atma. Auna is always
associated with satwo. The normalcy of fonita (ovum) and fukra (sperms) of mother and
father respectively greatly depend upon the use of satmya (wholesome, suitable or congenial
diet}. Considering this fact the formation of garbha (embryo) is said to be from sadbhaway
(six components i.e. mncitrja, pitrja, rasaja, dtmaja, satwaja and satmyaja bhawas). Caraka
has recapitulated the debate on this subject. He writes that neither mother, nor father. nor
Gtma (soul / self) nor wholesome suitable diet, nor use of eatable, lickable or drinkable
dietetics are capable of forming the fetus. Neither the satwa coming from other world enters
the fetus, or in other words none of these factors singularly are capable of forming the
embryo, it is formed only with combination of all these. Caraka has simulated the formation
of embryo with building of upper room (apartinent at the top the house) or a chariot. As
by combining and arranging different building materials the upper room is constructed or
with different parts « chariot is assembled, similarly with the combination of these six
components the fetus is formed. He has further advanced logic to support his view by desc-
ribing different body parts, arising [rom these specific components and thus has contradicted
the theory of formation of garbha by singular component. Bhela has also given almost
similar description albeit in summarized form.

ग्रति उसको कारणता we नहीं होती । क्योंकि आत्मा के जानने वाले व्यक्तियों ने यह देखा है कि अभीष्ट योनि, ऐश्वर्य

आत्मा के अतिरिक्त किसी अन्य कारण से उत्पन्न नहीं होता, क्योंकि बिना बीज के अंकुर की उत्पत्ति नहीं होती (अर्थात्‌
आत्मा ही गर्भ का मूल या बीज कारण है, इसके बिना गर्भ की उत्पत्ति नहीं होती) |

The mother, father and दकाद etc. factors are not totally independent for all their
functions. By these factors some of the functions are performed independently, some de-
pending upon the deeds (of previous life) and some upon the karana (means of actions or
instruments i.e. mana, buddhi and indriyas). At some places these instruments are much
potent and at others not so. When these sativa etc. instruments are normal, their functional
capacity wil] depend upon their relative strength, otherwise not (if these are abnormal, their
functional capacity will alter). However, in case of abnormality of these instruments the
atma does not become non-causative in the process of formation of garbha or in other
words its causativeness for formation of embryo does not break, because the persons know-
ing dtma have observed that birth in desired species, supremacy (aifwarya) and eternal
emancipation depend upon atmda. There is none other than dtma responsible for giving
feeling of pleasure and pain. As a sprout can not come up without seed, similarly birth can
not take place without Gtma or in other words root cause of garbha is Gtma without this the
formation of embryo is impossible.

काम-क्रोधादि के त्याग की क्षमता एवं तमोगुण विपरीतता हैं ।

अष्टाडरहदवकार के मत से पवित्रता, आस्तिकता, धर्म में रुचि एवं मति या बुद्धि सत्वज भाव हैं | टीकाकार अरुणदत्त
ने वाक्‌, काय एवं मन तीनों ही की पवित्रता के साथ उपर्युक्त गुणों को उपलक्षण मात्र मानकर कृतज्ञवा, दाक्षिण्य, व्यवसाय,
शौर्य, गांभीय, स्मृति, एवं Aer आदि को भी सत्वज माना है हि

Caraka has enumerated devotion, disposition or habit, piousness, hatred, memory,
infatuation, sacrifice or abnegation, jealousy, prowess, fear, anger, drowsiness, zeal, hot-
subtle or good temper and unsteadiness of mana (psyche). He, writes further that the
features described under psychic constitution are also features of satva.

Sugruta says that features described under psychic constitution should be taken here.

Vagbhata I has mentioned piousness, belief in existence of god, gratitude, dexterity,
quickness for work, prowess, sobriety, buddhi (knowledge), medha (brain or intelligence),
memory. cleanliness, interest in religion, devotion, capability of giving up sexuality and
anger and the qualities opposite to amas.

Vagbhata II has mentioned piousness, belief in existence of god, cleanliness, interest
in religion and buddhi, Arunadatta has added piotsness of words, deeds and thoughts,
gratitude, dexterity, business, sobriety, memory and intelligence to the list.

The mana of fetus attains the characters of satwa, raja and tama etc. depending upon

the psychological status of the mother and father, the topics being listened by the pregnant

woman, the influence of deeds of the previous life and specific practice of mana.

से ही आकृति भेद होता है। जिस प्रकार साँचे में ढला हुआ पुरुष पुरुष को, गौ गौ को, अश्व अश्व को उत्पन्न करता
है उसी प्रकार मनुष्यों में भी गर्भ की निर्वृत्ति होती है ।

Replying to the question that when all six basic factors responsible for conception are
similar in all the species, then why from human couple a human child is born ? Caraka says
that all the six factors of conception when enter in any species taking birth through placen-
tation or egg, attain characters of the same species in the same way as liquified gold, silver,
copper, zink or lead poured in a mould of bee wax acquire the shape of the same mould.
If these are poured in man shaped mould then these gold etc. will acquire the shape of a
man. Similarly when all these six factors collectively enter the human body, the birth of a
human child occurs. Being of the same species, it is said that from man a man is born.

Both the Vagbhatas have mentioned that action or result depends upon its means due
to its specific nature. Indu has explained that as from tila seeds only tila plant will grow
not the masa (a type of kidney been), similarly from collective efforts of mother, father,
bhittas, dwelling place, time, uterus and dietetics of the mother, the resultant conception
would be of similar shape. Vagbhata H and Kasyapa have also given similarity of mould
ete. as explained by Caraka.

After impregnation the openings of artavavulte srotasas are obstructed by conception,
due to this very reason the Grtaya (menstruation) is not seen after conception. Then this very
artava being repelled from downward passage gous upward and gets accumulated, which is
known as apara or jarayu, Dalhana quoting the pussage of Bhoja says that from rakta
(blood) placenta and from rasa the umbilical curd of fetus is formed. Indu opines that
besides the accumulation of G@rtava, the diet (used by mother) also plays a role in gradual

formation of placenta.

Suéruta explains that inspiration. expiration, activity and sleep of fetus are dependent
upon the mother i. e. inspiration of mother gives inspiration to the fetus etc. The fetal
umbilical cord is attached to the maternal rasavahanadi carrying the essence of mother’s
diet, and the fetus grows (by obtaining nourishment) through upasneha. From the lime of
conception upto the period untile the body parts of fetus are not fully conspicuous, it gets
its sustenance by upasneha through the vessels running obliquely into all body parts (fig.
6a). Dalhana has given the simile that as a tree situated on the bank of a full pond derives
its nourishment, similarly fetus also receives its nourishment. Further quoting Bhoja he says
that fetal nourishment takes place by kedarikulya@ nyaya.

Both the Vagbhatas have also expressed almost identical views, however, Vagbhata I
adds that from umbilical cord the rasa reaches pakwasaya (digestive system) of the fetus
(fig. 6 b,), there with its own kayagni (digestive fire) gets metabolised and provides nour-
ishment to it. Since rasa carries pure nutrients, hence, excretas are not formed. Indu has
explained that unctuousness is upasneha and moistening is upasweda.

## Scanned page 100

आयुर्वेदीय प्रसूतितन्द्र एवं स्त्रीरोग

१४ड८

It is evident from preceding description that entire fetal nourishment is divided into
two stages, before apparent evidence of organs or upto three months and after-wards. Before
implantation zygote gets its nourishment from exudates of uterine cavity and after implan-
tation but before complete placenta formation through chorionic villi present all over the
embryonic surface, which has very clearly been mentioned by Susruta that embryo gets
nourishment from the channels running all around it. After three months nourishment is
through umbilical vessels (fig. 6). It is difficult to explain the attachment of placenta with
mother’s heart, this might have been mentioned due to the fact that uterus in its full term
reaches upto xiphisternum and mostly placenta is attached to the fundus of uterus, thus
reaches to very close proximity of heart. However, probably with this very confusion
Sugruta has mentioned that umbilical cord is attached to rasavahé nadi of mother. If rasa
is accepted as plasma, the clarification can be given that the fine branches of umbilical
vessels running in placenta derive the nutrients suspended in plasma of mother’s blood.

If the relation of apara with heart is considered as relation to its function, then it can
be explained in the following way-(i) as in heart, the blood enters from veins, circulates
within its chambers and goes out through arteries, similarly in maternal side of apara
(placenta) the blood. reaches from maternal arteries, circulates within chorionic villies and
goes out from marginal sinuses or veins, in other words the circulation of blood in heart and
placenta is almost similar, (ii) to pump pure blood in the body and impure blood to the lungs
for purification is main function of heart, similarly palcenta receives the impute blood from
fetus, purifies it and sends it back to the fetus or due to similarity in function the apara is
said to be attached to the heart.

Two words upasneha and upasweda are given to define the process of fetal nourish-
ment. In explaining these words Indu’s version is more logical, because as fetus is domi-
nated by kapha, naturally it would need more unctuous substances to replenish this kapha,
or in other words simple osmosis can not serve the purpose, thus the word upasneha
probably refers to the selective osmosis, while upasweda to simple osmosis. Literally
upasneha refers to the absorption of moisture through pores of skin situated in hair roots
of the body and upasweda to osmosis, but earlier explanation is more logical.

Caraka says that in the first month dtma possessing all the quaiities, getting mixed up
or vitiated by all the dhatus (bhitas) attains the shape resembling the Slesma (mucoid
character) in which all the body parts though present are not conspicuous.
According to Susruta and both Vagbhatas. in the first month embryo is in the shape
of kaiala. Arunadatta says that before one week it is just like a solid mass of phlegm.
Harita elaborating the subject says that Sukra (sperms) after its union (with Sonita-
ovum) attains the form of kalala during the first day itself. In ten days the Sonita (ovum
with sperms) becomes budbuda, in fifteen days a solid, in twenty days a mass of flesh and
in twentyfive days becomes more conspicuous.
Bhawamisra opines that Sukra and artava deposited in uterus remain in their original
character (liquid state) during first month.

The embryo remains in movula sage for 4-5 days followed by blastocystic stage,
probably Arunadatta has referred to this morula as a solid mass before one week and Harita
has identified morula with kalala und blastocyst with budbuda. According to ayurvedika
philosophy all the five Shitas are present in sperms and ovum and reach there during
conception itself, thus description of their association after twentyfive days by Harita is a
bit confusing, however, it is just possible that since their functions in terms of formation
of different body parts become more conspicuous by twentyfive days, hence he has given
the description.

In second month the embryo becomes a solid mass. If this solid mass has oval (pinda)
shape the born child would be a male. if elongated (pest) the female and with rounded
(arbuda) mass the hermaphrodite. Sasruta and his follower Bhawamiéra corroborating the
above views have elaborated that these accumulated mahabhittas get processed by the
combined action of Slesmda, pitta and vayu and become solid. Harita is of the view that in
fifty days buds (of future body parts) in embryo come up.

ur आयुर्वेदीय प्रसूतितन्त्र एवं स्त्रीरोग

In third month all the indriyas and minor body parts become apparent, five buds one
for head and four for upper and lower extremities develop. Vagbhata I] opines that with the
development of head the embryo is capable of feeling sorrow or happiness. Kasyapa elabo-
rates that in this month the embryo starts quivering, develops consciousness and can feel
pain. Development of body hair is mentioned by Cakrapani.

As all the extremities etc. are already well evident just at 6th week, hence it is difficult
to explain the shape of embryo of 2nd month as described in ayurvedika classics. It is just
possible that the authors have described embryofogy on the basis of expelled products of
conception. Normally upto second month before complete formation of placenta the prod-
ucts of conception are expelled in pieces associated with big blood clots and’ the authors
could not visualize fetal parts. The expelled carneous mole might have been the source of
description of oval, round etc. shapes described earlier. Third month onwards due to for-
mation of bag of membrane and complete placenta, usually abortion resembles miniature
labour, wherein fetus with all its intact extremities may be expelled, thus the authors
conceived the idea that these might have developed in this very month.

According to @yurvedika philosophy the knowledge or perception is the result of
interaction between mana and indriyas. Since by 5th month auditory reflexes and peripheral
sensory reflexes develop to certain extent, hence the authors have mentioned the enlighten-
ment of mana. Normally the fetus of twentyone to twentyeight weeks of gestational age
does not survive if delivered, however, under specialized care the fetus of even twentyone
week (400 gms.) i.e. fast few days of fifth month can survive, thus the fetuses of twentyone
to twentyeight weeks are termed as previable. The description of ‘sujivara’ by Harita prob-

ably refers to this fact.

Caraka, Vagbhata I, II, Kasyapa and Bhavamiséra say that due to immaturity of fetus
the ojas remains unstable, it moves from mother to fetus and from fetus to the mother
through rasa carrying channels. Due to this transfer of ojas mother and fetus become happy
or dull alternately (happiness when ojas is present and dull when ojas has gone to the other
side). If delivery takes place the life becomes doubtful (at the time of delivery if ojas is in
the mother, the fetus will die, if it is in the fetus, the life of mother may be in danger). Wise
physicians do not consider this month fit for labour.

gg एवं धन्वन्तरि का मत कि सभी अंग-प्रत्यंग एक साथ उत्पन्न होते हैं अधिक युक्तिसंगत है।

There existed a lot controversy about the body part developing first and a good debate
ensued. Summing up the opinion god Dhanwantari and Atreya Punarvasu explained that all
the body parts develop simultaneously, the logic that being basic supporting structure or
abode of various features (oja, mana, atma, buddhi etc.) the heart comes first is not correct.
All the features are interrelated to each other and develop simultaneously (quoted by
Caraka). He explains further (quoted by Susruta) giving the example of sprout of bamboo
or fruit of mango, that as in the ripe mango fruit all its parts i. e. fibres, pulp, nut and kernel
are very conspicuous but are not so when it is unripe and small. It is only time factor which
is responsible for this change. Similar happenings are seen in sprout of bamboo (when it
grows, bamboo-wood, leaves etc. are apparent but not in earlier stage). Similarly in young
embryo all the features inspite of their presence are not conspicuous but are apparent after

50808 says that fetal liver and spleen get their origin from rakta, lung from the foam
and caecum from the waste product of rakta. The cream (sara) of Slesma and rakta getting
metabolised by pitta and followed by vayu form intestines, anus and bladder. Just as pure
gold is obtained by blowing (air into fire and heating the gold), similarly the tongue is
formed from the best part of kapha, rakta and mamsa getting metabolised in the abdomen.
The vayu associated with sma (pitta) canalizes the srotasas (channels), eatering the mamsa
(flesh) divides it into pests (muscles), ‘incorporating unctuous portion of medas forms ईद
(vessels) and sndyu (tendons) by mrdu (mild) and khara (strong) paka (heating) respec- °
tively; this very vayu by continuous practice or repeated actions forms the Gfayas (visceras).
The kidneys are derived from the cream portion of rakta and medas, the testicles (total
scrotum) from cream of mamsa, rakta, kapha and medas and heart from the cream of rakta .
and kapha. This heart supports all the pranavaha dhamanis (life carrying channels). Below
the heart on the left-side is spleen and lungs and on the right liver and kloma (pancreas).

VagbhataI says that. the liver and spleen are derived from essence part of blood
formed due to action of body heat influenced by force of samdana vayu. From froth of blood
the lungs; from waste product of blood and medas the vrkka (kidneys) and from essence part
of blood and flesh the intestines are formed. From essence part of slesma and blood, the
heart is formed, in left side of which the spleen and lungs and on right side the liver and
kloma are situated. From essence part of kephavaha and raktavaha srotasas as well as
mahabhitas the indriyas are derived. The tongue develops from essence part of flesh, blood
and kapha and the testicles from essence part of flesh, blood, kapha and medas.

Kaéyapa opines that prana (jiva) divides the bijadhatu (zygote) according to number
or systems of asthis (bones). The bija after its entry into the body is enveloped by rakta.
From sukra are derived bones, from bone the mamsa and from these two i. e. bone and
mamsa develop snayu (tendon) and all other major,and minor body parts alongwith indriyas.
From rakta heart is formed, from heart the liver, from liver the spleen and from spleen the
lungs. 811 these structures are attached to each other.

Caraka and Cakrapani say that there are certain permanent features in the body such
as extremities etc. and certain temporary ones such as teeth etc. Permanent feature of fetus
denote its specific female, male or hermaphrodite sex: for example permanent feature like
vulva etc. denote female sex, penis etc. a male sex and absence of both but presence of just
one aperture the hermaphrodite. Though breast (developed breast), moustache and beard etc.
are conspicuous only after birth, yet, these are also permanent features because the chest and
cheeks are permanent. The seed from which breast or hair of face would grow in chest of
female and cheeks of male respectively are present from the very birth, without the presence
of this initial seed these structures can not grow; these breast etc. develop at appropriate
period (or age) in the same way as seed of sali dropped in field will sprout only in its
appropriate season. Only apparent permanent features denote specific sex. The features
responsible for sex reside in atma (pradhana samSraya) or bhiitas of Sukra and Sonita ( guna
samSraya) and the formation of specific sex depends upon relative predominace of either
of them. The features of female are—klaivya (cowardice), bhirutwa (timorousness),
avatsaradya (lack of skill or fallibility), moha (mental confusion), anawasthdna (fickling
nature), adhogurutwa (heaviness of lower part), asahana (intolerance). Saithilya (laxity of

Besides this Sugrata quoting the views of others says that the colour of diet (used by
the mother) also influences the complexion. Vagbhata I elaborates further that (1) if semen
is white or has the colour of ghee or manda (the scum of boiled rice) the complexion would
be fair; if semen resembles oil in colour then dark and if it is honey coloured then com-
plexion would be swarthy, (2) similarly if pregnant woman has used milk etc. sweet sub-
stances and bathing or swimings then the complexion would be fair; if black tila etc. vidaht
(producing burning sensation ot pungent or actid) substances then dark and if mixture of
diet then swarthy, (3) complexion also depends upon dea (place of living), kula (race or
family) and also mode of livelihood. Indu says that all the factors together play a role in
the formation of complexion of the body.

Vagbhata I has described that complexion of body is also influenced by colour of
semen, while he himself has described only white colour of healthy semen, naturally these
colours become pathologic, and it is not possible to offer any explanation for this descrip-
tion. The concept of more than three complexions by Susruta and Harita denotes probably
their living areas, wherein these might be prevalent.

Sex of the child depends upon relative predominance of sukra or artava i.e. if कफ
is more then the fetus would be a male and if raja then a female. Caraka has further
explained that as a healthy seed after sowing sprouts and grows according to its own
character, such as the paddy seed will grow as paddy a barley seed only as barley, similarly
male or female are born according to dominance of Sukra or Grtava respectively.

श्र आयुर्वेदीय wafers एवं स्त्रीरीग

Arunadatta has mentioned that if the man first ejaculates (after the peak of orgasm)

the fetus would be male, if the female excretes first then the child would be a female. Due

‘to this very cause some of the male children have maternal characters while the females

paternal or in other words if there is predominance of sukra but female excretes first or her

orgasm perishes earlier than male the born male child will have characters of mother and
vice versa, :

Dalhana has advanced the explanation for predominance of sukra and Grtava. He says
that Grtava is four afijali and Sukra one prasyti_ in quantity or Grtava will always be more
in quantity than sukra, but it is not so, here the quantity of pure artava situated in uterus
re:ponsible for fertilization should be considered. However, occasionally due to over excite-
ment etc. the quantity of ejaculated sukra (semen) may be more, or due to psychological
depression it may be less which influences relative amount of sukra and artava. Citing the
opinions of others he has mentioned that instead of amount the functional potency of Sukra
and Grtava influences the formation of sex.

Bhavamigra corroborating the above views adds that the quantity of dosas etc. of the
body is unstable. Age, day, night, season and stage of food consumption etc. influence their
quantity or the quantity of Sukra and drtava may change due to above reasons.

Yogaratnkara besides giving the importance of predominance of Sukra and artava,
has mentioned that from daksina nadi (right ovary) the male child is born and from left the
female.

Harita says that if retas and/or sukra of male is more and raja and indriyas (sexual
power) of female is Jess then male child would be born and if retas and/or raja of female
is more and Sukrendriya (seminal ejaculate and sexual power) of male is less then female
child would be born. If sukra and raja are equal then hermaphrodite will be born. If dosas,
bala (strength), prakrti and vikrti (physiopathology) of both male and female are equal then
from fukra and raja a female hermaphrodite would take birth.

Sarngadhara says that besides role of sukra and artava, the will of god is responsible
for formation of sex.

Suéruta says that when vayu divides this bija in two pieces, the two jiwas come there,

Division of bija by vayu has been described by both Vagbhatas and Kasyapa and of :

Harita opines that origin of all fetal parts depends upon specific combination of dosas
and dhatus. When husband and wife copulate with fickling mind, then because of unstability
of mind (which influences the dosas) the twins are born, which are a source of amusement
to others.

of mother, the vitiated dosas produce abnormalities of fetus, affecting its appearance, complex-
ion and indriyas. As a tree fallen in stream of water of a river gets disfigured due to effect of
(being knocked by) woods, stones and current of flowing water, similarly the aggravated dosas
situated in kuksi (uterus) disfigure the fetus.

१८० आयुर्वेदीय प्रसूतितन्त्र एवं स्त्रीरोग

Abnormalities of Sukra and vayu, as-well-as vitiated vayu located in Sukra are also said
to produce congenital anomalies.

Caraka has explained further that teratologic abnormalities depend upon the condition
of bija, not on the physical status of couple, or in other words what-so-ever part of bija is
defective, the body part developing from that portion of. bija will be abnormal. Any organic
abnormality cai not occur without abnormality of corresponding portion of bija. Thus if the
portion of bija of a kusthi (leprous) man responsible for formation of skin is.defective then
only the born child will have kustha, however, if that, part is not abnormal then the child
will be healthy. All the indriyas are derived from Gtma, thus their presence, absence or
abnormalities depend upon the fate. An idiot or blind father does not always produce idiot
or blind child, however, if the bija of a blind man possesses the abnormal factor for
damaging eye-sight, then the born child would be blind by kakataliya nyaya, otherwise 101.
Similar hypothesis has also been expounded later, that due to abnormalities in dietetics etc.
of woman, if her entire bija becomes abnormal then she will not conceive, however, if a
small portion is defective then the born child will have the abnormality of corresponding
body part of maternal origin. Psychology of the woman also effects the fetus i.e. at the time
of impregnation, to what-so-ever type of animal the woman thinks, the child will have
similarity with that.

Suéruta says that the fetus having shape of snake, scorpion or field-pumpkin etc. are
the results of sins or bad deeds. Due to vitiation of vayu and insult or nonfulfilment of
dohrda (desires of pregnant mother) the fetus may become humpbacked, maim or croocked
armed, lame, dumb and nasal voiced. Dilating the same he writes further that this
nonfulfilment of dauhrda results in birth of crooked-leged, idiot, dwarf, dishaped-cyed or
absent-eyed child, objects/desires of what-so-ever indriya are neglected/ not provided, the
fetus develops abnormality of the same. Thus in short athcism of parents, bad deeds of
previous life (of the fetus) and aggravation of vayu are three causes of teratologic abnor-
malities. Development of body parts is a natural phenomena, the qualities and normalcy in
body parts are the results of righteousness and the abnormalities of unrighteousness. Bear-
ing-down efforts made by the woman in absence of labour pains are also said to produce
deaf, dumb, hump-backed child or the one with abnormally located body-parts.

Vagbhata I and II say that the cause of teratologic abnormalities is Vitiation of vayu
and also due to vayu located in Sukra. Indu opines that other dosas also cause fetal abnor-
malities, while Arunadatta says that upward movement of dosas is a causative factor.
Vagbhata I has enumerated the causes as impregnation of a woman of less than sixteen
years of age, conception during first three days of menstrual flow, abnormality वी Sukra and
@rtava and also delivery of hump-backed child due to bearing-down efforts made in absence
of labour pains. He has also described the abnormality of a part of bija etc. as described
by Caraka.

Bhela has enumerated bija-dosa of mother and father, absence of use of beneficial
(pathya) rasas, suppression of natural urges and yoni-dosa (gynecological abnormalities) as
causative factors for both infertility and teratologic abnormalities. The woman not using

गर्भ-विज्ञानीय अध्याय ह
१८१

proper rasas during rtukala delivers abnormal child. The couple suffering from udavarta,
consuming injurious diet give birth to a weak and blind child. The vitiation of vayu and

akaga and also curses of god result in birth of a child having abnormal shape like an
elephant or dog etc.. .

Bhavamisra emphasising the abnormality of Sukra as a cause of congenital blindness
etc. has corroborated the views of Sugruta.

Yogaratnakara has described only unrighteousness as a cause.
