(४) विकृत गर्भोत्यत्ति का भय दिखाकर स्त्री को अग्नाकृतिक संभोग की प्रक्रिया से दूर रहने का निर्देश ।

In Gyurvedika classics it is clearly mentioned that conception is the result of union of
Sukra, Grtava and jiva. The Sukra excreted by female is' useless for conception, thus the
occurance of pregnancy without active participation of male partner is neither mentioned in
classics, nor seen in practice, nor stands the test of logics. Probably due to this confusion
Jejjhatacdrya has not quoted these verses. However, probable explanations can be given in
following way:—

1) The verses are not authentic and have been added by some later worker.

2) The description is of women having perverted psychology or hypersexuality. In
various psychological conditions specially related to reproductive system ameno-
trhoea is one of the common manifestation, probably amenorrhoea followed by

_ Menstruation having excessive clotted blood is the source of this description.

3) The women having got themselves criminally aborted for illegal pregnancy, special-
ly during early stage of gestation and expelling the products of conception in pieces
gave this misleading history, which was accepted by the authors.

4) The author’s main aim was to deter the women from these abnormal sexual
behaviours by infusing fear of abnormal fetus.

nck आयुर्वेदीय प्रसूतितन्त्र एवं स्त्रीरोग

जरायु से मुख के आच्छादित होने, कण्ठ के कफ से आवेष्टित या अवरुद्ध होने तथा वायु के मार्ग का निरोध होने
के कारण गर्भस्थ शिशु नहीं रोता । टौकाकार डल्हण ने स्पष्टीकरण में लिखा है कि घोष-जनक ary के मार्ग का अव्रोध
होता है, क्योंकि नि:श्रासादि रूप वायु का वर्णन किया जा चुका है इसका मार्ग अवरुद्ध हो जाने पर गर्भ जीवित ही नहीं
रहेगा । ः

As the aperture of fetal mouth (mukha) is enveloped with Jarayu (amniotic membrane),
the throat is covered with kapha (mucus) and the passage of vayu is obstructed, hence the
fetus does not cry. Dalhana has explained that the passage of ghosa-janaka vay (vayu
capable of producing sound) is obstructed, but not of normal one, as its functions of
respiration etc. have already been described earlier and obstruction to its passage would lead
to fetal death.

SuSruta says that since the excretas are very less in quantiy and the vayu aa not in
functioning state or has negligible functions in pakwasaya (large bowel), thus the fetus does
not pass flatus, feces or urine.
Vagbhata 1 opines that since in fetus, food and liquid do not enter directly (into their
digestive system) and the ahdra-rasa is free from waste products or is essence of digestive
food, thus there is no gross amount of feces in the fetus.
Bhela and Bhavaméra have also expressed almost similar opinion.

Though normally fetus does not pass flatus or feces, however, it does secrete urine,
hence Susruta’s version of absence of: micturition does not seem to be proper. If gross
amount of feces described by Vagbhatl is considered as feces of large bowel, then it is

also not absent, though normally fetus does not pass it, yet in hypoxic state the fetus does
pass it.

Fetus never cries, however rarely, during internal version or after rupture of amniotic
membrane during normal or premature delivery, the atmospheric air entered in uterus is
inhaled then exhaled by the fetus repeatedly producing typical sound called vagitus uterinus
which does not have any untoward effect upon the fetus.

Nimitra (efficient cause) for conception, its atm (self), prakrti, gradual development
in uterus and factors responsible for growth are five auspicious features of conception. The
factors responsible for non-achievement of conception (infertility), destruction of fetus and
teratologic abnormalities are three inauspicious features or garbhavighataka (destructor of
fetus) features. The physician whe knows these eight auspicious or inauspicious features of
conception is capable of treating the king. The physician possessing bounteous intellect is
capable of understanding the methods of achievement of conception and causes of its
destruction.

The fetus stays in uterus with all its body parts fully flexed and facing towards the
back of the mother. Caraka has mentioned the position of head as upwards. Vagbhata I has
added that the fetus keeps its both palms joined together over its forehead and if it is male
its situation is more on right lateral side of abdomen, if female then on left lateral side and
if hermaphrodite then it remains centrally situated.

Bhela explaining the position of fetal head has said that Saunaka and Bhardwaja have
mentioned the situation of head as upwards and downwards respectively. However
Punarvasu Atreya has clarified that it is not so, if the head remains upwards it can kill the
mother and if downwards then will kill ownself, thus the position of head is neither upwards
nor downwards. rather it is oblique.

If the methods prescribed in vedas for achieving male or female progeny are used
before the conspicuousness (vyaktibhdva) of organs the change of sex is possible. If the
pumsawana karma is done keeping in mind the living place (4८९४०) and specific period (kala)
the result is definite, otherwise it is just reverse (if due consideration to deSa and kala is
not given then sex may not change). pusmsawana karma should be done after conception but
before conspicuousness of organs or upto two months.

before conception use of inhalation of drugs etc. foflowed by coitus is for achievement of
conception, (2) immediately following concepiion is for its proper implantation and (3)
before three months for change of sex or for having male progeny.

Vagbhata I corroborating the period given by Caraka says further that it should be
done only during pusya naksatra. Citing the opinions of others, he says that some advise
the duration of pumsawanakarma for twelve days. others during even days of these twelve
days, while some advise its daily use. Indu has given four options: (1) only on first day (2)
on even days, (3) daily (4) every even day of twelve days period. Further he says that
success depends upon the favour of luck.

Vagbhata II agreeing with the period i. e. before conspicuousness of body parts says
that potent pumsawanakarma can alter the luck. Arunadatta has explained that as a potent
pumsawanakarma can alter the luck, similarly potent luck can make the karma unsuccess-
ful, thus the success of pumsawanakarma depends upon relative strength of luck.

विमर्श (Comments)

गर्भाधान करने वाले शुक्राणु का fey गुणसूत्र निश्चित होता है, अत: गर्भाधान के पश्चात प्रयुक्त किसो भी विधि
से गर्भ के fog परिवर्तन को सम्भावना नहीं रहती | अष्टाड्डसंग्रह वर्णित बारह दिन की समय सीमा सम्भवतः ऋतुकाल
को इंगित करती है। deer seen ने औषधि प्रयोग का काल प्राम्यधर्म सेवन से पूर्व स्पष्टर लिखा
है । 'प्राकृव्यक्तोभाव' से भी गर्भ व्यक्तीभाव अर्थात्‌ गर्भाधान (शुक्र शोणित संयोग के पूर्व) के पूर्व अर्थ कर सकते हैं । यह
सम्भव है कि ऋतुकाल अर्थात्‌ गर्भाधान के पूर्व किया गया पुंसवन कर्म स्त्री-शरीर विशेषकर स्त्रीबीज में इस प्रकार के
परिवर्तन कर दे कि वह वांछित शुक्राणुओं को ही आकर्षित कर प्रविष्ट होने दे।

An ovum js fertilized by the sperm of specific sex chromosome, naturally after fertil-
ization the chances of reversal of sex by any procedure does not seem to be possible. The
time limit of twelve days given by VagbhataI probably refers to rtukala. Dalhana has
mentioned the period of use of drugs before coitus in unequivocal words. The description
before conspicuousness of body-parts can be considered as before conspicuousness of
garbha i.e. before fertilization of ovum by sperms. It is hypothetically possible that specific
procedure done before fertilization may produce some such changes in female body special-
ly in ovum, that it attracts or permits its penetration by specific sex chromosome bearing

sperms only.

आयुर्वेदीय प्रसूतितन्त्र एवं स्त्रीरोग

२००

‘After describing the [catures of sadyograhita garbha Caraka and Sugruta have men-
tioned the word + garbhint tiga’ or the signs/symptoms of a pregnant woman. Caraka has
clarified that the description is being given for recognition and management of dohrda.
Cakrapani has included third month onwards period under this category. *’agbhata { has
used the term vyakta-garbhd to which Indu has explained that these are the sigits / symp-
toms of a pregnant woman who possesses the embryo of conspicuous but under developed
body paits.

The signs / symptoms are as follows : amenorrhoea, excessive salivation, dislike for
food, vomiting, anorexia, craving for sour substances, alternate desires of high or low
articles (the eatables of high or low qualities), heaviness of body, languor of eyes, milk
secretion in breasts, blackening of lips and areola, slight edema of fect, development of
romaraji (linea nigra) and dilatation of vagina are the features mentioned by Caraka.

Suégruta and Bhavamisra besides mentioning blackening of areola and development of
linea nigra have included repeated blinking of eye lids, vomiting without apparent cause,
aversion from good smelis, salivation and tiredness ete.

Vagbhata I has written heaviness of abdomen, depression of voice and eyes, disordered
eye-lashes or quivering of eye lashes or pubic hair (Indu), sleepiness, yawning, swooning,
vomiting, anorexia, edema of feet, desire for sour or high or low articles etc. Her cheeks

and breasts become corpulent and lips and nipples become black. Increase in weight of”

embryo causes diversion of her nutrients thus energy also decreases.

Vagbhata II has given the signs/symptoms described by Caraka and Vagbhata [ with
omission of a few and addition of emaciation, indigestion, burning sensation of whole body
and expression of various desires in the list.

विमर्श (Comments)

विमर्श (Comments)

यदि गर्भिणी स्त्री का आहार-विहए सामान्य हो, वह व्याधि रहित रहे, तो चतुर्थ मास के उपरान्त सप्तम मास तक
उसके शारीरिक भार में काफी वृद्धि होती है अतः गर्भिणी में कृशता का प्रश्न ही नहीं उठता। यह सम्भव है कि त्वचा
में रंजक wel के एकत्रीकरण के कारण उत्पन्न धब्बे विशेषकर मुख के धब्बे ऐसा आभास प्रदान करें कि गर्भिणी के वर्ण
का हास हुआ है परन्तु वास्तव में ऐसा प्रत्येक गर्भिणी में नहीं देखा जाता। वर्धित होते हुए गर्भ के कारण उत्पन्न
उदरगुहान्तर-भार-वृद्धि से स्त्री की कार्य-शक्ति का हास होता है जिसे ही बल-हास शब्द से एवं जलीय-अंश कौ वृद्धि
के कारण उत्पन्न रक्त की द्रवता को रक्त के हास शब्द से सम्भवतः आचार्यों ने वर्णित किया है।

उपर्युक्त वर्णन का निश्चित स्पष्टीकरण कठिन है।

If the diet and health of the pregnant woman is normal, she gains considerable weight
from fourth to seventh month, hence the question of emaciation 2088 not arise. Face-mask
or deposition of pigments in other parts of the body might have been referred as loss of
complexion. The decrease in the working capacity due to increased intra-abdominal pres-
sure and reduction in hemoglobin concentration due to hydremia might have been referred
as loss of strength and blood respectively.

Suéruta has mentioned that the pregnant woman in whom milk secretion appears first

amrdataka etc., whose face is bright and romaraji has upward direction will deliver a male
child. Opposite to this will have a female. Whose abdomen is depressed on both sides and
projects forward and has above mentioned mixed characters will deliver a hermaphrodite.

The woman possessing two hearts (one of her own and other of the fetus) is called
dauhrdini. The period of dohrda and specific longings during this period have been de-
scribed elaborately in Gyurvedika classics. Bhela has advised to examine dauhrda of fetus

by congenial diet.

आधुनिक विज्ञान के अन्वेषणों से यह fg हो चुका है कि गर्भावस्‍था के चौथे सप्ताह में ही मानव भ्रूण का एक
कोष्टीय हृदय अपना स्पन्दन प्रारम्भ कर देता है अत: अष्टंंगसंग्रहकार द्वारा तीन पक्ष या ६ सप्ताह में द्विहदया गर्भिणी का
वर्णन सराहनीय है । ऐसा प्रतीत होता है कि स्त्री द्वारा गर्भस्पन्दनानुभूति के काल में भेद होने के कारण आचार्यों ने भिन्न
भिन्न दौहद उत्पत्ति-काल वर्णित किया है।

SuSruta and Bhavamisra have mentioned its period as fourth and Harita as third month
of pregnancy. Others have not mentioned this period separately but have referred it in the
description of fetal development, accordingly third month has been mentioned by Caraka
and Vagbhata I and second month by Vagbhata JI. However, citing the opinions of others
Vagbhatal has referred this period from three fortnights (six weeks) of conception upto the
completion of fourth or beginning of fifth month.

One chambered embryonic heat starts its first beat at the end of four weeks, thus the
description of six weeks period by Vagbhata I is praiseworthy. The difference in the period
by various authors is probably due to relative sensitivity of the woman for feeling of
quickening.

Caraka opines that when indriyas of the fetus become conspicuous, the mana gets
association of vedanda or feelings of happiness and sorrow during same period, due to this
the fetus starts quivering and expresses the desires based on the experiences of previous life,
that is why elder persons have called it dauhrda. The fetal heart formed with the maternal
components is attached to the mother’s heart via rasavahi channels and by these channels
it expresses its longings through the mother, or in other words the desires expressed belong
to the fetus not to the mother. Cakrapani says that the fetus quivers to get rid of the sorrows
and obtain happiness.

Sugruta has said that during this period due to conspicuousness of heart cefana
(consciousness) also becomes apparent as heart is its seat, thus in fourth month the fetus

त्पत्ति का वर्णन दिया

गर्भिणी-चिह्न एवं गर्भिणी-परिचर्या २१९ है

आचार्य भावमित्र ने शब्दभेद से महर्षि सुश्रुव का अनुगमन किया है' केवल 'खंज' के स्थान पर 'षण्ड' लिखा है।

Caraka says that as desires of the fetus are expressed through the mother hence
dauhrda should always be fulfilled, because the negligence or non-fulfilment can cause
abnormalities or even death of the fetus. Mostly welfare of the mother is identical to that
of the fetus, thus wise persons always treat pregnant woman affectionately and with ben-
eficial substances. What-so-ever the dwihrdaya woman desires. it should be fulfilled except
the things likely to injure or fell-upon the fetus. However, if her desire to use the articles
likely to harm the fetus is very acute, the articles should be provided with addition of
beneficial substances capable of counteracting the harmful effects. Suppression of desires
vitiates vayu, which moving in the body of the fetus produces various diseases, abnormal-
ities or even death. Cakrapani has clarified that suppression of acute desires causes death
of the fetus while that of mild ones the abnormalities. If desires of fetus expressed by the
mother are suppressed then due to direct association of these desires with very delicate
fetus, its vayu gets vitiated and injures it. However, if mother’s own desires are suppressed
then vitiated vayu of mother reaches the fetus, because welfare (the condition providing
pleasure or satisfaction and the opposite or harmful things to be given up) of both is same,
and this aggravated vayu influencing mana (psyche) of the fetus produces various abnormal-
ities. At certain times due to slight difference in welfare of both, the abnormalities of mother
like hunger etc. do not affect the fetus. This congenial and affectionate treatment should be
extended even to non pregnant woman during rtukala.

Susruta has mentioned that non-fulfilment of desires produces the fetus: which is
hump-backed, crooked armed and leged, idiot, dwarf, dis-shaped eyed or has absence of
eyes. What-so-ever she desires should be fulfilled due to fear of fetal abnormalities. Non-
fulfilment can harm both mother and fetus, specially suppression of desirés related to
specific indriya produces abnonmality of corresponding indriya of the fetus. Fulfilmertt of
desires results in birth of child possessing high qualities and longevity. .

Both Vagbhatas have followed Caraka describing the subjectin short, similarly Bhavamisra
has followed Sufruta substituting crooked leg with impotence.

Harita has mentioned that fulfilment of dauhrda gives birth to a very handsome,
valiant, intelligent and well behaved child.

Caraka says that the pregnant woman desirous of producing a thorough (healthy and
good looking) child should give up non-congenial diet and mode of life and protect herself
by doing gocd conduct and using congenial diets and mode of life.

Suéruta has advised that the woman from the very first day of pregnancy should
remain in high spirit, pious, decorated with omaments, wear clean white garments and
perform religious rites, do auspicious deeds and worship deity, bra@hmanas and privst. Her

sleeping and sitting place should be covered with soft cushion or mattress, not be very high,
d-rest and should be perfect and very comfortable.

She should use palatable, liquid, sweet and unctuous substances treated with appetizing

things. This mode of life should be continued till delivery.

Vagbhata I has said that since welfare and contraindications of mother and fetus are
identical, hence the pregnant woman should use desired congenial diet and proper mode of
life, avoiding factors likely to harm the fetus. The pregnant woman is fit for the use of

vrmhana (anabolic) therapy.

Vagbhata If has advised external (for preparing water for bathing or irrigation etc). and
internal (powder, cold percolation, decoction etc.) use of jivantya group of drugs. Atfection-
ate and good behaviour of husband and servants helps in maintenance of pregnancy. She
should always use butter, ghrta and milk ete.

Kasyapa says that what-so-ever eatables or drinkable are consumed by the pregnant
woman, same become congenial to the fetus, thus diet should be taken considering place of
living, time or season and digestive capacity, it should never be neglected. She should use
meritorious, auspicious, pious, new and intact or unbroken garments and ornaments possess-
ing masculine names. No article bearing feminine or common gender name should ever be
used. Her appropriate abode is that which is being fumigated (with fragrant drugs), where
worships are being performed, is free from insects like mosquito etc., vedic hymns are being

महर्षि हारीत ने इस मास में घृतपूरक या घेवर का प्रयोग बताया है ।

Caraka says that in this month rice gruel prepared with milk and mixed with ghrta
should be given. Bhadrakapya opines that it shouid not be given, because by use of this the
child may become tawny in complexion. Punarvasu. Atreya agrees that it does produce
tawny complexion, however, it is not useless, because by use of this the pregnant woman
remains free from diseases, and delivers the child possessing best health, energy, complex-

.ion, voice, compactness of the body and much superior to other family members. Cakrapani

explains that since the side-effects are negligible and benefits much more hence it should
be used.

Suégruta has indicated that in this month for clearing the retained feces and anulomana
(regulation or putting in right direction) of vayu. the dsth@pana basti (evacuative enema)
should be given with decoction of badai mixed with bald, atibald, Satapuspa, palala
(pestled sesamum seeds), milk, curd, mastu (sour butter), oil, salt, madanaphala, honey and
ghrta. This should be followed by use of anuvasana basti (uncting enema) of oil medicated
with milk and decoction of drugs of madhura group. Due to movement of vayu in its right
direction the lady delivers without difficulty and remains free from complications. After this
she should be given unctuous gruels and meat-soup of wild animals. The body of woman

thus treated becomes unctuous, she gains strength and delivers normally without complica-
tions.

Vagbhata I has incorporated the description of both Caraka and Suéruta with only
replacement of name of Bhadrakapya to Khandakapya and achievement of sarwa (vitality)

month, however, in the regimen of eighth month after use of enema continuous use of

indicates that Susruta has advised use of unctuous gruel and meat-soup of wild animals in
ninth month also.

गर्भिणी-चिह्न एवं गर्भिणी-परिचर्या . २२७

Emphasizing the importance of woman’s diet authors have mentioned that the rasa
derived from the diet taken by the pregnant woman serves three purposes (1) nourishment
of her own body, (2) nourishment of the fetus and (3) nourishment of breast or formation
of milk which has already been discussed under fetal nourishment.

मधुरवर्ग की औषधियाँ वृंहण हैं, अतः इन दोनों के प्रयोग से गर्भ एवं गर्भिणी का स्वास्थ्य सामान्य रहेगा।

During first trimester of pregnancy most women experience nausea and vomiting, thus
can not take proper diet. Use of cold and sweet liquid diet and milk will prevent dehydration
and supply required nourishment, besides the drugs of madhura group being anabolic will
help in maintenance of proper health of mother and fetus. Fourth month onwards muscular
tissue of fetus grows sufficiently requiring more protein which is supplied by use of meat-
soup. By the end of second trimester most women suffer from edema of feet and other
complications of water accumulation. Use of goksuru a good diuretic in sixth month will
prevent retention of water as well as its complications. The drugs of viddrigandhadi group
are diuretic, anabolic, relieve emaciation and suppress pitta and kapha, their regular use in
seventh month might help in maintaining health of mother and fetus. Most women expe-
rience constipation in late pregnancy due to pressure of gravid uterus over the bowels and
effect of progesterone. Use of enema in eighth month will relieve this constipation, besides
this may also affect the autonomous nervous system governing myometrium and help in
fegulating their function during labour. Tampon of oil may destroy pathogenic bacteria of

influence autonomic fibres governing myometrium and help in regulating their functions,
Besides, this might soften the perineum and help in its relaxation during labour.

Milk and drugs of madhura group have been advised for entire pregnancy period. Milk
is a whole diet. The drugs of madhura group are anabolic, thus use’ of these will help in
maintenance of proper health of mother and growth and development of fetus.

Caraka says that the pregnant woman should aviod use of pungent things, (excessive)
exercise and coitus, Following factors are harmful for the fetus such as—use of excessive
heavy, hot and pungent substances; harsh or voilent activities (activities niuch beyond one’s
own capacity) and others as instructed by elder persons, she should not wear red garments
for protection from the effect of gods, demons and their followers; should not use intoxi-
cating substances and wine, ride over vehicle (running on uneven path), use meat (exces-
sive) and give up the things contrary to indriyas and other harmful articles, the things
should also be given up as instructed by old ladies.

Susruta has mentioned that from the day of conception the woman should totally give
up coitus, excercise, excessive satiation (samlarpana or anabolics), excessive emaciation
(apatarpana or catabolism), sleeping in day and awakening in night, grief, riding on vehicle,
fear, squatting or the posture of sitting on the hams with the soles of feet touching the
ground (utkatukésana}, and avoid untimely use of snehana (oleation), blood letting and
suppression of natural urges. The coitus troubles the fetus. She should not touch dirty or
disfigured persons possessing less body parts; should give up foul smelling, awful looking
substances and exciting stories; should not eat dried up, stale, putrified or wet (moistened)
food. She should avoid outing, visit of lonely place, chaitya (haunted tree), cremation
ground or shade of a tree,.acts likely to promote anger and disgrace, talking in high pitch
etc. all the things likely to harm the fetus. Repeated excessive massage of oil and unguents
should not be done, and she should not fatigue herself.

Vagbhata [ has corroborated the views of Caraka, however, alike Susruta he has also
given the list of contraindications as—coitus, exercise, emaciation, trauma, conveyance i.e.
carriage or animals causing excessive jerks, night awakening, day sleeping, suppression of

२४० आयुर्वेदीय प्रसूतितन्र एवं स्त्रीरोग

केशी (जटामाँसी), शतवीर्या, सहख्वीर्या आदि औषधियों को प्रजापत्य विधि से उखाड़कर बाद में पुष्य नक्षत्र में धारण
करे । frga को मणि बनाकर गर्भिणी et कमर में हर समय बाँधे ।

Caraka and Kasyapa have prescribed certain’ drugs during pregnancy without specify-
ing their indications, period or method of use. Cakrapani has clarified that garbhasthapana
drugs are those which after counteracting the effect of harmful factors (, garbhopaghatakara
bhavas) for fetus help in its proper maintenance, thus these can be considered even as a
treatment for abortion.

Vagbhata I has indicated use of prajasihapana drugs described in siitrasthana after
purtsawana karma. Indu says that these drugs prevent abortion.

Kagyapa has advised these to be used as a routine by pregnant woman. Routine use
of these drugs might be beneficial for maintenance of proper health, growth and develop-
ment of mother and fetus respectively. With this idea the drugs are being enumerated here.

Caraka and Vagbhata have enumerated aindri, brahmi, satavirya, sahasravirya or
durva,amogha, avyatha, Siva, arista, vatyapuspi, viswaksenakata or viswaksena in the list
and have advised the oral use of milk or ghrta prepared with these drugs. The bath with
these drugs (cold decoction of these drugs) during pusya naksatra should also be taken.
These drugs should also be kept in close contact of mother and amulets of these be tied in
head or right arm (only Caraka). Similarly the drugs of jivaniya group should also be used.

Kaéyapa has advocated that bahuputra, ananta, téwari, mudita, brahmi, sahadeva,
indravaruni, jivaka, rsabhaka, bharngi, samanga, rohapada, vata Sunga (leaf bud), Gtma-
gupta, arista, pittana, kes, Sataviryé and sahasravirya drugs should be uprooted with
enchantation of mantras and tied as amulet during pusya naksatra. Amulet of trivrta should
also be tied in the waist of pregnant woman.

Caraka opines that the diseases of pregnant woman should be treated with the use of
soft, sweet, cold, pleasing and gentle drugs, dietetics and behaviour. She should not be given
emetics, purgatives or suberrhines (sternutatery drugs), bloodletting should not be done.
Asthapana and anuwasana basties (cleansing and nutritive enemas) should not be used
frequently, however, if the disorder is acute, moderate use of these can be done. After eighth
month the diseases curable by emetics etc. should be treated with gentle emesis etc. OF such
other procedures which give similar benefits, such as instead of emetics or putgatives the
drugs causing spitting or suppositories respectively should be used. Use of pungent drugs,
exercise and coitus should be avoided. The pregnant woman should be treated just like a
pot filled with oil, as slightest oscillation of such pot causes spilling of oil. similarly
slightest excitement to the pregnant woman can initiate abortion etc.

Suéruta has advised that if the disease is acute and/or serious, emetics should be given

followed by use of sweet and sour edibles mixed with anulomaka (carminative) drugs. All
food or drinks. Diet should

the pacifying drugs should be soft and be given alongwith
consist of the. article which are soft, sweet and harmless to the fetus. Appropriate use

(neither too less, nor excessive not abnormal) of such gentle emeties etc. purifying measures

should be done which are congenial to the fetus.
$ of Caraka adds that if the disease is very serious,

Vagbhata corroborating the view:
the life of woman should be saved by use of drastic measures and pungent drugs (even if
those are harmful to the fetus).

गर्भिणी-व्याधियाँ एवं उनकी चिकित्सा २४७

उपर्युक्त वर्णित विषय का अवलोकन करने पर गर्भ वमन के निम्न तीन कारण स्पष्ट होते हैं ।

All the classics have mentioned excessive salivation and nausea etc. as symptoms of
normal pregnancy. In the description of disease chardi Suéruta has enlisted pregnancy also
as a causative factor. Under its fifth type i. e. @gantuja or dwistarthaja chardi the dauhrda
is also enumerated in etiology. Dalhana has explained that non fulfilment of dauhrda and
presence of fetus cause vomiting. In Madhukosa commentary it is mentioned that vayw
being pushed upward by fetus gets provoked and causes vomiting. For its management
assessment of relative predominance of various dosas should be made. This statement
clearly indicates that this description is aimed at mentioning disease hyperemesis
gravidarum having etiopathogenesis identical to general chardi. Above mentioned
etiopathogenesis clarifies three specific causes for this hyperemesis gravidarum:

(2) बातव-वैगुण्य (Vata-vaigunya)
वायुदोष नाड़ीवह संस्थान का च्योतक है, अत: इसकी विगुणता से स्त्री की संज्ञावह नाड़ियों के कार्य में विगुणता

आकर विपरीत प्रत्यावर्तन (रीफ़लेक्स had) हो वमन हो सकता है, अथवा स्त्री की मानसिक स्थिति (इमोशेनेल या
साइकॉजेनिक फ़ैक्टें) में विकार हो वमन हो सकता है।

Vata denotes nervous system including psychology of individual. Abnormality of this
may initiate vomiting by exaggerated or abnormal reflex action or in other words this
heading indicaies reflex and psychogenic factors as causation of hyperemesis.

(2?) deg अवमानन (Dauhrda avamanana or non. fulfiiment of dauhrda)
स्त्री को अधिकांशतया दौहद उन चीजों का होता है जिनकी शरीर में कमी होती है। दौहद को अपूर्ति से उस
कमी के कारण का अन्तर्भाव कर सकते हैं। है

Normally the woman desires the substances for whom she is deficient. Nonfulfilment
of these may produce certain deficiency and this may initiate vomiting.

(3) गर्भ निमित्त (Garbha nimitta or due to fetus)

जहाँ गर्भावस्‍था के अतिरिक्त अन्य कोई भी कारण ज्ञात न हो अर्थात्‌ ट्रॉफॉब्लास्ट द्वारा निर्मित अंगरसों के प्रति स्त्री
द्वारा प्रतिक्रिया WI अथवा अज्ञात कारणजन्य।

Where in except existance of pregnancy there is no other demonstrable cause, thus
vomiting occurs either due to immune response of woman for trophoblastic hormones or
idiopathic. .

महर्षि काश्यप ने अन्तर्वत्नीचिकित्साध्याय में विभिन्न दोषोत्पन्न छर्दि की चिकित्सा का वर्णन किया है, परन्तु दौहदजन्य
या गर्भजन्य छर्दि की विशिष्ट चिकित्सा का उल्लेख नहीं किया। जिससे स्पष्ट होता है कि यह वर्णन गर्भिणी कौ विशिष्ट
oft (हाइपेंडमेसिस tae) का न होकर गर्भावस्‍था में होने वाली अन्य कारणोत्पन्न छर्दि (अंसोशिएटेड वॉमिटिंग)
का है।

उपर्युक्त वर्णन के आधार पर गर्भिणी छर्दि का निम्न वर्गकरण कर सकते हैं:-

(अ) लक्षणान्तर्गत वर्णित हल्लस या मुखप्रसेक इमेसिस ग्रेविडेरम या ifr fate

Before fourth month of pregnancy if woman suffers from fever, she should be advised
to fast for one day, followed by use of drinkabies free from fat and salt. Use of pungent
dietetics and drinkables, sudorifics and exercise should be avoided. She should take only
rice gruel. After subsedence of aggravated dosas by the use of rice gruel, the wise physician
should prescribe her cereals with soups. With further subsidence of dosas by this procedure
she should be advised meat soups and milk. No medicine should be given.

में neti काश्यप ने ज्वगवस्था में प्रयुक्त शोधन कर्मों से उत्पन्न उपद्रवों का वर्णन किया है। वर्णन की सुगमता एवं
सम्पूर्ण विषय के एक स्थान में संकलन को दृष्टि से महर्षि चरक, वाग्भट एवं काश्यप आदि सभी के द्वारा वर्णित विषय
एक साथ हो दिया जा रहा है। ज्वरार्त होने पर गर्भिणी स्त्री को अग्निकर्म, विष -प्रयोग तथा लंधर्न निषिद्ध है।

All the authors have enlisted the state of pregnancy as one of the condition in which
use of cleansing measures such as oleation, sudation, emesis, purgation, enemas before
seventh month, inbalations (nasya), smoking, cauterization, application of corrosive agents
and venesection etc. are contraindicated. Caraka has described certain complications likely
to occur in pregnant woman by use of sternutatory drugs, emetics and purgatives (described
in subsequent pages). Other authors have also warned that use of these cleansing measures
in the unfit persons can make their disease incurable or even cause death. All these
contraindication are for pregnant woman in general, not specific to the febrile state, how-

ever, Kagyapa has described certain complications of these various measures if applied ©

during febrile state of pregnancy. Description of all these authors is given together in
subsequent pages. Use of cauterization, visa (poisonous articles) and fasting is
contraindicated to a febrile pregnant woman.

If constipation occuring due to uddvarta during eighth month of pregnancy is not
relieved either by use of anuvdsana basti (uncting enema) or else with unctuous edibles
mixed with substances capable of suppressing vata alongwith uncting enema with the oil
prepared with madhuka, then it should be considered as incurable by this procedure and
niritha basti (evacuative enema) prepared with following drugs should be used.

Roots of virana, sali, sastika, kuéa, kaSa, iksuwalika, vetasa and parivyadha; bhitika,
ananta, kaSmari, pariisaka, madhuka and mrdwika all should be cooked with standard
procedure of decoction keeping half quantity of water and half milk, when quantity of water
and milk together is reduced to oneeighth, it should be filtered. Now in this filtrate paste
of priyala, kernel of bibhitaka and tila along with little quantity of salt should be mixed and
niritha basti of this very substance keeping it juke warm should be given. Vagbhata has
omitted sastika.

कारण किसी भी अवस्था में अतिसारजनक हो सकते हैं, परन्तु गर्भिणी में अल्प विकार भी अतिसारोत्यादक हो सकते हैं ।

All the above mentioned etiological factors can be grouped under five categories : (1)
Dietetic abnormalities producing digestive disturbances resulting into diarrhoea or indiges-
tion diarrhoea. (2) Use of uncooked fruits and polluted water resulting into entry of infective
organisms or infective diarrhoea. (3) Fear, grief etc. psychological trauma or nervous diar-
rhoea. (4) Satiation or emaciation etc. or nutritional diarrhoea. (5) Due to dosas or other
diseases of body or toxic diarthoea. All these conditions can cause diarrhoea to any body,
however, during pregnancy presence of least abnormalities may produce diarrhoea.

After describing the treatment of various disorders afflicting a pregnant woman
Kigyapa has mentioned certain signs/symptoms, presence of which indicates bad prognosis.
These can be classified under three categories:

i) Signs/symptoms likely to injure the fetus or in other words if pregnant woman
exibits these, the fetus will either die or get aborted.

ii) Signs/symptoms in presence of which born child dies. It is just possible that these
signs/symptoms might be appearing in third trimester of pregnancy but do not
cause immediate danger to the fetus, howevc:, produce some such abnormality
that neonate is unable to survive in new environment.

iii) In first two categories though clinical features appear in mother, yet do not harm
her, but clinical features of third category show bad prgnosis for the pregnant
woman herself.

Out of five verses mentioned above probably first hints towards excessive anaemia,
second to diabetes mellitus (as excessive eating and unconsciousness are the clinical fea-
tures) and third to nephritis or toxaemia of pregnancy (edema around the eyes is a sign).
In all the above three conditions, if these turn serious, abortion is inevitable. Fourth verse
probably indicates some congenital abnormality of uterus and the fifth to arthritis. Though
normally arthritis does not cause abortion or intrauterine death of fetus, however, in acute
conditions these complications may happen.

from mouth, unconsciousness and delirium does not survive.

labour), who wears red garments and garlands, uses red anointments, smiles during sleep
and goes towards cremation ground does not survive.

The pregnant woman who dreams of riding over donkey, hog, buffalo, dog or camel
does not survive.

80809 says that if the trouble is intolerable or incurable, abortion should be induced,
lest the condition of woman deteriorates further or even she dies, the available short time
should not be wasted.

Dalhana has explained this verse that in event of failure of teatment with Sastra
(instruments) and mantra etc. the abortion should be induced to protect the life of pregnant
woman, The word ‘adi’ i.e. etc. used after mantra, refers to use of drugs. This verse follows
indications of destructive surgery for midha garbha (obstructed labour), but does not appear
to be related to it, because Sugruta has used term garbhapata for expulsion of fetus in fifth
or sixth month, while obstruction in the process of labour occures after this period i.e.
seventh month onwards. Explanation of Dalhana i.e. failure with the treatment with instru-
ment, mantra etc. (drugs) does not appear to be proper, because these are the only methods
to terminate pregnancy of any duration. The emphasis on available short time indicates
acuteness of disorder. Considering acuteness and seriousness of disorder and indication of
abortion it may be considered as a description of toxaemia of pregnancy.

Revati produces various abnormalities by afflicting the woman during her various

garding birth of revit. Prajapati initially created kala followed by ceva, asura, father,
human being, seven domestic and wild animals alongwith medicinal herbs and plants. After
all this he created ksudhd (hunger) which entered in his own body. To get rid of this hunger

he consumed essence of herbs and plants. After getting satiated, he transferred this hunger -

to the kéifa. The hungry kdla started eating devas and asuras. Pleased with the prayers of
devas and asuras. prajdpati preached them about amrta (nectar). Devs, aller using this
nectar defeated both ksudha@ and kala. Defeated kala snatched all above things from
prajapati and then asuras attacked devas. One asura daughter named dirghajihvi started
killing devas. On the prayers of the devas, kartikeya sent revati, Who impersonating a she
jackal first of all killed dirghajihvi and further started killing the army of asuras. Lateron
assuming the shape of vulture started showering meteor, thunder-bolt, stones and weapons.
Getting defeated, these asuras entered the embryos of human and other animals. Revatt
assuming the name of jataharini killed these réksasas there also. This jataharint is known
by names of revati, pilipicchika, raudri and varuni. By the permission of skanda, she
afflicts the impious or immoral persons of all the castes and kills villainous or unrighteous
persons. She is seen by divine vision and religious virtues are the only remedies.

The jataharini after entering inside the body through the pores created by unrighteous
acts produces following clinical features.

Due to affliction by jataharini the woman gets withered and has these clinical fea-
tures :— bewildered looks, absence of nourishment in appropriate time, unsteadiness of
psychology {satwa) or decline in endurance, absence of enthusiasm, pain in abdomen,
disagreable looks and suffers from various disorders. She starts every work in opposite way
and consumes opposite or non congenial edibles. She commences every work in unbridled
way with impudence and abnormality. She does not get money, her property is lost. The
calves of her cow, goat, sheep and buffalo do not survive. She gets badly defamed, becomes
widow and jafahdrini after seizing destructs her family.

The expulsion of fetus upto fourth month of pregnancy is termed as garbha-srava
because the products of conception are liquid, there after in fifth and sixth months it is
termed as garbha-pdta, because by this period the fetal parts have attained some stability
or have become solid. Bhoja opines (quoted in Madhukosa commentary of Madhava
Nidana) that the period of garbha srava is upto three months.

Expulsion of fetus from very early or blastocystic stage to second trimester is the
main clinical feature of andaghni, durdhara, kalaratri and vasya etc. jataharintes, similarly
putraghni (repeated abortion of sthita garbha or after fourth month), vadmini (expulsion of
raja alongwith Sukra or very young zygote) and asraja or apraja (abortion due to bleeding
after conception) etc. yonivydpad also denote repeated abortion. Thus while considering the
etiology of abortion causes of yonivyapad have also to be considered. Mithydacdra,
Grtavadosa, bijadosa and daiva-prakopa are main causes of yonivydpad. Taking into ac-
count the causes of abortions, yonivyapat and also jataharini following factors may be held
responsible for abortion.

1) Unknown or idiopathic—Curses of god, infliction by ja@taha@rini and effect of
deeds of previous life.

2) Fetal factors—
a) Genetic or chromosomal defects or bijadosa.

b) Fetal infections or krmi.
c) Other diseases of fetus.

3) Maternal factors—

a) Abnormalities of anatomic components of reproductive systems i.e. garbhdsaya or
. yonidosa.

b) Hyperactivity or stimulation of myometrium—

1) Reflex stimulation of myometrium in diarrhoea etc. or during suppression of nat-
ural urges.

2) Sudden increase in intraabdominal pressure due to trauma, racing, walking, falling,.
sleeping in abnormal posture etc. described earlier as well as due to straining in
diarhoea etc. causing myometrial hyper-stimulation.

3) Hyper excitability of nerves or abnormalities of vata.

The pathogenesis of obstructed [80007 and abortion is described together.

descending downwards from the hallow space between liver, spleen and bowels produces
irritation in the abdominal cavity. The apane vdyu getting aggravated due to this irritation
causes pain in flanks, kuksi (lower abdomen or uterus), bastisirsa (neck of bladder), abdo-
men and vagina, along with flatulence or distention of abdomen, retention of urine etc.
several other symptoms and troubles the young fetus with bleeding.

ग्र्भ-चलन की चिकित्सा (Treatment of garbha-calana)

महर्षि हारीत एवं योगरलाकरकार ने गर्भ-चलन की भी मासानुमासिक चिकित्सा का वर्णन किया है। गर्भ का
चलायमान होना उसकी अपरिहार्यता का द्योतक है अतः इसकी चिकित्सा करने से साधारणतया गर्भ के स्थित होने अर्थात्‌
गर्भपात न होने का प्रश्न ही नहीं उठता। ऐसा संभव है कि यहाँ पर आचार्यों का चलायमान से तात्पर्य गर्भल्ाव-प्रक्रिया
की प्रारम्भ की अवस्था अर्थात्‌ जब तक कि गर्भ परिहार्य है अर्थात्‌ रोका जा सकता है से हो अथवा गर्भचलन का तात्पर्य
गर्भ की अत्यधिक गतिशीलता (स्पन्दन) से हो।

The word calana or movement indicates the movement from its own normal place,
thus the question of prevention of expulsion of fetus in case of garbha-calana should not
have arisen. However, in the classics, month-wise treatment of this condition has also been
prescribed, which shows that’ probably this is also a condition of threatened abortion or
exessive quivering.

Powdered lodhra and magadhika mixed with honey and milk should be prescribed for

गर्भपात प्रतिषेधार्थ वरणबन्ध (Varanabandha for preventing abortion}

महर्षि काश्यप ने कल्पस्थान के रेवती कल्पाध्याय के अंत में गर्भिणी स्त्री को वरणबन्ध बाँधने का विधान बताया
है। यह वरणबस्ध मंत्र-चिकित्सा का ही एक रूप है, इसकी उपादेयता के बारे में निश्चित रूप से कुछ भी कहना कठिन
है, लोक में भी यह अधिक प्रचलित नहीं है।

Kasyapa has prescribed a type of mantra treatment for preventing abortion. It is
difficult to explain its utility as it is not in practice.

वरणबन्ध का काल (Period of varanabandha)

बन्धो हि गर्भिण्या: क्षयति प्रागष्टमान्मासात्‌, अत ऊर्ध्ब॑ प्रतिषेधस्तस्यान्यत्र ॥ (ato Ho कल्प० ६/८० )
यह बन्ध गर्भिणी को आठवें मास के पूर्व ही बाँधना चाहिए। आठवें मास के पश्चात्‌ इसको प्रयोग करने का .
निषेध है। -
‘It 06 be applied before eighth month. After this month it is contraindicated.
विमर्श (Comments)

चूँकि वरणबन्ध का मुख्य उद्देश्य गर्भपात का निवारण है एवं नवम मास का एक भी दिन हो जाने पर प्रसवकाल
माना जाता है, अत: आठवें मास के बाद वरणबन्ध का निषेध यथोचित ही है।

Since the purpose of this treatment is prevention of abortion or premature delivery,
hence its contraindication after eighth month is justified.

वरणबन्ध की उपादेयता (Benefits of varayabandha)

महर्षि काश्यप ने वरणबन्ध का वर्णन करते समय बन्धन विधि में मांगी विद्या के प्रयोग का विधान बताया है । जिस
विद्या की उपादेयता का वर्णन करते हुए इसे स्वस्ति एवं शान्तिकर, GI को उत्पन्न करने वाली, गर्भ का बन्धन करने
चाली, विमल, अमोघ, कल्याण करने वाली बताया है तथा लिखा है कि ऋतुमती स्त्री को सुनाये जाने पर वह गर्भवती
हो जाती है, गर्भवती स्त्री को सुनाए जाने पर वह पुत्र वाली हो जाती है, प्रसव-कष्ट से पीड़ित को सुनाये जाने पर उसे
via प्रसव हो जाता है तथा जिसके पुत्र मर जाते हैं उसे सुनाये जाने पर उसके पुत्र जीवित रहते हैं. । इन लाभों के अतिरिक्त
इस विद्या को भय एवं शत्रु का नाशक आदि भी बताया है, जो अप्रासड्जिक होने के कारण यहाँ पर वर्णन नहीं किए जा
रहे ।

सम्पूर्ण वरणबन्ध की उपादेयता के at में लिखा है कि इससे स्त्री को aan की प्राप्ति होती है, उसे सर्वभूतों

Pious and fasting physician should apply varanabandha to the woman, who has rev-
erence, observes righteous virtues and has been fasting for three days. After this bandha she
should worship the goddess by desired sacrificial offerings, thus the goddess provides her
with progeny. For this the woman should take bath during sambhdra or rohini naksatra, It
should be taken inside the house during night, while during day time secretly amidst the
forest is the opinion of persons. The process of bath should be started after protecting her
by covering the place from all the sides. Now the physician should besmear with cow-dung
and water the altar made in pious place and measuring in size to gecaria . The physician
ufter taking bath and wearing new garments and ornaments should sit facing to the east, and

twice or thrice (according to some other persons). After this he should touch his both the
eyes, ears, nose and anus with (fingers dipped in) water. When the bright sun is visible he
should bedew the altar and write the symptoms narrated by the pregnant woman on the
bunch of darbha which is held alongwith the gold by the pregnant woman; after writing the
symptoms he should bedew the bunch of darbha, go out and do obeisance to the fire.
Afterwards, collecting all the things needed for yajfia should sanctify these; then holding
kusas he should go round the altar from left to right direction, thus, keeping the fire always
on the right side. He should now place the idols of kumara, sastht and visakha made with
any one out of gold, silver, ustra or darbha in front of fire, the brakma of yajfia in the south
and pot of water in the north side. After sanctifying the ghrta with two darbha of similar
length with intact tips and tied together, he should recite the mantra that this is ajya,

of sacrificial ladle made of darbhas for oblation. Now the pregnant woman who has already

quietly over a wooden comfortable seat facing northwards, holding two darbhas. The preg-
nant woman should sit calm and quiet. The physician after obtaining the permission of
others should offer oblation in the fire daily and after pouring ghyta in the fire offer,

Due to non-availability of proper diet (nourishment) to the fetus or vaginal discharges
(bleeding) after conception the fetus suffers from Sosa (emaciation or dryness). This fetus
attains its proper growth or maturity after years and the woman delivers it after years or
prolong delay. Vayu is also said to be a cause for dryness of fetus.

SuSruta opines that due to affliction by vayu the fetus gets dried up, does not fill
properly the mother’s abdomen and quivers very slowly. Dalhana elaborating the etiology
says that due to effect of vayu the fetus has absence of ojas. Further quoting Vrddha
Kasyapa writes that the rasa either flows slowly or does not flow in the rasavahdnadt of
fetus thus it developes very slowly

The upwards moving vayu dries rasavahi channels of the fetus, thus it suffers from
vata disorders, becomes emaciated and remains in uterus for years together is the opinion
of Vagbhata I. Vagbhata II opines that vayu dries the fetus

Bhela says that when vayu situated in yoni gets mixed up with sukra and conception
takes place with the union of healthy Grtava and this vitiated Sukra, then if bleeding occurs,
the fetus gets destroyed and this condition is termed as vatodara.

Bhavaprakaga and Yogaratnakara have followed Susruta.

After some development and attainment of sara (after fourth month) by the fetus if
bleeding per vaginum or other types of vaginal discharges occur due to use of pungent and
hot articles by the pregnant woman, then the fetus does not grow properly due to these
discharges, and stays in the uterus for a very long time. This condition is termed as
upavistaka.

Vagbhata I mentioning the causes of upavistaka and upasuska both together writes that
after attainment of sara by the fetus if woman uses contraindicated articles, bleeding per
vaginum or other vaginal discharges start. Vata aggravated due to this bleeding withholding
pitta and slesma compresses the rasavaha nadi of the fetus. Because of this obstruction to
rasavaha nadi causing improper flow of rasa, the fetus does not develop properly and
becomes upavistaka or upasuska, in the same way as the paddy does not grow properly if
the water does not reach the field due to obstruction with leaves and grass etc. to its flow

it. This is called n@godara. In this condition size of abdomen also decreases and quivering
of fetus is delayed.

under-developed fetus remains in the uterus for years just like the fetus of elephant. Because
of the bleeding per vaginum occurring after the fetus has become jétasdra (after 4th month
of pregnancy) it does not develop properly. gets desiccated and remains in the uterus.

Bhavapraka§a and Yogaratnakara have given similar description as written by Susruta.

Preceding descriptions clearly show that garbhafosa or ksaya is a condition of
underdevelopment of fetus due to inadequate nutrition or intrauterine growth retardation of
fetus.

Upavistaka (not described by SuSruta) is a condition developing fourth month on-
wards in pregnancy having bleeding per vaginum, absence of further development of uterus
but presence of quickening of fetus.

Caraka and Vagbhata II have not specified any gestational age of fetus for upasuska
or nagodara. Susruta considers it a diseases of very early gestational age while Vagbhata I
has mentioned that this entity also develops fourth month onwards. Susruta has incorpo-
rated two conditions under this i. e. carrying away of fetus by naigamesa and nagodara.
It is just possible that in very early pregnancy due to absence of proper development,
the fetal parts could not be detected by the woman during its expulsion, thus she thought
that it has been taken away by bhkiitas, however, when fetus remained in uterus without

garbhasaya (uterus) and have regular appearance of drtava (menstrual blood or ovum)
which is accumulated. It does not develop in young girls or aged women.

Their absence of freedom, ignorance and engagement in service of others is also
responsible for development of raktagulma (due to above causes she may have to suppress
her natural urges which may aggravate doses). Cakrapani and Indu opie that this disease
develops in active reproductive age, neither to the young girls due to absence of menarche,
nor to aged women due to menopause, or even to the women having watery menstruation.
However gulma of rakta dhdtu can develop even to men.

Fert एवं सम्प्राप्ति (: Etiopathogenesis)

महर्षि चरक ने चिकित्सास्थान तथा अष्यांगसंग्रहकार ने निदानस्थान में सामान्य गुल्मों के निदान एवं सम्प्राप्ति का

General etiopathogenesis described for all types of gulmas is not to be considered here.
Cakrapani has very clearly mentioned that this general etiopathogenesis does not apply for
raktagulma. Specific etiopathogenesis is given here-under.

‘The woman who suppresses her natural urges due to absence of freedom, ignorance
and engagement in service of others and uses vata agyravating diet or mode of life during
amagarbha (pregnancy of very short duration), immediately following abortion, delivery or
during rtuk@la (menstrual period), her vayu gets aggravated very quickly. This aggravated
vayu entering garbhasayadwara (cervix uteri) obstructs the Grtava (menstruation). Every
month accumulated this a@rtava causes development of kuksi (uterus). Fasting during rtukala,
fear, use of dry dietetics and mode of life, suppression of natural urges, use of stambhaka
(causing cessation of bleeding per vaginum) and lekhana {causing medicinal curettage
of uterus) drugs and yonidosa (gynecological disorders) also are causative factors for
raktagulma.

Suéruta has held responsible only use of improper diet during ytukala, after abortion
or delivery as a causative factor. है

VagbhataI says that the woman who uses vata aggravating diet, her artava getting
admixed with excreted Sukra but with absence of jivatama or sometimes even without Sukra
gets accumulated, increases and gives clinical features of pregnancy, this entity is gulma.
Further both the Vagbhatas have mentioned use of vata-vitiating diet following delivery,
during yonirogas and rtukala. as etiology of raktagulma.

Kasyapa giving detailed account of etiology says that the woman who has had abnor-
mal labour, is carrying Gmagarbha (pregnancy of early first trimester), has had abortion,
indulges in excessive coitus, is over anxious to become pregnant, has excessively cold
Grtava (menstruation), suffers from udavarta, if uses diet or mode of life capable of viti-
ating vata, then her vayu gets aggravated. When the woman due to shyness, fear or being
engaged in coitus suppresses her urge of defecation, urination or passing of flatus then also
her vayw gets aggravated. If the woman who has had abortion due to abnormality of vayu
and further uses improper mode of life and diet then also her vayu gets vitiated. This
aggravated vayu withholding rakta, moving upwards, entering yoni, reaches the srotasa or
garbhaSaya (uterus). There it settles down with rakta or Grtava inside the uterus, thus. the

appear. These are—colic, stiffness of body, burning sensation, diarrhoea, thirst and fever,
Due to retention of abnormal or vitiated artava the woman suffers from severe pain in
uterus, continuous but scanty vaginal discharges specially foul smelling and severe pain
specially of pricking type in vagina, quivering is of solid mass, delayed, occasional and with

Kasyapa opines that due to association of vayu there is excessive quivering in gulma.
The woman suffers from indigestion, anaemia, emaciation, cough, colic, fever and diar-
thoea. She feels as if all the body parts are numb and heavy and she is entering in dark.
She suffers from excessive vomiting, does not feel taste of food, glands appear over the
abdomen, breasts and umbilical region and romaraji appears blue. She becomes uncon-
scious. Her lips and areola become black, milk appears in breasts. gets dohrda. She desires
articles of various tastes, spits repeatedly and gets agitated with good smells. Her complex-
ion becomes better and she gets all the clinical features of pregnancy. Considering her seif
pregnant carries the disease for years together with great agony. Some times due to time
factor if gulma is expelled, then due to absence of fetal parts women call it divya garbha
(divine fetus) or say that fetus is taken away by bhiitas.

Bhela has followed Kasyapa and Madhavanidana, Bhavaprakasa and Yogaratnakara
have followed Caraka, however, these authors have given very short description.

In the commentary of Madhukosa and Bhawaprakaéa it is explained that all the clinical
features i.e. amenorrhoea, yellowishness of face, watering of mouth, blackening of areola
and dauhrda etc. are present in the raktagulma or the gulma developing due to a type of
rakta i.e. Grtava. The presence of these clinical features is due to specific nature of disease

in the same way as sexual desire in tuberculosis and dark colouration of skin and nails etc.
in piles are seen.

fetus, however, due to resemblance with fetus and psychological feeling of being pregnant,
the woman behaves as if pregnant. Dalhana says that presence of clinical features simulating
pregnancy is specific character of the disease. :

गर्भ-व्यापद्‌ 02

Though bad prognostic sign/symptoms specially for raktagulma have not been de-
scribed, however, features of incurability mentioned for gulma in general can be considered
for raktagulma also. These are—

Gradually accumulating gu/ma involving larger area, solid, having deep seated roots,
covered with net of vessels, having protuberance like tortoise, and associated with weak-
ness, anorexia, nausea, cough, vomiting, uneasiness, fever, thirst, drowsiness, hiccough,
flatulence, pain, coryza, dyspnoea, diarrhoea and cdema is incurable. The patient of gulma
already having fever, dyspnoea, vomiting and diarrhoea if develops edema over cardiac and
umbilical region and also on extremities, then the patient dies.

आचार्य भावमितश्र, माधव एवं योगरलाकरकार ने भी दशम मास के पश्चात्‌ ही चिकित्सा का विधान बताया है. टीका
में स्पष्टीकरण चक्रपाणि की ही भाँति दिया है कि दश मास के पश्चात्‌ चिकित्सा गर्भ-शंका के कारण न होकर सुखसाध्यता
की दृष्टि से वर्णित है, क्योंकि दश मास के पूर्व रक्तगुल्म की लीनता के कारण गर्भाशय-आघात आदि होने की सम्भावना

अधिक होती है ।
Treatment of raktagulma should be done after tenth month of its onset or after the
period of normal labour has elapsed. Cakrapani has clarified that tenth month period has

been said as it is easily curable after this period. If treatment ig attempted before tenth

month, excessive bleeding and injury to the uterus etc. complications are likely to occur.
The idea that after tenth month gulma will also automatically get expelled just like fetus is
not correct, because sometimes fetus stays in uterus for years together and gulma is expelled
before tenth month. Dalhana opines that presence of identical dosas and dusyas in fever and
prameha respectively and chronicity in raktagulma are the features for easy curability,
however, if proper localization of raktagulma occurs it can be treated even before tenth
month. Indu says that tenth month period is advised for differentiating it from the fetus.

Kaéyapa has written that as the fruit gets ripened in its appropriate time, similarly
gulma attains maturity in ten months and then it is easily curable and gets expelled easily,
however before this period the treatment is a bit difficult.

ii) To suppress vata, oleation, sudation and carminatives should be used. Sudation

vii) To relieve the pain kalyGnaka, paficagavya, satpala or tiktaka ghrta should be
prescribed on the basis of specific dosa.

जा) Meat soup of wild animals or birds medicated with decoction of bilva and Syonaka
should be given for loosening the raktagulma.

ix) To mobilize the gudma and for purgation trivrt or triphala mixed with soup of
kulattha or meat of quail should be given.

x) Once the gudma is mobilized, then for cleansing and expelling it, powders of haritakt,
vaca, hingu, rock salt, amlavetasa, yawani and yawaksara should be prescribed with
hot water.

xi) Methodical use of haritaki, yawaksdra, and sauva,cala salt with ghrta expells the
gulma.
xii) Either powdered patra, ela, pippali and sunthi mixed with vid salt or powders of
nagara with bhasma of Sukti should be prescribed with cow’s urine.
xili) Pestled small variety of ela, kufcika, cavya, pippali and citraka either mixed with
juice of balvaja or water prepared with scum of boiled rice should be given.
xiv) Medicines prescribed for expelling the placenta can be used.

xv) Padma etc. plants along with their roots should be burnt, and decoction of this ash
should be prepared. When the decoction gets thickened, powders of Suntht, pippali,
kustha, cavya, citraka and daru should be mixed in it and boiled till the substance
is so thick that it gets adhered in the ladle. Use of this electuary expells the guima.

xvi) Use of silajita and abhayarista as a kalpa is also beneficial in raktagulma.

xvii) Decoction of lodhra, arjuna, khadira, magadhika, samanga mixed with amlavetasa,
honey and sugar cures immediately raktagulma, hytkleda (nausea) and rakta-dosas
(blood disorders).

xviii) Milk mixed with ghrta and sauvarcala salt should be prescribed in raktagulma,
yakrta (liver) and ksataja (traumatic) disorders.

xix) Pestled Satahwa, stem bark of cirabilva, daru, bharngi and kand mixed with decoc-
tion of tila should be prescribed.

xx) Use of juice of dhatri mixed with powder of marica cures raktagulma.

xxi) To eradicate dosas of the woman suffering from raktagulma powders of gundra or
mundi and rocanikaé mixed with honey and sugar should be prescribed.

xxii) Yawaksara mixed with powder of tryiisana and ghrta should be prescribed.

xxiii) Use of powders of root of tila, stem bark of Sigru, root of brahmadandi, madhuyasfi
and trikatu is beneficial to the woman suffering from amenorrhoea and vatagulma.

xxiv) Powdered root of danti, hingu, yawaksdra, seeds of alabu and pippali mixed with
jaggery should be triturated with latex of snuht and tablets should be made. Use
of these tablets in the dose of one karsa cures raktagulma and initiates bleeding
per vaginum.

करता है।

Literally word gulma means clump or cluster or bush. It arises due to aggravation of
vayu, which either alone or in association with other dosas gets accumulated in respective
locations of dosas or at some other place. Location of gulma is in between Ardaya (heart)
and basti (urinary bladder). It has shape of a granthi (gland), is mobile or immobile,
increases or decreases in size and is circular in appearance.

Just like bush its root or base is hidden and. the size is big. Dalhana opines that
sometimes gulma increases and then decreases in size and sometimes initially gets stabi-
lized and then increases in size. Gulma either does not get suppurated or very rarely
suppurates because the dosas get accumulated in their own normal or physiological places.

Considering raktagulma in the perspective of above mentioned description of general
gulma, it appears that raktagulma occurs in the uterus (as the place of rakta as well as
specific location is uterus) due to accumulation of rakta. It is circular or just like bush in
shape, is spreaded or involves larger area, decreases in size after initial increase and occurs
only in the woman of middle age having normal menstrual cycle. Etiopathogenesis of
raktagulma is different from other gulmas.

गर्भ-व्यापद्‌ ves

Haematometra arises due to imperforated hymen, complete stenosis of vaginal canal
or cervix uteri, In these conditions question of woman being rtumari (menstruating) or

having recently undergone a labour does not arise. Haematometra requires surgical treat-
ment not the medical.

Ovarian tumours are usually not associated with amenorrhoea, however, bilateral
tumours involving entire ovarian tissue can cause amenorrhoca. The ovarian tumours are not
situated within the uterus, can not be treated medicinally and can not be got expelled
vaginally, moreover ovarian tumours are not caused due to abnormality or collection of
menstrual blood while raktagulma develops due to accumulation of unexcreted rakta i.e,
menstrual blood.

Fibromyomas or other uterine tumours are usually associated with menorrhagia rather
than amenorihoea, moreover, these are made up of muscle-fibres with fibrous tissues not
of blood, and can not be treated medicinally.

Tendency of spontaneous vaginal expulsion is not seen in tumours.

All the three diseases mentioned above require surgical treatment, medicinal treatment
has no place, while raktagulma is mainly treated with oral or local medicines.

Considering all the points none of the above mentioned three disorders can be simu-
lated with raktagulma and some other congruence has to be attempted.

Normally all those conditions arising after menstruation, labour, uterine curettage or
other yonirogas (gynec disorders), having cardinal symptom as amenorthoea in association
with fever, diarrhoea, colic, cough, and dyspnoea etc. can be considered under rakiagulma.
Most important condition of this category is acute infective or inflammatory disorders of
uterus (pyometra) and its 40700, Due to acute inflammation of endometrium there may be
amenorthoea (as seen in pyometra), the pelvic congestion may produce diarrhoea due to
hyper-stimulation of bowels. The existing infection can produce fever, cough, dyspnoea and
parenteral diarrhoea along with foul smelling vaginal discharges. Amenorrhoea associated
with any acute disorder is transitory and will riot give the symptoms of pregnancy. The
treatment has to be given for actual disease and not to expell the gulma or in other words
the condition does not simulate raktagulma.

Chronic tuberculosis is associated with fever, diarrhoea etc. and due to weakness and
emaciation there may be amenorthoea. Due to chronic nature of disease this amenorrhoea
can produce the symptoms of pregnancy or pseudocyesis and treatment may also had to be
given to induce menstruation. Thus this condition resembles to certain extent with
raktagulma, however, in this condition the blood is not accumulated in uterus, rather it is
not formed at all. The accumulation of blood is basic criteria for diagnosis of raktagulma.
As nothing is accumulated in the uterus, so the physician will not find enlargement of uterus
and will not consider it as raktagulma.

Due to presence of amenorrhoea, suspicion of pregnancy, period of treatment and
medicines prescribed for its expulsion; molar pregnancy seems to resemble raktagulma. In

## Scanned page 237

आयुर्वेदीय प्रसूतितन्त्र एवं स्त्री रोग

SS

molar pregnancy there is initial amenorrhoea and presence of all the clinical features of
pregnancy followed by recurrent bleeding per vaginum. Due to association of infection, the
fever, cough and foul smelling vaginal discharges can be seen. The product of conception
assumes shape of rounded mass or bunch of grapes in carneous or hydatiform mole respec-
lively. The trace of exact fetus is rarely found.

Probably due to findings of both types of mole i.e. with evident fetus or fetal parts and
without evident fetus or fetal parts Vagbhata expounded the theory of drtava accumulating
छत fukra (with fetus) or without Sukra (without fetus). Principle of treatment of molar
pregnancy is to get it expelled. In carneous mole uterus decreases in size after initial
increase which is described by Susruta as caya (accumulation) followed by apacaya (de-
crease).

Taking into account etiopathogenesis and clinical features of raktagulma, all the local
(relating to reproductive system) and general conditions described in modern medicines
giving rise to amenorrhoea can be considered under raktagulma. However, raktagulma seem

- to be specifically analogous to-molar pregnancy. Initial increase followed by decrease hint
towards carneous mole; while hidden root, excessive enlargement and association of severe
nausea and vomiting etc. towards hydatiform mole. Due to its hidden roct some times
complete expulsion does not take place and recurrence of bleeding or reappearance of
vesicles is noted. It may get changed into malignancy and give symptoms described for,

incurable gulma.

८. एननसेफैलि पीड़ित गर्भ के दीर्घकालीन गर्भाशयान्तर are की स्थिति का भी सामान्य ग्रसव-काल गणना में हो
समावेश |

Minimum and maximum duration of gestation considered as normal for labour in
Gyurvedika classics is not acceptable to-day, because the delivery in the beginning of ninth
month is termed as premature and after second week of tenth month as postmature. How-
ever, in exceptional cases intrauterine stay of normal fetus (after probable date of cohabi-
tation) for 331, 349, and 360 days and of alive but anencephalic fetus for no less than 389

days has been mentioned in operative obstetrics.' This difference might have appeared due
to following reasons:—

. Pregnancy occurring during lactational amenorrhoea or other secondary amenor-
rhoeas resulting in ignorance about exact month of impregnation.

ii. Prolongation of normal menstrual cycle:— Some times without any specific ab-
normality menstrual cycle is prolonged for 45-60 or 90 days etc. Ovulation
occures mostly 14-15 days prior to the onset of menstruation. If conception
occures in such cycle the gestational period may appear to be prolonged beyond
a normal limit.

iii.

Miscalculation of amenorrhoea period: Few women count month of last men-
strual period as first month of pregnancy, for example a woman having her last
menstruation in February will count Feb. as first month of pregnancy and March
as second. This results in difference of one month in duration of gestation.

iv. Lunar months are not of thirty days rather usually of twentyeight days, thus 280-
287 days described for normal labour cover the period of ten months or more, not
of only nine calender months + 7 days.

ए. More than one factor described above operating together may give false impres-
sion of normal labour occurring in eleventh or twelfth month,
vi. There are great individual variations in duration of normal gestation.
vii. Consideration of exceptions under general rule.

viii. Consideration of prolong intrauterine stay of anencephalic fetus under normal
duration of labour.

I, Operative Obstetrics by Munro Kerr, Page 620, 621.

५- काल-प्रकर्ष-मर्भावस्‍था के एक निश्चित काल के पश्चात्‌ ही शरीर में प्रसवोपयोगी परिवर्तन होते हैं यथा

गर्भाशयोत्तेजना में सहायक होता है | गर्भाशय-मांसपेशी में ऑक्टोमायोसिन अपनी अधिकतम सीमा में एकत्रित

कर देता है आदि। यह सभी परिवर्तन काल पर ही आधारित होते हैं।

Detachment of nddi-nibandha, swabhava (nature), indifference of fetus from intra-
uterine stay, full maturity of fetal parts and time factor are the five causes enlisted as
responsible for labour. All these can be explained in the following way:—

i. Detachment of nadi-nibandha—Nadi word denotes sensory or motor nerve fibres
and umbilical cord. Release or detachment of nibandha means release of obstruc-

tion in their normal functions or detachment of attachments situated between nadi
and maternal body or uterus.

Pitocinase enzyme inhibits the action of pitocin during pregnancy or this enzyme
inhibits the myometrial stimulation, a normai function of motor fibres of nerves. Few days
preceding labour this pitocinase disappears allowing the pitocin to act, thus motor fibres of

nerves stimulate myometrium, or in other words obstruction in function of nerves (nddz) is
released.

The umbilical cord derives its nourishment from placenta, to which it is attached. As
the term approaches infarcts appear-at maternal side of placenta which hamper free flow of
oxygen causing anoxia to the fetus, a cause of labour. In other words attachments situated
inbetween umbilical cord (rasavahanadi) or placenta and maternal body or uterus are de-
tached which initiate labour.

ii. Swabhava (Nature)—Unknown cause.

iti. Garbha-vasa vairagya (Indifference of the fetus from its intra-uterine stay)—Changes
in the fetus caused due to anoxia, and its hormones initiate labour.

iv. Garbha sampirnata (Full maturity of feta! parts) :—Generally above mentioned fac-

tors operate together only when the fetus is mature and then delivery of full term
fetus occurs.

vy. Kala prakarsa (Time factor)—After a specific period of gestation, changes necessary
for labour occur in the body, such as estrogen inactivated due to conjugation be-
comes free and sensitizes myometrium for the action of pitocin, thus helps in
myometrial stimulation. Actomyocine also gets optimum deposition and starts 005
traction of myometrial fibres. Uterus attaining its maximum distension starts con-
traction. All these changes occur after a specified period.

An abode for expectant woman should be constructed before ninth month of pregnancy
on a land free from stone, sand or gravel and pieces of broken earthen pots (either already
absent or removed before construction), and having excellent appearance, rasa (taste i. e.
land should not be salty etc.) and smell (not having foul smell etc.). The house should face
east or north and be constructed with the wood of any tree out of bilva, tinduka, inguda,
bhallataka, varuna or khadira or with any other wood advised by brahmanas or the persons
having knowledge of atharvaveda. The house should be well clothed, smeared with cow
dung or lime, covered or roofed (with roof of wooden frame) and curtained or having well

विमर्श (Comments)

सभी आचार्यों ने नवम मास के पूर्व ही यूतिकागार के निर्काण की व्यवस्था दी है जिससे यह प्रतीत होता है कि
सम्भवत: प्रत्येक प्रसव के लिए नवीन सूतिकागार का मनिर्माण होता था। काष्ट से सूतिकागार-निर्माण के तीन कारण हो
सकते हैं (१) आसानी से उपलब्धि (२) उल्कापात से सुरक्षा; क्योंकि काष्ठ में उल्का का प्रभाव नहीं होता (३) कार्य
हो जाने पर हटाने में सुविधा । महर्षि सुश्रुत के अतिरिक्त सभी ने इसका द्वर पूर्व या उत्तर की ओर रखने का निर्देश दिया
है जो सम्भवत्त: प्रातःकाल में सूर्य-रश्मि के sae एवं मध्यान्ह के उपतप्त सूर्य कौ किरणों के प्रवेश-निषेघ की दृष्टि से
वर्णित है। सम्भवतः महर्षि सुश्रुत ने मध्यान्ह को सूर्ब-रश्मि के प्रवेश को उचित समझकर एवं वायु आदि के समुचित
प्रवेश की दृष्टि से दक्षिण की ओर द्वार रखने का निर्देश किया हैं। महर्षि सुश्रुत एवं भावमिश्र वर्णित आयाम अत्यधिक
न्यून प्रतीत होता है, सम्भवत: वह आयाम केवल प्रसव कराने के लिए निर्मित कक्ष का हो न कि सूतिका के रहने के
लिए,। महर्षि सुश्रुत-वर्णित जाति-भेद से काष्ठ-भिन्नता का समुचित स्पष्टीकरण कठिन है सम्भवत्त: यह शरीर के वर्ण की
दृष्टि से अथवा सूतिकागार-निर्माण में प्रयुक्त HB के वर्ण को देखकर प्रसूता स्त्री की जाति के ज्ञानार्थ उल्लिखित हो।

As construction of house has been advised before or during ninth month of pregnancy,
thus it appears that a new accouchement room/ward was constructed for every parturient
woman. Construction with wood might have been advised due to three reasons 1.6. easy
availability, protection from thunder-bolt because the wood is bad conductor of electricity
and easy to dismantle after completion of its purpose. The house facing to the east will have
easy access to wind and rays of rising sun, while facing to the north will prevent entry of
rays of mid-day hot sun, probably Suéruta might have preferred the entry of rays of mid-
day sun and also good air, thus he advised the door of the house to be on south instead of
north. The dimensions described by Suéruta seem to be too small for a ward, however, these
might be referring to-the labour room not to the ward.

[- भूवतत्कालोचितव्यवहारकुशलाभि: स्त्रीभि: परिवारिता ॥
१. सूतिकापरिवारिता-अनेकबारप्रसवानु' (अ० go शा० tase को अरुणदत्त टीका)

प्रमव-विज्ञानीय ४३३

After beginning of ninth month, on some auspicious day, when moon situated in
highest place has association of other benefical planets, then during maitra period pacifying
oblation should be offered. Now the cows, brahmanas along with fire and water should he
made to enter the ward. The pregnant woman should offer grass, water, honey and parched
paddy to the cows, should wash hands and feet of seated brahmanas, offer them washed
rice, flowers and nandimukha ({ruit (the fruits used in nandimukha rites or kharjura etc.
fruits) and reverential salutation, then she should’ sip the water and take blessings for
welfare. Now the pregnant woman should enter the labour ward by keeping her right foot
first and following cows and brahmanas reciting holy words (fig. 7). She should stay there
and wait for onset of labour.

Vagbhata 1 says that the pregnant woman should enter labour ward during favourable
naksatras, having enchantation of auspicious words, after reverential salutation to cow,
brahmanas and elders, be in constant association of women having qualities described
earlier. She should remain busy in auspicious virtues and use such dietetics which facilitate
proper excretion of flatus, urine and feces. In cases of constipation or retention of urine
phalavarti should be used.

SuSruta and Vagbhata II have given similar but very short description.
विमर्श (Comments)

महर्षि वाग्भट ने सूतिकागार में प्रवेश का कोई निश्चित काल नहीं बताया उन्होंने नवम मास के पूर्व ही सूत्तिकागार
निर्माण की व्यवस्था बताई है जिससे स्पष्ट होता है कि नवम मास के आने पर उससमें स्त्री का प्रवेश कराया जाय । महर्षि
चरक ने स्त्री के प्रवेश के पूर्व गौ एवं ब्राह्मण के प्रवेश का विधान दिया है जो संभवत: उस काल में प्रचलित सामाजिक
संस्कारों के कारण हो । यह भी संभव है कि पूर्व हो निर्मित सूतिकागार में उसके सामान्य जनपद से दूर होने के कारण
कोई अवांछित वायु या जीव प्रविष्ट कर गया हो अतः गर्भिणी का प्रथम प्रवेश निषिद्ध किया गया तथा ब्राह्मण एवं गौ
को आगे प्रवेश कराके अनुगमन कराना ही सुरक्षित समझा गया हो। *

सूतिकागार में निवास के दो लाभ हो सकते हैं (१) स्त्री का सामान्य जन-सम्पर्क से दूर रहने के कारण किसी
भी औपसर्गिक व्याधि के उपसर्ग से सुरक्षित रहना।

(२) मानसिक रूप से प्रसब-वेदना सहन करने के लिए तैयार होना, क्योंकि यह प्रमाणित तथ्य है कि स्त्री की
मानसिक अवस्था का प्रसब-वेदनाओं में अत्यधिक प्रभाव पड़ता है।

Though Vagbhata has not mentioned specific period for entry in labour ward, however,
he has also accepted its construction before ninth month, others have clearly mentioned stay
in labour ward from ninth month of pregnancy. Entry of cow and brahmanas described by
Caraka might have been given due to social customs prevailing at that time. The labour
ward was constructed at a distant place from normal village / city where-in likelyhood of
entry of some harmful or unwanted animals or gases can not be ruled out, these can injure
the pregnant woman. Initial entry of cow and brahmanas will avoid this risk.

Stay in labour ward may prevent the contact of infections since the pregnant woman
will be seggregated, besides it may also prepare woman psychologically to withstand the
labour pains.

होने से fr पहिले उत्पन्न होता है ।

At the onset of labour the head of the fetus gets turned and comes forward due to
action of prasiiti-maruta and then is expelled through vaginal passage: this is normalcy,
other situations are abnormal. For this natural phenomena deeds of previous life are held
responsible by Dalhana. After delivery of fetus placenta getting detached from maternal
heart comes out. After delivery the fetus becomes independent for its nourishment. Indu
says that fetus situated facing back of the mother gets turned and then facing umbilicus and

keeping head at the fowest is delivered. Bhela says that fetal part positioned in the front (at
the pelvic brim) delivers first. Punarvasu Atreya opines that head being heaviest comes first.

In normal intrauterine situation of fetus Caraka has described upward position of head,
while others not specifying Position of head have accepted universely flexed attitude. How-
ever, all of them agree that head position / delivery is normal. Head usually attains down-
ward situation in the last trimester of Pregnancy, however, in exceptional cases it does rotate
Just prior to.labour. Since more than 95% deliveries occur in head position, thus all the
classics have mentioned this normal situation.

With the word “parivrtya” or rotation actually internal rotation occuring during labour
should be considered. In this context head Tefers to vertex, because face, brow etc. have
been mentioned under obstructed tabour, thus the description should be considered as for-

ward position of vertex obtained by internal rotation; which is corroborated by the clinical
feature after parivartana of garbh.

there are no structural attachments between chest/heart and uterus/fetus. It appears that —
feeling of relief from compression of chest due to descend of fetus in the pelvic cavity has
been mentioned as release of bonds. Increase in frequency of defecation and micturition and
pain alongwith compression etc. are the clinical features of further descend of fetus. Caraka, ~
Vagbhata and Kasyapa have described ‘parivartana’ of fetus which has already been dis-
