बताया है ।
After onset of labour pains, the woman should be made to sit on a soft cushion
spreaded over the ground, The women having qualities described earlier and experienced in
conducting the labour should encircle and encourage her by consoling and pleasant words.

Suéruta says that the woman for whom auspicious hymns for her welfare and prosperity
have already been recited and is ready to deliver, should be encircled by kwmdaras (male
children) and hold the fruit bearing masculine name. She should be given massage (with oil),
bath with lukewarm water and made to drink good, strength producing tice gruel, filling her
stomach to its fullest capacity. Now the woman should steep in supine position with flexed
thighs on a soft bed having pillow and be attended by undaunted, mature and expert four
women having their nails trimmed.

Vagbhata giving the description like Susruta has not advised presence of kumaras.
Besides he has specified the hymn as “kautuka-mangala” and the bed that a soft cushion
should be spreaded over the ground and be covered with skin of red bull. The women
attending her should wear intact clothes. The delivering woman should be given repeatedly
inhalation of powdered kustha, ela, langali, vaca, cavy4, citraka and cirabilva (any one or
all together) ot intermittent inhalation of smoke of bhurjapatra, leaves of SimSipa and
sarjarasa. Indu opines that inhalation should be given during inter-contraction period. Gentle
massage with lukewarm oil over flanks, back, sacrum and thighs should be done. This
procedure brings the fetus down.

Vagbhata IT has advised the massage over infraumbilical region of the delivering
woman and repeated yawning and slow walking by her. Arunadatta has explained that oil
js massaged to avoid aggravation of vata and has advised its continuation till expulsion of

fetus.

Kagyapa has written that after observing the clinical features of onset of labour, senior
experienced women after taking bath, and having recitation of words for welfare by
brahmanas should enter the labour ward. These sweet speaking women, urging prajapati for
economic and religious achievements, should console, encourage and delight the pregnant
woman, natrate to her the pleasures of children and sorrows of childless couple. They should
pray aditi, kaSyapa, deva, indrani, indra, agwinikumiras and auspicious gods who have
number of children and long life. The woman anxious to deliver should remain happy, free

_ from shyness and sitting encircled with old women and money should attempt for delivery.
He has also advised use of meat soup during this period.

अन्य aaa पीने को दें। यदि इस विधि से प्रवर्तन न हो तो तीक्ष्ण तैल से अनुवासन दे ।

If the woman, inspite of having labour pains does not deliver, then she should be asked

to get up and holding a pestle or any other heavy thing should strike the paddy filled in .

mortar, should yawn repeatedly and walk inbetween, is the opinion of few. Atreya contra-
dicting this says that heavy exercise is always contraindicated to a pregnant woman; spe-
cially during delivery, because at this time all the dosas and dhdatus of body are moving or
are excited, thus the vdyu of delicate woman getting excited due to exercise with pestie etc,
enters the hallow spaces of the body and kills her. The treatment of woman at this stage is
very difficult, considering this the use of pestle etc. is contraindicated, however, yawning
and walking is beneficial. Inhalation of powderd kustha, ela, langali, vaca, citraka,
cirabilva and cavya or smoke of bhurjapatra or resin of Simsipad should be given; in-
between massage with Jukewarm oil over waist, flanks, back and thighs, then. gentle knead-
ing should be done. By this process the fetus descends downwards.

_ SuSruta says that fetus having gone to opposite or wrong direction should be brought
to right direction and the one which is straight should be pulled or extracted. Dalhana has
explained that this is just a hint for the management of obstructed labour.

Vagbhata I has expressed almost identical opinion as given by Caraka.

Kasyapa expressing opinion about different exercises just like Caraka explains that
besides displaced dosas and dhdtus, the woman has predominance of kleda (humidity) also,
thus is more vulnerable for diseases and sorrows. Other women observing her agony remark
that her one foot is in the house of yama (the god of death) and other on this side (i.e. she
can die at any,moment). Any exercise can kill the pregnant woman immediately, even
excessive walking can kill the delivering fetus and produce several fatal disorders. He has
also advised inhalations, (instead of SimSipa he has written nameru and guggulu) and oil
massage etc. Few authors advise use of wine for weak women, however, Kasyapa has
contradicted this and advised use of rice gruel to quench the thirst.

Bhela says that one aksa boiled red sali rice mixed with sour drinks and (cow) urine
should be given or else this rice should be given with decoction of danti, dravanti, vrscikal,
punarnava and banatiktaka, Gruel made with old Sali rice is also prescribed. If fetus does
not descend with this, then anuvasana basti with pungent oil should be given.

The accoucheuse or female attendants should educate the woman “do not bear down
in the absence of labour pains, because it would be useless (in terms of progress of labour).
One who does it, her child becomes abnormal, deformed or afflicted with dyspnoea, cough,
emaciation and diseases of spleen. In the absence of natural urge inspite of best efforts as
one either does not get or gets with difficulty sneezing, eructation, flatus, urine and feces,
similarly bearing down efforts made in the absence of labour pains do not bring the fetus

: down. As suppression of sneezing etc. natural urges is harmful, similarly absence of efforts
to bear down during labour pains is also harmful”. Considering this the woman should bear
down as instructed by accoucheuse. Initially (early second stage) the bearing down efforts
should be mild, but should be forceful at the end. At the moment of this bearing down the

attendants should pronounce “delivered, delivered, you are fortunate, fortunate, you have

delivered a male child.” Hearing these words the woman gets strength due to happiness.
in the absence of labour pains. When the

Suésuta and Vagbhata have prescribed certain drugs for the treatment of garbhasanga
without elaborating its clinical features. The word garbhasanga denotes attachment of fetus
ot cessation in the progress of labour. Books Yogaratnakara and Bhavaprakasa have not
used the term garbhasanga, but have prescribed certain drugs for the treatment of “delay
in labour”. Since both the conditions are actually the same, hence all the prescriptions are
recaptulated at on place.

Vitiated vayu located in Sukra is also said to cause saga or delay in labour.

The position of parturient woman ie. supine with flexed thighs described in

dywrvedika classics resembles with Sim’s position used today. Though Caraka has advised
initial squatting position, however, before delivery the woman was made to lic down.

During first stage sitting or walking is beneficial in bringing down the fetus and also in
‘agbhata’s description of

distracting her attention from the labour pains. Caraka’s and Vi

conduction of labour on the bed is a better procedure than Suétuta’s description of conduc-
tion of labour on floor. Why Kaégyapa has advised squatting position is difficult to explain,
because by that time lying position was prevalent. Use of skin over the bed by Vagbhata
is probably first description of mackintosh.

Holding fruits bearing masculine names by the woman at the beginning of labour
pains, initial encirclement by male adolescents etc. hint towards the social condition prevail-
ing at that time, where-in male children were more wanted. Pronouncement of delivery of
a male child and other encouragements to bear down were probably used to boost the
morale of parturient woman, because it is established fact that psychology of woman plays
very important role during labour.

Drugs prescribed by Caraka to bring down the fetus (which has failed to come down
inspite of presence of labour pains) probably stimulate the uterine musculature and improve
the expulsive efforts, however, their routine use described by Vagbhata is not justified,
because over-stimulation to normally functioning uterine muscles can cause certain compli-
cations. As explained earlier that descend of fetus is indicative of second stage of labour,
the treatment prescribed by Caraka before the descend of fetus is to stimulate the uterus in
the beginning of second stage. Garbhasanga (uterine inertia) described by Susruta etc. is an
abnormality of second stage of labour, however, since Vagbhata has described garbhasanga

१) उदरगुहान्तर्गत भार-वृद्धि करा कर (By increasing intra abdominal pressure)

वेणी से कण्ठ-स्पर्श (द्वारा उत्पन्न कास), स्फिगू दबाना आदि वाह्य उपचार इस वर्ग के अन्दर आते हैं ।

Touching of palate or throat with braid of hair or finger wrapped with hair may
produce instantaneous cough thus may suddenly increase intraabdominal pressure. Similarly
compression of hips and/or violent jerks may also increase intraabdominal pressure and help
in expulsion of placenta.

२) गर्भाशय को संपीडन करके (By compressing the uterus)

सुश्रुतोक्त अंसपिण्डिका का सम्पीडन यदि अंश्नपिण्डिकावत्‌ सम्पीडन माना जाय तो यह आधनिक पुस्तकों में वर्णित
ieee विधि ही प्रतीत होता है क्योंकि अंसपिण्डिका को पकड़ने में हाथ की चारों अँगुलियाँ एक ओर तथा अँगूठा दूसरी
ओर रहेगा क्रेड्ज विधि में इसी प्रकार गर्भाशय को पकड़कर दबाया जाता है। नाभि के ऊपर दबाव भो गर्भाशय को
संपीडित कर अपरा-पातन में सहायक होगा ।

Compression of uterus after holding it just like shoulder resembles to certain extent the
Crede’s method because while holding the shoulder one has to keep four fingers on one side
and thumb on the other and then compression is given; similarly pressure over umbilicus
will alsc compress the uterus.

3) गर्भाशय मांसपेशी-संकोच बढ़ाकर (By increasing myometrial contractions)

योनि-धूपन, fry, विभिन्न बस्तियाँ तथा आभ्यन्तर प्रयुक्त औषधियाँ इस वर्ग में आती हैं । शिर में अवसेचन एवं
हाथ पैर आदि में आलेपित औषधियों की क्रिया-विधि के बारे में निश्चित स्पष्टीकरण कठिन है, परन्तु यह सम्मव है कि
किसी प्रत्यावर्तित क्रिया द्वारा अथवा मानसिक प्रभाव के कारण हाइपॉथलमस के मार्ग से पश्चिम पीयूषग्रन्थि के स्राव का
निष्क्रमण होकर अपश-पातन होता हो। उदर में आलेपित औषधियाँ सम्भवतः sax की पेशियों की क्रियाशीलता बढ़ाकर
एवं उदरणुहान्तर्गत भार-वृद्धि कर अथवा प्रत्यावर्तित क्रिया द्वात्त अपरा-पातन में सहायक होती हों ।

Vaginal fumigations, anointments, tampons, all basties and oral medicines come under
this group. It is difficult to explain mode of action of the drugs used as an irrigation over
the head or anointment over palm or sole, however, it is just possible that either by some
reflex action or through psychological effect these might be influencing posterior pituitary
via hypothalamus and increase the secretion of posterior pituitary which stimulates
myometrium. The drugs applied over abdomen may increase intraabdominal pressure and
may also reflexly stimulate the uterus.

When all the drugs/methods fail the placenta is removed manually.

## Scanned page 260

४६८ आयुर्वेदोय प्रसूतितन्त्र एवं eit

ii) Upto sixth month the expulsion of fetus is called garbhapata. Exact term to be
used for delivery of the fetus in seventh month (having all the body parts) has not been
given in any of the classic, commentators Arunadatta and Vijayaraksita have attempted to
explain this in following way :—

a) Explaining development of fetus during seventh month Arunadatta has mentioned

that in this month fetus attains development of all body parts and capability to survive.
Though the child born in this month does survive, however, due to akala-prasava (delivery
in improper time) it does not possess longevity etc. characteristics as seen in full term
delivered child. If the child born prematurely in this month (@ka@la-prasava) was definitely
not to survive then specific mention of death of fetus born during eighth month was su-
perfluous. This indicates that the child born in seventh month does survive.
: (b) Vijayaraksita and Srikanthadatta in their Madhukosa commentary have elaborated
that description of garbhapata in fifth and sixth months has been specifically given to high-
light the survivality of child born in seventh months. [f delivery in seventh month takes
place normally (normal labour) without any abnormality (diseases of the mother or fetus)
or birth is enuguna then the born child survives, however, if delivery has occured due to
some abnormality (viguna) then the child does not survive and delivery in this month also
may be called as garbhapata. Since the delivery in seventh month occurs due to abnormality
of dosas hence it is called “viprasava”.

iii) Caraka has mentioned that abnormalities of factors responsible for normal devel-
opment cause intrauterine death of the fetus or it ends in acirajata. This has been explained
by Cakrapani that if amount of vitiation of dosas is less then it ends in acirajata. Taking
the literal meaning of word acira (early) jdta (born) it can be considered as reference for
premature labour. .

iv) Complications of delivery in eighth month have already been discussed earlier,
which is a clear reference of premature labour.

v) Harita has referred that due to abnormalities of dosas specially propelled by vayu
the delivery may take place before completing full term. Thus born child is weak.

vi) Caraka says that for normal full term delivery normalcy of sukra, drtava,
Gtmakarma, asaya, kala and diet along with mode of life of mother is esséntial. This implies
that abnormality of either of these factors can cause premature labour.

vii) SuSruta has mentioned that treatment of disorders of apaprajata woman should
be done on the lines of any normal individual. Dalhana has explained the word apaprajata
ie. akalaprasuta or delivered in abnormal time, which can also be considered as premature

labour.
viii) Aggravated vayu located in Sukra is said to cause premature expulsion of fetus.

This garbhagalya (dead fetus acting as extraneous substance lodged in the body and
giving it very great pain) should be treated either with suppressive measures alongwith the
methods prescribed for the treatment of retained placenta or with the use of hymns men-
tioned in atharvaveda ot should be extracted by an experienced surgeon. Cakrapani has
clarified that since proper extraction of the fetus with either of the methods is difficult,
hence these different opinions have been given. At another place Caraka has cited
garbhasalya as an example of Salyas to be treated by extraction.

After extraction of falya or expulsion of ama (immature) fetus, for cleansing the uterus
and alleviation of pain along with elevation of her mood the woman should be prescribed
sura, sidhu, arista, madhu (a type of wine), madira and Gsava or other alcoholic drinks
according to her-strength. After this to protect ‘her strength she should be given fat free,
anabolic or satiating rice gruel and appropriate diet beneficial for this period. This dietetic
regimen should be continued till the k/eda (moisture) of dosas and dhatus is cleared. After
this uncting substances, enemas and specific diet medicated with appetizing, life prolonging,

* anabolic, sweet and vata suppressing drugs should be prescribed.
The woman with mature fetus should be prescribed fats from the day of extraction of

the fetus.

In explaining above definition three points have to be considered—

a) Which specific condition should be considered as state of stupefaction
(midhatwa) or clarification of above definition.

b) At what gestational age the fetus can become a mitdhagarbha (obstructed labour).
c) Whether this obstruction occurs in alive or dead fetus.
a) Explanation of definition given in classics

The litera] meaning of word mitdha which is derived from dhdtu “muh” is to become
stupefied, unconscious or swooned, to become bewildered or going in wrong direction and
become lazy. Obstructed movement and abnormal alongwith obstructed movement is the
explanation given for the word midha by Bhavamisra and Madhukosa commentary respec-
tively. Thus mitdhagarbha refers to the condition in which the fetus has gone astray, is
swooned with absence of discend. The definition given by Susruta and Vagbhata actually

includes almost all the conditions of obstructed labour described today, as explained here-
under—

iv) Abnormality of apana vayu causing sammohana of garbha—The word “samm-

ohana” has been explained by all the commentators as unconsciousness of the fetus, how-

apana vayu situated in the maternal body, which is totally unrelated to the consciousness
of the fetus. The maintenance of consciousness of the fetus is a function of prana vayu
situated in fetal body which is not deranged, thus the question of fetus becoming uncon-
scious does not arise, rather it gets stupefied. Main function of apana vayu is to expell the
fetus by stimulating myometrium, naturally its abnormality will produce obstruction to the

movement or delivery of the fetus by influencing myometrial activity. Considering these

points this description should be considered as obstruction to the process of descend of fetus

or in the progress of labour due to abnormal or feeble uterine contractions or uterine inertia.

death of fetus should be considered as causative factor for midhagarbha also. Susruta
giving caption to the chapter as “midhagarbhanidana” (etiology of obstructed labour) has
discussed the causes of abortion which are being recapitulated here.

prognosis of midhagarbha. In cases of cervical prolapse, proper dilatation of cervix does
not take ‘place thus obstructs the labour.

The fetus remains in the uterus because of its nddi nibandhana. Release of these bonds
initiates labour as explained earlier. In this reference also the release of bonds should be
interpretted as release of nddintbandhana. Dalhana’s explanation about muscles or vessels
attached to the uterus is not proper, because the fetus is not directly attached to the muscles
or vessels of the uterus. It is difficult to explain the word atikramana or transgression,
because transgression of uterus will happen only after its rupture. If transgression is ex-
plained in a way that leaving its normal situation the fetus descends for expulsion, then
also there will be difficulty, because in this condition the descend will precede the trans-
gression, while in description the transgression precedes descend. Due to these facts here
the word ‘garbhasayamatikramya’ has to be explained on the basis of ‘kram padaviksepe’
i.e. over irritation or stimulation of uterus due to hyperactivity of extremities of the fetus
caused by detachment of its bonds. The fetus with inconspicuous body parts or in unsolid
state (up to 3rd month) remains within the pelvic cavity, thus consideration of spaces
inbetween liver and spleen in the pathogenesis of abortion does not arise, because, this level
is attained during eighth month of pregnancy. The word midha used in pathogenesis
denotes abnormality or absence of movement of apana vayu and fetus both. In abortion
the abnormality of movement of only apana vayu occurs, while in midhagarbha both i.
e. fetus and apana vayu have abnormality or absence of movement. On the basis of above
explanations pathogenesis of abortion and midhagarbha may be considered in following
way—

a) Abortion—Due to causes mentioned earlier the fetus getting detached from its bonds
of na@dies, descending from the spaces of bowels irritates the kostha (abdomen). Due to this
irritation the apana vayu having abnormal movements producing pain in flanks etc. symp-
toms followed by bleeding per vaginum produces abortion.

b) Miidhagarbha—The fetus getting detached from its bonds of nddies, anxious to
deliver, having hypermobility of its body parts produces extreme irritation/stimulation to
the uterus. Due to this hyperactivity of uterus the fetus descending (forcefully) from the
spaces inbetween liver, spleen and bowels causes irritation to the kostha (abdomen), which

प्रसव-विज्ञानीय vee

Specific clinical features of midhagarbha are its various positions and presentations.
The fetus engages in the pelvic cavity by its head or shoulder or thighs (breech). These
indicate abnormalities of vertex, transverse and breech positions/presentations.

Midhagarbha occurs due to abnormality of vayu, being compressed by this abnormal
vayu, having various movements it presents in numerous ways, however, for understanding
the subject Susruta and Madhavanidana etc. have described these in two way : (i) types of
midhagarbha (ii) its gaties. Vagbhata has described only different gaties in relation to
treatment. Harita has envisaged the role of different dosas and classified midhagarbha
accordingly.

3) हारीत संहिता-वर्णित दोषिक मूढ़यर्थो के लक्षण (Clinical features of dosika midhagarbhas as per

१) वातिक मूढ़गर्भ (Vatika midhagarbha)
वातजन्य गर्भसंरोध में बस्ति-शूल, योनिद्वार का अवरोध, जठर-गर्जन (शब्द), SHAM, तोद, agi में टूटने सदृश
बेदना तथा निद्रानाशादि लक्षण होते है ।

In the obstruction of fetus caused by vara, the lady gets pain in the region of urinary
bladder, obstruction to the vaginal passage, gurgling sound in the abdomen, flatulence, pain
(in abdomen), breaking type of severe bodyache and insomnia.

२) पैत्तिक मूढ़गर्भ (Paittika mitdhagarbha)
पित्तजन्य गर्भावरोध में शूल, त्रिदोषज ज्वर, तृष्णा-दोष, भ्रम, मूत्रकृच्छ तथा शिरोवेदना होती 21

In this condition the woman suffers fron pain (in abdomen), fever caused by all the
three dosas (tridosaja jwara), thirst, giddiness. dysuria and headache.

3) श्लैष्पिक मूढ़गर्भ (Slaismika midhagarbha)

श्लैष्मिक yaad में आलस्य, 7H, निद्रा, जड़ता, आध्यान, वेषथु (कम्प), कास तथा मुखवैरस्व होता है ।
In this condition the lady has idleness, drowsiness, sleepiness, stillness, flatulence,
tremors, cough and testelessness of mouth.

4o¥ आयुर्वेदीय प्रसूतितन्त्र एवंस्त्रीरोग

माधवनिदान, भावप्रकाश तथा योगरलाकर में भी लिखा है कि शिर को धारण करने में असमर्थ या अबनत शिर
वाली, whats, लज्जा-शून्य, कुक्षि में नील वर्ण को Rei से युक्त स्त्री गर्भ को तथा वह गर्भ उस स्त्री को नष्ट कर
देता है तथा योनिसंवरण, कुक्षि-सद्ग (योनिसंवरण जन्य प्रकुपित वायु से गर्भाशय में रुका हुआ गर्भ) तथा मक्कल्ल एवं
अन्य उपद्रबों से पीड़ित मूढ़गर्भा स्त्री जीवित नहीं रहती ।

In the presence of garbhakosaparasanga, makkalla and yonisamvrti the mitdhagarbha
becomes incurable. Last two (i.e. seventh and eighth garies described earlier) are also
incurable. Other varieties of miidhagarbha when associated with hallucination or perception
of non existent or opposite things by sensory organs, convulsions, disorders of vata, yoni-
bhraméa (prolapse of uterus), yonisamva:ana, makkalla, §wasa (dyspnoea), cough and gid-
diness should also be left or should not be treated.

The woman who is unable to hold her head or strikes her head repeatedly, whose body
is cold, has become shameless and blue vessels have appeared over her abdomen, she kills
her fetus and fetus kills her. Both Vagbhatas have mentioned presence of foul smell in

~ breath also as a sign of incurability.

Kasyapa has given entirely different description in following way—

A woman with obstructed labour (midhagarbha) having foul smell in breath, severe
pain in abdomen and over-sleepiness does not survive.

A woman with mitdhagarbha who sees the fire just like neck of a peacock (blue in
colour), whose feet and face are swollen does not survive.

The woman having midhagarbha, if wears red garments and garlands, uses red anoint-
ments, smiles during sleep and goes towards cremation ground (in dream) does not survive.

Hiarita opines that if the garbhakosa is apanna (uterus is diseased), fetus has slow
progress (due to ineffectual uterine contractions) or there occurs yonisarga (obstruction to
the labour due to constriction of ‘yoni or pelvis) then also the miidhagarbha is incurable.

MadhavaNidana, Bhavaprakasa and Yogratnakara etc. books also have expressed simi-
lar views. .

surgical treatment for these both has been advised. This indicates that here the incurability
refers to the impossibility of delivery by use of drugs, hymns or manual extraction. Surgical
procedures were never free from risk, thus these both the gaties have been enlisted as
incurable. The clarification of abnormalities of passage and general disorders is being given
here. है

A) Abnormalities of passage

i) Garbhakosa-parasaiiga — Dalhana has offered two explantions to this word i. e. over
clinging of fetus in the uterus or attachment of fetus in other than its normal place. Over
clinging does not seem to be proper explanation as word ‘para’ denctes away not excessive
or over. For attachment or stay of fetus at other place than the uterus the rupture of uterus
is essential. Sir M. M. William has explained the word ‘parasanga’ as ‘cleaving’ which
means split (often asunder, in two) and break also. Rupture of uterus sometimes is seen in
cases of obstructed labour and is considered to be one of the serious complication even
today: Considering all this, here garbhakosaparasanga should be considered as rupture of
uterus. :

Apannata of garbhakosa or diseased state of uterus can be either due to rupture of
uterus occurring at the time of delivery or congenital anomalies such as uterus arcuatus,
didelphis, septate etc. or else due to fibroid uterus, which produce obstruction in the labour.
In all these conditions the delivery can be effected only with cesarean section.

ii) Makkalla—Dalhana while commenting on verse of sittrasthana has referred it as
accumulation of blood in uterus during labour before delivery of the child or intrapartum
haemorrhage, however, in nid@nasthana he explains it as the pain arising after delivery due
to blood getting obstructed by vdyu. This latter explanation does not seem to be proper as
the question of delivery in a case of obstructed labour does not arise. Adhamalla has very
clearly classified makkalla in two i.e. developing during pregnancy and during puerperium.
The fetus afflicted with physical and psychological diseases produces pain in abdomen, |
which is known as garbhamakkalle. Makkalla is characterized with spasmodic contraction
of uterus, thus in reference to obstructed labour it denotes either intrapartum haemorrhage
associated with, severe pain or tetanic or spasmodic irregular: uterine contractions.
Intrapartum haemorthage and tetanic or irregular uterine contractions are one of the
imprortant cause of difficulties in management of obstructed labour.

iii) Yonisamvrti or yonisamvarana—Though Susruta and Vagbhata have referred this
word, yet have not detailed the disease. One finds the description of disease in Madhukosa
commentary, Bhavaprakaga and Yogaratnakara in following words— ~~

Due to use of dietetics capable of vitiating vata, excessive coitus and night awakening
the vayu situated in yonimarga (vaginal canal) of pregnant woman getting aggravated con-
tracts the vaginal orifice. This very va@yu after obstructing the vaginal orifice moving in-
wards obstructing the apperture of saya (cervix of utenis) troubles the fetus situated inside
the uterus. Fetus dies due to obstruction of its mouth and respiration. This inward moved

## Scanned page 280

५०८ आयुर्वेदीय प्रसूतितन्त्र एवंस्त्रीगोग

aggravated vayu causes feeling of ligature or tightness in the cardiac region, shallow expi-
ration (breathing) along with and upward movement (displacement of apex beat due to over
distension of abdomen) along with obstruction to the heart of pregnant woman and then kills
her. This dreaded disease is known as yonisamvarana which is always fatal.

In this condition due to abnormality of vayu or nervous functions the spasm of yoni
(vaginal orifice) and garbhasayadwara or cervix of uterus occurs or in other words this
refers to severe degree of cervical dystocia in which condition cesarean section is needed.

iv) Yonibhraméa—Here with yonibhraméa the uterine prolapse should be considered.
In cases of prolapse the labour is often obstructed and very difficult.

v) Slow progress of fetus or uterine i.ertia— Due to uterine inertia the progress of
labour becomes very slow. Though usually myometrium responds to uterine stimulants, yet,
in few cases it becomes totally innert and does not respond to stimulants, thus, the fetus has
to be extracted by cesarean section or in other words uterine inertia also causes incurability
of midhagarbha.

vi) Yonisanga— Yonisarga refers to the obstruction of fetus in the materal passage
probably due to contraction of pelvis. In contracted pelvis also the mitdhagarbha becomes
incurable as the delivery had to be completed by cesarean section.

B) General disorders

General disorders such as opposite or abnormal perception by cognitive organs and
convulsions or tremors (due to excessive trouble, insoninia or toxaemia), dyspnoea, giddi-
ness, foul smelling expiration (smell of ketone bodies due to marked catabolism in absence
of nourishment), coldness of body (due to improper functioning of circulatory system),
absence of shyness and appearance of blue vessels over the abdomen are indicative of loss
of physical and psychological power, in which conditions obstructed labour becomes incur-

able. .

Till the fetus is alive every effort should be made to deliver it. If delivery does not

Vagbhata II has added that besides above treatment the yoni (external genitalia and
vaginal canal) should be irrigated with lukewarm water followed by anointing it with

jaggery, kinva (seeds or drugs used for fermentation) and salt. The vagina should be repeat-

obtained from atast.
Harita has prescribed following drugs for quick and easy delivery—
a) Root of /angali pestled with hot water should be applied over umbilicus.
b) Root of bala, sirryakanti and somavalli pestled with kanjt should be applied.
०) Roots of bhiru, bhiinimba, vartakt and pippaltyaka, yawani, agra and vaca pestled
with warm water should be applied below the umbilicus.
d) Roots of laigali and devadali, tumbica and koSataki pestled together should be
applied. :
e) Following mantras should be recited for easy delivery.
i) “In northern bank of Aimdlaya there lives a rdksast named Surasa, by hearing the
sound of her nipura (an ornament) the woman delilvers easily”.
ii) Use of water or milk treated with “An hri calaya calaya swaha” etc. mantra
facilitates delivery.
iii) “An hram....hrah” etc. hymn should be written on upper portion of bhisrjapatra,
this should either be shown to the woman or kept under her bed.

(straightening) and darana (incision) etc. all the acts had to be done only with one hand
taking care not to injure the mother and fetus (if alive) both.

कि शस्त्र-कर्म करने से चहिले भोजन नहीं देना चाहिए, टीकाकार अरुणंदत्त का मत है कि भोजन का निषेध है परन्तु

In five disorders i.e. mitdhagarbha, aréa (piles), asmari (urinary bladder stones),
bhagandara (rectal/anal fistula) and mukharoga (diseases of mouth) the surgery should be
done in empty stomach, because in full abdomen there may be difficulty in insertion of
instruments or the patient may die and vata also gets aggravated.

Ingestion of food is contraindicated before surgical treatment of madhagarbha. Aruna-
data says that though the food is contraindicated, yet the wine should be prescribed,
however Hemadri also has contraindicated both.

उसकी (मूढगर्भ-शल्योद्धरण की) विद्या-सहित (पूर्वकर्माभ्यास से प्राप्त ज्ञान के आधार पर) उपक्रम करे क्योंकि अक्रिया
या शल्योद्धरण न करने से मृत्यु (स्त्री की) निश्चित है तथा उपक्रम करने में संशय या सफलता की प्राप्ति में संदेह
है। टीकाकार इन्दु का मत है कि ईश्वर से पूछकर कार्य करने में स्त्री की मृत्यु हो जाने पर भी अयश नहीं मिलता ।

अष्यड्वहदयकार ने भी लिखा है कि वैद्य ईश्वर (नृप-अरुणदत्त ) से पूछकर यलपूर्वक शीघ्रातिशीघ्र आहरण (गर्भ
का) करे। हु

Before extraction of miudhagarbha the consent of guardian must be obtained explain-
ing that if the surgical interference is not done death (of mother) is sure and even in surgical
procedure there is doubt-in success. After this, placing her in proper position surgery should
be done. Indu has explained that by obtaining consent the physician does not get defamed
even if woman dies.

भावप्रकाश तथा योगरत्नाकरकार ने लिखा है कि सर्पिषाक्त हस्त का योनि में प्रवेश करके जीवित गर्भ को यत्न
से निकालना चाहिए. |

Once the fetus is dead or medicinal treatment has failed, the extraction of fetus should
be done by keeping the woman in supine position with flexed thighs, her hips should be
elevated by keeping a thick pad of cloths (fig. 17). The vagina and hand (fig.18) should be
lubricated with mucinous substance or gum of dhanwana, nagavrttika (sallaki), Salmali and
ghrta. Now the fetus should be extracted by inserting the hand.

Both the Vagbhatas, Bhavaprakasa and Yogaratnakara have expressed almost identical
views, however, Hatita says that the lady should be made to sit over a circular thick pad
made for the purpose, with extended (abducted) thighs during extraction of midhagarbha.

The fetuses delivering with different positions/presentations should be extracted in
following way— है

Presentations/positions Manipulations and extraction of fetus

a) Both the thighs Draw in the same or downward proper direction

(fig. 19a, b).
First deliver another thigh (fig. 20a) then extract
the fetus (fig. 200).

Dislodge the buttocks, push, them upwards
(ig. 21a), bring both the thighs downwards (fig.
214) and deliver the fetus (fig. 210).

Push the back side or hips of the fetus upwards,
bring the head downwards to the passage (fig. 22
a, b), straighten it and extract (cephalic version)
(fig. 22c).

Disledge the shoulder, push it upwards, bring the
head to the maternal passage and extract the fetus
(cephalic version). .

Push both the arms ‘upwards by pressing the ©
shoulder region, (fig. 23), bring the head down to
the passage and extract the fetus.

b) One thigh

c) Buttocks

d) Oblique or transverse just
like a wooden belt used to
fasten the door

e) Head moved to the lateral
side (shoulder presentation)

f) Both arms

In short, it can be said that in former three presentations delivery is to be completed.
with thigh or foot presentation, in latter three presentations cephalic version should be done
and the fetus should then be delivered. In last two presentations (described under gaties)
manual extraction is not possible thus surgery has to be done. :

The position of various abnormally situated fetal parts should be corrected by drawing,
dislodging, compressing, pulling downwards, pushing upwards and bringing appropriate
part to the maternal passage, then the fetus should be extracted, such as in face or brow
presentation the frontal portion or forehead should be dislodged and pushed upwards thea
the vertex should be compressed and pulled downwards and delivery conducted (fig. 24).

Harita says that after making the woman sit over circular pad with streched or abduct-
ed thighs her back should be gently compressed and the fetus should be brought downwards
in the abdomen. Once the fetus reaches vaginal passage, the hand lubricated with tila oil
and water should be inserted in vagina already oleated with tila oil and water. Now the neck
of fetus should be grasped with index finger and thumb and fetus extracted.

rasna@ and cavya should be prescribed with fat preferably oil for relief of pain and rigidity
of vagina and flanks and excretion of rakta (blood) and eda (moisture) etc. 40545, Alter-

natively decoction, paste or powder of these drugs without fat (ghrta or oil) can also be
used.

b) For relief of pain and excretion of dosas powdered stembark of Saka, hingu, ativisa,
patha, katukarohini and tejovati be prescribed with the method described supra.

c) Powder, paste or decoction of dipyakd, ativisd, rasna, hingu, ela and pancakola
should be prescribed with ghria.

d) Decoction of Sirisa and kakubha is beneficial if held in mouth. Tampon soaked with
this should be placed in vagina.

¢) For suppression of vayu use of baldtaila in the form of tampon or vaginal irrigation
(yoni-santrapana), massage, tisane, enema and with diet is beneficial. Just like balataila,
others such as Satapaka balataila and oils prepared with atibala, guduci and nilotpala etc.
can be used.

iv) Duration of use of drugs and congenial diet is as follows—

For three, five or seven days medicine described above (under 3a, b, ०), then‘in the
morning fat (medicated ghrta or oil) and in the evening well treated asava and arista should
be given (total 10 days). For subsequent ten days milk medicated with the drugs capable
of suppressing vata, then for another ten days meat soup should be prescribed. After this
period (three groups of ten days each i. e. one month) use of unctous, light and congenial
diet in little quantity, sudation, and use of bald etc. oils as massage, tampon, enema or tisane
should be continued for four months (total four months or diet etc. for further 3 months).
During this period she should avoid anger. After relief from complications and attainment
of proper strength and complexion within these four months, she should discontinue this
congenial mode and enjoy other pleasures of life.

Dalhana has clarified that above procedure is applicable in cases of extraction of full
term fetus. In case of midhagarbha of fourth, Sth or 6th month of pregnancy, after extract-
ing the fetus only fasting followed by fat and salt-free gruel made of uddalaka etc. cereals
should be prescribed for the number of days corresponding to the duration of pregnancy in
months (i, 6. 4th month pregnancy then four days treatment). After this period i.e ii
seventh and eighth month the procedure described above should be prescribed.

v) Complications arising during this period should be managed with appropriate mea-
sures.

vi) The treatment described for intrauterine dead fetus by Caraka can also be used.

vii) Use of sudation is beneficial, specially to the one who is free from complications.
vii) Use of cold water is congenial.

Method of preparation—

All the drugs (described under b) together should be taken in 1/4 quantity of oil. The
decoctions (described under a) and oil should be mixed with the paste of these drugs and
cooked in low fire. When oil is properly prepared this should be filled in the pot made of
gold, silver or clay and be kept in secret and protected place.

This oil is praised by lord Dhanwantari. It should be prepared for kings, other influ-
ential persons like kings, delicate, cheerful and wealthy persons.

प्रसव-विज्ञानीय ५३७

The oil should be used orally, inhaled, massaged and also as an enema, it should be
given orally to a puerperal woman; be used by the woman desirous of having a conception
(infertile woman), the man suffering from loss or deficiency of sukra (frigidity and
infertillity), others (both sexes) having véitaksaya. injuries to the marmas (vital parts), crush
injury, other trauma, fracture of bone, dislocations of joints, injury due to fall, or who are
tired due to excessive exercise. It can also be used by emaciated persons, puerperal women,
children, old persons, persons seized with grahas, suffering either from chronic diseases
or for a long period, having colic, psychological fever (mdansikajvara) or daiwaprakapa
(curses of god). It is also beneficial in convulsive disorders, paralysis, facial paralysis and
other disorders of véita, Aikka (hiccup), kaésa (cough), adhimantha (hemicrania), gulma and
severe swdsa (dyspnoea). Its continuous use for six months cures Gntravrddhi (hernia),
increases dhdtus, retains youth and gives a woman desired son. It also increases strength,
virility, memory, intellect, agni (digestive/metabolic power), virya and ojas. It also cures
fever, unmada (insanity), miitraghata (suppression/retention of urine), yonivyapat (gynec
disorders) and ksaya (tuberculosis). -

In a woman who has died during labour just like a killed goat (vastamara) if quivering
of abdomen still persists, the abdomen should immediately be opened and fetus extracted.
Dalhana has explained this verse that the procedure is to be done in ninth month (full term)
of pregnancy and in a woman who has died accidentally all of sudden in the same way as
a goat throttled or sacrificed by priest dies suddenly without much trouble; in such case
immediately within two ghaties or one muhiirta (fortyeight minutes) the fetus should be
extracted by laparotomy (fig. 30) or else the fetus will die. In Vangasena this Dalhana’s
view is given in unequivocal words that when a woman carrying full term fetus dies due
to trauma (sudden accidental death) but the quivering of fetus (fetal heart sounds) still
persist, then the fetus should immediataly be extracted by laparotomy. .

Viagbhatas have inentioned that during janmakdla (delivery of full term fetus) if quiv-
ering of abdomen over bastidwara (neck of bladdez or suprapubic or bladder region) of dead
woman is persistent then the fetus should immediately be delivered by laparotomy. Indu
opines that the laparotomy should be performed over bladder region. In one edition of
Susruta Samhita the word bastidwara has been used in place of vastamara, which will have
similar -explantion as that of Vagbhata.

Arunadatta has explained that if the abdomen of woman dieing during first stage of
labour excessively quivers near the bladder-region, then the expert physician should per-
form the laparotomy during interval period of quiverings and extract the child.

सूतिका-विज्ञानीय 77 ०

(NORMAL AND ABNORMAL PUERPERIUM)
सूतिका की परिभाषा (Definition of sittika or puerperal woman)

सभी आचार्यों ने अपरा-पतन के पश्चात्‌ ही सूतिका-परिचर्या का वर्णन दिया है जिसका अन्तर्निहित अर्थ यह ही
होता है कि अपरा-पतन के पूर्व स्त्री को सूतिका नहीं कहा जाना चाहिए। स्पष्टतर निर्देश महर्षि काश्यप ने क्रिया है कि-

(बालक का) प्रसव होने के बाद भी यदि अपरा न गिरे तो उसे प्रसूता नहीं कहा जा सकता अर्थात्‌ अपरा गिरने
के पश्चात्‌ ही वह प्रसूता या सूतिका कही जानी चाहिए।

Though all the classics have advised specific management of siika (puerperal: woman)
only after expulsion of placenta, however, explicit description is given only by Kasyapa. He

says that after delivery of child till the placenta is not expelled, the woman can not be called
sitika, im other words siika term can be used only after expulsion of placenta.

"Anatomic changes occurring in reproductive organs during pregnancy reach their
almost prepregnancy stage after about six weeks, however, in resumption of prepregnancy
physiology i.e. ovarian and menstrual cycle great individual variations occur, as some
women restart their menstruation from the second month of delivery, while others may not
get it even for one or two years. Considering this individual Variation, the authors have not
given any specific time limit, rather have just said that ‘reappearance of menstruation’, In
other words it can be said that 1% months duration and feappearance of menstruation is
given considering anatomical and physiological changes of teproductive system respective-
ly. The limit of six month probably reflects the idea about Teappearance of menstrual cycle,
while four months period is probably given keeping in view the mudhagarbha or other
abnormal labours, where-in Post-operative management for four months has been advised.

delivery)

Three factors have been emphasized i.e. replenishment of dhdtus, steadiness of body
and accumulation of blood in yoni (uterus). The explanation of each one is given here-
under—

a) Replenishment of dhatus—This indicates replenishment of all the seven dhdtus i.e.
from rasa to Sukra. Sometimes in anaemia caused either due to excessive postpartum
haemorrhage or due to certain other causes the onset of menstruation after delivery may be
delayed. Sukra the seventh dha@tu and Grtava an upadhatu refer to anterior pituitary and
ovarian hormones respectively. Proper presence of these is indispensible for onset of men-
struation.

b) Steadiness of body—Here this steadiness refers to healthy state of body. Certain
diseases may influence the formation of proper dhatus thus the menstruation. Psychology of
woman also plays an important role in menstrual physiology. Only after proper physical and
psychological health the woman restarts her menstruation.

c) Accumulation of blood in yoni or uterus—The blood collected in uterus for whole
month within its dhamantes is discharged during menstruation. Inspite of proper physical
and mental health, if endometrium ts diseased (due to acute puerperal infection etc.) the
blood will not get accumulated and menstruation will not restart.

महर्षि वाग्भट ने सूतिका को बृंहण के योग्य माना है है। महर्षि काश्यप ने मण्ड-प्रयोग का निर्देश दिया है।

In general all the classics have advised massage, oral administration of fats with
medicines and decoctions for three to seven days after delivery. Use of medicated rice gruel
is prescribed in diet. From seventh or twelfth day medicated meatsoup is advised. However,
there is slight difference of opinion in the list of drugs amongst various authors.

Caraka says that when puerperal woman feels hunger she should be prescribed pow-
dered pippali, pippalimila, cavya, citraka and Srngabera with any one out of ghrta, oil,
vasa (animal fat) or majja (marrow) considering her tolerability for these, and in the quan-
tity which she can digest easily. After ingesting this, her abdomen should be massaged and
wrapped properly with a big clean cloth. This wrapping produces compression of abdomen,
thus prevents presence of hallow space, so the vayu does not get vitiated. After digestion
of ghrta etc. fats, liquid gruel made with rice and medicated with pippali etc. drugs men-
tioned above and mixed with ghrta should be given. During both the times i.e. morning and
evening imtigation or bath with hot water should precede use of ghrta etc. and rice gruel.
Cakrapani says that in the moming irrigation should be given before ingestion of oleaginous
substance and should be repeated after its digestion, afterwards rice gruel should be given.
After use of this regimen for five or seven nights (day and nights) gradual administration
of vrmhana substances (anabolic or likely to increase flesh and energy) should be done. This
regimen is not suitable for the women of aniipadega (marshy land), because in the persons
of this area the kapha is dominant. This regimen is suitable for the woman of jangala (wild
or dry) area.

Sugruta says that after applying massage with balataila (described under obstructed
labour) the puerperal woman should be prescribed decoction of bhadradaru etc. drugs
capable of suppressing the véita for oral administration or irrigation. If some dogas or blood
is still left inside (some blood clots are retained in uterus), powdered pippali, pippalimula,
hastipippali, citraka and Sragabera with warm jaggery-water should be given. This should
be continued for two or three days till the abnormal blood (lochia rubra) is properly excret-
ed. Afterwards rice gruel prepared with the drugs of vidarigandhadi group and mixed with
ghria or milk should be given for three days (from third or fourth day to sixth or seventh
day after delivery). Then (from 7th or 8th day) cooked §ali rice with meat soup of wild
animals prepared with yava, kola and kadattha should be prescribed considering her strength
and digestive power. Normally the woman should be given good irrigation with hot water
and should avoid anger, exercise and coitus. Dathana says that irrigation should be done by
pouring water in a stream, so that abnormal blood (accumulated in uterus) produced duc to
irritation by garbha (delivery) is excreted properly and vata is also suppressed. After
delivery of full term fetus the sudation should be given.

Vagbhata I has mentioned that massage with baldtaila should be given to the puerperal
woman. After feeling of hunger she should be given congenial oleaginous substances mixed
with either powdered paficakola or powder of yawant, upakuiicika, cavya, citraka, vyosa
and rock salt, in the quantity which she can digest in whole day. The woman unfit for use
of oily substances should be given decoction of either laghupaficamiila or drugs capable of
suppressing vata. After this oval administration of oily substance or decoction, her abdomen
should be massaged with ghrra and oil and wrapped with cloth to prevent vitiation of vayu
likely to occur due to availability of hallow space. After digestion of oleaginous substance,
liquid rice-gruel properly prepared with either above mentioned drugs or viddryadi group
of drugs or milk should be given in the quantity which she can digest properly. During this
entire period morning and evening irrigation with hot water should precede use of ghyta ete.
or rice-gruel. This regimen uged for three, five or seven nights should be followed by use
of light diet with soup of yava, kola and ladattha, After twelve nights giving duc consid-
eration to strength and digestive capacity, gradual satiation or strengthening should be done
by use of meat soup of wild animals; besides, oil, ghrta or decoction prepared with jivantya,
vrmhaniya, madhura and vatahara drugs should be used in the from of massage, unguent,
irrigation and batheing. Agreeable diet or drinks should also be given.

Vagbhata Ii has also given almost similar description as Vagbhata I, however, he has
advised massage of even yoni alongwith body and use of hot jaggery-water just like Susruta.
Avunadatta has explained that if meat preparations are used before twelve days, it invites
the danger of infliction by skanda etc. twelve grahas.

Kaéyapa says that the puerperal woman should use specifically raksoghna (antiseptic)
and beneficial things. Detailed management should be done giving due consideration to
place of living (deéa and videsa) and traditions of the family. The woman immediately after
delivery should be encouraged by sweet-spoken accoucheuse, and made to lie down in

सूतिका-विज्ञानीय
ण्परे

hunch-back position. Now she should rub her back, press her abdomen/flanks and then
compress her abdomen having been moved by vayu (entire musculature of abdomen acts
with force due to effect of apana yayu to expell the fetus) in order to expel the dosas left
over after delivery. After this, abdomen and flanks should be wrapped with clean bi 100,
by this wrapping abdomen reaches its proper place and vayu also subsides. The very ral
woman should always sit over a small chair covered with leather-bag fitled ‘th ho
baldtaila, with this her yoni becomes healthy. Sudation in the yoni should be iven with
oleo prepared with priyargu etc. drugs. After proper sudation hot water bath Followed i
rest should be given, after overcoming the tiredness, fumigation with kustha, guggulu 4
agaru mixed with ghrta should be done. Now, considering her strength and digestive ower
seu of boiled rice should be given for three or five days, then the woman using beneficial
diet should take orally oleaginous articles (oil, gérta etc.). After digestion of this oil etc. salt
free rice gruel mixed with little quantity of oleaginous substance and powdered pippall and
nagara should be given. This should follow (after 6 or 7 days) use of rice gruel mixed with
sufficient quantity of salt and oleaginous substance, then meat soup of wild animals and
soup of kulattha mixed with oleaginous substance, salt and sour articles and kigmanda (a
kind of pumpkin-gourd), radish, cucumber etc. vegetables fried in ghrta. After delivery the
woman should use oleation, sudation and hot water with full alertness for one month. The
management of puerperal woman should not be considered in isolation, due consideration
had to be paid to traditions as well as beneficial things or diet to the family and also place
of living. Sudation is contraindicated. हु

ह Harita has advised that after delivery the decoction of available drugs out of lodhra.
arjuna, kadamba, devadaru, bijaka and karkandhu should be given for purifying the blood
and also yeni. Vaginal filling with oil and massage followed by sudation with hot water
should be done. After fasting for first day, on second day in the morning ndgara and
harittakt with jaggery, then in the afternoon warm soup of kulattha should be given. Rice
gruel mixed with paficakola or caturjataka should be given on third and fourth day respec-
tively, on fifth day cooked Salt or sastika rice be prescribed in diet. This regimen should
continue for ten or fifteen days. The wise physician should permit the puerperal woman to
see or meet other women on twelfth day.

Bhavaprakasa has given very short description, that the puerperal woman should use
congenial, diet and mode of life, give up exercise, coitus, anger and cold air. She should use
एल, yee congenial diet and daily sudation and massage for one month with full
alertness. Yogaratnakara has added that immediately after delivery hei i

Authors have advised various protective measures described in chapter ten to prevent
mother and new born child from the seizure by -grahas or bhitas (infection), thus this also
forms a part of management for puerperal woman.

Use of asthapanabasti (evacuative enema), venesection, sternutatory drugs, purgatives
and sudation is contraindicated, however, Sarigadhara has advised sudation after delivery.
She is fit for the use of brmhana drugs. Use of manda is beneficial.

Kasyapa has described puerperal disorders at two places once in dusprajata-
cikitsitadhydya without giving exact number but numbering thittyfive and again sixtyfour
disorders in sitikopakramaniya adhyaya. Twentyfive disorders have been enumerated at
both the places while others differ. Thus total puerperal. disorders described at both the
places taken together become seventyfour which are given here under.

Disease entities described at both the places — (1) Yonibheda (vaginal tear),
(2) Yonisofa, (inflammation/edema of vagina}, (3) Yonivedana or yonisula (pain in vagina)
(4 Prsthasila (backache), (5) Katistila (pain in Jower back or sacral region), (6) Hrdisita
(cardialgia), (7) Plihodara (splenomegaly), (8) Sakhavata (hemiplegia), (9) Hanugraha
(lockjaw), (10) Manya stambha (neck rigidity), (11) Sofa or Sotha (edema or inflammation)
(12) Kamala (jaundice), (13) Jvara (fever), (14) Atisara (diarrhoea), (15) Visarpa
(erysipelas), (16) Chardi (vomiting), (17) Pravahika (dysentery), (18) Adhmana (tym-
panites), (19) Miitrarodha (retention of urine), (20) Malarodha (constipation),
(21) Aksiroga (eye disorders), (22) Kampa or vepathu (tremors), (23) Varasthila (perineal
swelling), (24) Vatagulma (phantom tumour), (25) Vicarcika (skin disorder).

Disease entities described only under dusprajatacikitsitadhyaya — (1) Asrgdara
(bleeding pec vaginum or menometrorthagia), (2) Sala (pain in abdomen) (3) Yonidosa
(gynecological disorders), (4) Moha (unconsciousness), (5) Dadru (ring worm infection),
(6) Pama (skin disorder), (7) Kitibha (skin disorder), (8) Visphota (blisters), (9) Ardha-
Siroruja (hemicrania), (10) Hrdroga (cardiac disorders).

Disease entities described only in sittikopakramaniya adhyaya — (1) YonibhramSa
(uterovaginal prolapse), (2) Yoniksata (vaginal ulceration), (3) Yonisrava (vaginal dis-
charges) (4) Yoniprasuptata (anaesthesia over vagina/vulva), (5) Parswasiila (pain in
flanks), (6) Visicika (pricking pain in abdomen associated with severe diarrhoea or chol-
era?), (7) Mahodara (ascites), (8) Angamarda (bodyache), (9) Praksepaka (convulsions),
(10) Apatanaka (emprosthotonos), (11) Makkalla (spasmodic contraction of uterus after
delivery), (12) Vidradhi (abscess), (13) Pralapa (delirium) (14) Mitrasanga (suppression of
urine), (15) Unmada (insanity or psychotic ‘condition associated with insomnia),
(16) Daurbalya (weakness), (17) Bhrama (giddiness), (18) Karsya (emaciation), (19)
Bhaktadweéa (anorexia), (20) Avipaka (indigestion), (21) Trsna (thirst), (22) Hikka (hic-
cup), (23) Swasa (dyspnoea), (24) Kasa (cough), (25) Pandu (anaemia),
(26) Raktagulma (molar pregnancy), (27) Anaha (flatulence), (28) Mukharoga (diseases of
oral cavity), (29) Pratisyaya (coryza), (30) Galagraha (stiffness of inner components of
throat), (31) Rajayaksama (tuberculosis), (32) Ardita (facial paralysis), (33) Karnasrava
(otorrhoea), (34) Prajagarana (insomnia), (35) Usnavata (gonorrhoea), (36) Grahabadha
(acute infective disorders) (37) Stanaroga (diseases of breast), (38) Rohint (diphtheria) and
(39) Raktapita (haemorrhagic diathesis).

विशिष्ट यूतिकाव्यापद्‌ (Specific puerperal disorders)
१) सूतिकारोग (Sitika roga)

we आयुर्वेदीय प्रसूतितन्त्र एवं स्त्रीरोग

body, hence under classification this is included in raktavidradhi.

According to Vagbhata internal raktaja vidradhi, while according to Indu external and

internal both raktaja vidradhi develop only in woman.

Bhoja (quoted in Madhukosa commentary) says that from dhatu form of rakta the
vidradhi does not develop, however, it develops only from the rakta accumulated in uterus
after delivery or makkalla which is a form of artava.

Opinion of 50801 seem to be more logical because internal and external raktaja-
vidradhi (infected internal and’ external haematomas) can develop in either of the sex,
however, uterine abscess of unexcreted blood after delivery develops only in females.

Clinical features of only external abscesses have been described in the books with the

indication that internal abscesses are indentical to external ones. Clinical features of external
raktaja vidradhi are—that it is covered with black blisters, is of black colour and associated

with severe pain, burning sensation, fever along with other features of pittaja vidradhi.

On the basis of these clinical features it is difficult to establish congruence with any
uterine disorder. It could be some acute infective/pyogenic condition of uterus. Explanation
of raktavidradhi described by Suéruta is being given here.

After abortion or abnormal delivery, if some products of conception are retained, these
may get infected and cause inflammation and suppuration thus produce abscess in the
uterus. However, sometimes even in normally delivered woman due to infection some
inflammation and suppuration inside the uterus or pelvic cavity may occur. If blood clots
are retained in the uterus these may facilitate growth of pyogenic bacterias. The abscess of
uterus and pelvic cavity if not incurable are difficult to be cured even to-day. Considering

these points this raktavidradhi seems to be description of acute puerperal pyometra or
pelvic abscess.

External medicines

ili) Snehana (oleation), upanaha (poultice) and anulomana (carmination) should
always be used.

iv) Once suppuration has occurred, it should be incised followed by irrigation with the
decoction of either ksiri (latex yielding such as banyan tree etc.) or aquatic plants (lotus etc).

honey and ghrta then bandaged with thin cloth.

(Drainage of pyometra through laparotomy is seldom done, hence this should be

point of posterior fornix or pouch of Douglas can be done).

Prevention of suppuration of abscess and effect of suppuration

All-out efforts should be made that the abscess dees not suppurate, since it has the
tendency of getting vidahi (suppurated), hence, is termed as vidradhi. Once it is suppurated
treatment (result) is at the mercy of god. In comparison to other diseases the treatment of
this disease should be started very quickly.

Excnination of abscess for its suppuration and method af its drainage

When pain 15 localized, there is no pain on pressure around the abscess, burning
sensation etc, have decreased and other clinical features suitable for instrumental interfer.
ence fave appeared, then the abscess should be incised and future treatment done like a
wound.

In a case of antarvidradhi (internal abscess) after knowing about its suppuration ‘by
above clinical features or else when the pus is draining through upper or lower orifices, one
should wait for ten or twelve days protecting the patient from complications.

Treatment of incompletely drained internal abscess
In a case of incomplete drainage of pus or presence of k/eda (moisture), decoction of

paste of varandadi group of drugs or madhusigeu should be given with any one out of kaiy7,
‘ara, asava, maireya or hot water for its proper drainage.

Rice gruel prepared with the decoction or Paste of roots of above drugs (drugs of
varanadi group or madhusigru) mixed with soup of yava, kola and kulattha should be siven
given.

Alongwith above mentioned causes if one uses incompatible things or articles contrary
to each other in qualities, fats or unctuous substances and cold water in the form of bath,
drink and with diet, then suffers from severe sannipdtaja jwara.

While describing general etiology of vitiation of all the three dosas, Kasyapa says that
if puerperal woman indulges in coitus, consumes incompatible or abnormal eadibles, does
night awakening, day-sleeping, worry, jealousy, greed, and uses non-satiating (emaciating)
measures, or the woman having undergone abnormal/difficult labour, does various types of
abnormal acts, then all the three dosas get vitiated and produce fever etc. various disoders,
which are difficult to cure.

As the body of puerperal woman becomes languid due to over exertion caused by
continuous strong labour pains, vata etc. dosas are irritated, indriyas (conative and cognitive
organs) are exhausted and dhatus have loss of their sdra (essence) due to haemorrhage,
hence even if one dosa gets aggravated it gives too much trouble. हे

As it becomes very difficult even for a expert person to clean an old extremely dirty
cloth, because it gets tattered with slightest negligence, similarly it becomes very difficult
to cleanse (purify) the body of puerperal woman, because due to haemorrhage the dosas are
too much aggravated and adhered to the body parts.

As an old house can not withstand rain, wind and tremors due to looseness of its
bonds, similarly the puerperal woman is unable to tolerate the diseases caused by vata, pitta
or kapha due to exhaustion of labour and blood loss.

The dosas sustain the body. In case of their decline the puerperal woman suffers from
fever characterized with rise in temperature. The temperature shoots very quickly. in the
same way as the dry wood catches fire:

Clinical features of fever arising due to sight (effect) of grahas, fear, vata, trauma and
shaking or trembling are as follows—

Tremors of whole body, crying or deep breathing, abnormal visual perception, tired-
ness, tremors/twitching of hands and eyes, yellowishness of face and eyes, quick alteration
in body complexion into blackness or normal colour, inspite of full consciousness crying
and plucking of hair and other features of fever caused by vata are the clinical features’ of
fever caused by grahas. In this disease measures to pacify grahas and other treatment
prescribed for fever due to vata should be used.

Due to excretion of blood through uterus after delivery, the dosas following it also get
dropped or trickie down, emeties, sternutatory drugs (suberrhines), enemas and purgatives
should not be prescribed, because the dosas in the body are comparatively in lesser amount.

Giving due consideration to the strength of dosas these cleansing measures should be used -
very judiciously.

The woman suffering from fever and having lost sufficient amount of dosas should not
be prescribed sharp emetics and purgatives with pungent drugs. Paripaka (metabolic chang-
es) of dhatus occur due to heat generated by fever in the body and use of pungent drugs
as emetics or purgatives makes these dhatus abnormal.

ii) Decoction of paola, musta, madhuka, rohini etc. mixed with ghrta should be

iii) In fever due to sannipata having predominance of kapha, decoction of patola,

iv) In fever due to sannipaia having predominanance of pitia, decoction of ela,

v) For anulomana of dosas (movement of dosas in their normal channels) either
decoction of bhdrAgi, srigi, trivrt, dant, daSamiila, durdlabha, katwanga, triphala, Suntht
and pippafi mixed with rock salt and yawaksdra or ¢rivrt mixed with cow urine or only vaca
(decoction) should be given. Once dosas have started moving in their proper channels and
grahani (digestive capacity or appetite) has become strong, then properly prepared ghria
should be given for drinking.

vi) Use of either ghrta prepared with madhuka, ativisa, rohint and bhadradaru, or
kalyanaka ot mahdkalyanaka ot pahicagavya ghrta in appropriate and suitable period cures
fever due to sannipata.

vii) After lapse of eight days of fever, then use of light diet with samsarjanakrama
(serial way) if in the fever caused by two dosas (dwandwaja) or all the three dosas
(sGnnipatika) delirium due to predominance of vayu, specially retention of urine and con-
stipation associated with pain and dyspnoea occur, then meat soup of wild animals mixed
with old ghrta should be given. Afterwards use of decoction of dasamiila, kulattha, yava,
kuwala, kulirasrngi, rasna, Safi, puskaramila, bharagi and durdlabha pacifies vitiated vayu
and fever both.

viii) Two pacifying cooled-decoctions prepared with either pippalt and duralabha or
pippali and mrdwika should be used with honey in the cases having remission of fever due
to use of digestive or metabolising drugs but retention of mala (feces) left over after proper
metabolisation and reduction in the strength of dosas.

ix) Ghrta prepared with juice of gudisct and admalaka alongwith paste of sariv, Sunthi,
lodhra, dadima and candana is known as mangalyaka ghrta. This cures visamajwara (in-
termittent fever) and is beneficial like nectar in all types of fevers.

What should be the normal duration in between two pregnancies has not clearly been
spelled in classics. Susruta says that after one delivery, if the woman delivers subsequently
after six years then the born child is short lived. Dalhana explaines that subsequent delivery
should take place in five, four, three or two years, after lapse of this period the born child
is short lived, because she has not conceived due to existence of certain abnormalities in

Caraka says that the attendant should care the new born in following way. She should
produce sound by striking or rubbing two stones together near the base of ear of the neonate.
sprinkle over face of the child the hot or cold water alternately or on the basis of season
i.e. cold water during summer and hot water during wiuter. With these procedures the child
gets relief from the troubles caused by compression in the yeni (maternal passage) or from
the instruments used at the time of delivery, besides it also regains the life. Once the child
has properly. regained life and has become totally normal, bath should be given and anai
orifice should also be cleaned. Now the woman should wrap the finger, nail of which is
already trimmed, with well washed cotton swab and cleanse the palate, lips, throat and
tongue of the child with this finger and then cover the brahmarandhra (anterior fontanelle)
with cotton impregnated with oil. Now ghrta mixed with rock salt should be given orally
for producing emesis, cutting of umbilical cord and jatakarma should be done according
to the rituals prevaleut in country at that period and also in one’s own caste or family, then
first feeding with honey and ghrta treated with mantras should be given.

Susruta says that after removing ‘va (vernix caseosa) from the body and cleaning the
oral cavity with rock salt and giyta, mitrdha (forehead or anterior fontanelle) should be
covered with tampon soacked with ghyta or bala taila, then umbilical cord should be cut.
Now the child unconscious due to compression in yoni and by instruments should be revived
or encouraged by sprinkling or irrigating cold water, and after performing the jatakarma
honey, ghrta and powder of anantéd (gold) in the dose of one guija with index finger should
be given for licking, then after massaging with bald taila the bath should be given,

Vagbhatal has advised removal of wlba (vernix caseosa) with rock salt and ghrta, After
this the child who is suffering from fever and deep unconsciousness, is unable to cry as per
intensity of pain, whose dAdtus have decreased and are unstable, attainment of youth is
doubtful or is unable to survive long, touch of hand, cloths or bed gives the pain as if being
cut by saw and appears to be dieing due to unconsciousness caused by compression in yoni,

should be irrigated with bala taila. Strikiag of two stones together should be done near the
base of ear. After proper revival, umbilical cord should be cut and bath given. Now tongue,
lips and throat should be gently cleaned with nail trimmed, properly washed, dried and
cotton wrapped index finger of right hand. After elevating the tau (palate) bregma should
be covered with tampon soaked with fat. Now the child should be given paste of aindri,

Description of cutting of umbilical cord after bath etc. procedures (described above)
by Caraka and indication for cleaning the vernix caseosa before revival or resuscitation by
SuSruta and Vagbhata-1 and induction of emesis after oral feeding of specific drugs by
Vagbhatas does not seem to be proper.

Striking of stones near the base of ear might have been advised to examine the
condition of central nervous system which resembles to certain extent with Moro’s reflex.
Advice to clean anus and elevate the palate is probably given to emphasize specific exam-
ination of these body parts.

Sprinkling with hot and cold water advised by Caraka has been explained by
Cakrapani that the hot or cold water is to be used according to specific season. However,
it might have been prescribed for alternate use. The practice of stimulating respiratory
centre in asphyxia-livida through skin reflexes produced by. alternate hot and cold bath was
prevalent in twentieth century also.!

If the born child is unconscious (asphyxiated) then fanning with winnowing basket
made of &rsnakapdlikd i.e. isika@ or nala, mujija, vamSa etc. or a blackened broken earthen

_ pot should be done. This fanning and other procedures i.e. striking of stones near the ear-
base and irrigation of face with hot or cold water (alternately) should be continued until the
neonate is revived or its respiration has established properly.

Vagbhata I expressing almost similar views has advised fanning with the winnowing
basket blackened by applying domestic soot and also enchantation of mantras (described
here-under), at other place has mentioned that the disease developing during fertilization or
delivery cause pain or death, in other words this should be treated immediately.

विमर्श (Comments)

महर्षि सुश्रुत एवं अष्यड्रहदयकार ने अचेष्ट बालक की किसी भी चिकित्स्ा-विधि का वर्णन नहीं किया। सम्भवत:
जन्मोपरान्त जातकर्म के पूर्व शीतल जल से (मूर्छित शिशु को-डल्हण) आश्वासन का सुश्रुत तथा मन्त्रोच्चारण का अष्टाज्भ-
हृदय द्वास निर्देश अचेष्ट शिशु के प्राणप्रत्यागमनार्थ ही दिया गया है।

Suéruta and Vagbhata वी have not described any management specifically to be done
for asphyxiated child, however,. mention of revival of child by’ sprinkling cold water by
SuSruta and description of mantras by Vagbhata II hint towards this topic.

According to Sugruta tying of umbilical cord with thread should precede its cutting.
Dalthana has explained that hanging of cut umbilical cord with neck prevents further dis-
charge (of blood) and has advised irrigation of cut umbilical cord with kustha taila.
Both the Vagbhatas have advised that only four aftgulas (about 2”) distal to the um-

Eight angulas distance of umbilical cord given by Caraka and Sugruta seems to be
slightly more. Tying of umbilical cord after its cutting as advised by Caraka does not seem
to be proper, specially when it is to be held only gently between two fingers, because the
bleeding may persist in the interval between cutting and tying of umbilical cord.

All around the dwelling place of puerperal woman and the child (sitikagdra or labour

guggulu etc. raksoghna (antiseptic) drugs should be hung on the upper portion of door-

bed and both the pannels of door. Fire should be lit daily with the woods of kanakakantaka
or tinduka inside the labour ward. The women having qualities described earlier (under
jabour) and other well wisher women should remain awaken for ten ot twelve days (in order
to take special care of mother and child). The labour ward should be full of gifts, auspicious
recitations, blessings, praises, playings of music and musical instruments, clean and dainty
food and drinkables alongwith loyally devoted and delighted persons. For the fortune and
welfare of the mother and child the brahmanas possessing knowledge of atharvaveda
should perform santihoma (pacifying oblations to avert or remove evils) morning and
evening both the times.

Entire raksakarma is aimed at offering protection from infective disorders to the
mother and child. It is just possible that various drugs prescribed for the purpose might be
either making the environment free from infective organisms or else reduce the virulence
of these organisms.

The sixth day’s rituals might have been advised because the risk of tetanus to the
neonate is maximum upto this period, if not, this might be reflecting the social custom
prevailing even to-day. :

Sugruta and both Vagbhatas say that on first day honey and ghrta mixed with ananta
(gold, durva or yawasaka) and consecrated with mantras should be given thrice. On second
and third day ghrta medicated with Jaksamana, on fourth day twice i.e. morning and noon
honey and ghyta in the amount which fills the palm of neonate, there-after from evening free
breast feeding, as desired by the child, should be started.

विमर्श (Comments)

Feeding schedule for first three days advised by Susruta and both the Vagbhatas does
not seem to be proper, because respective feeds are advised thrice or during three periods
1.6. morning, noon and evening. If it is inferred that any number of feeds can be given
during these periods, then amount of honey and ghrta ingested by the neonate would be
much beyond his digestive capacity, however, if the feeding is given-only thrice, then it will
not be sufficient for nourishment specially for requirement of water. Advice of Caraka i.e.
breast feeding from first day is more logical. Breast feeding at the earliest possible time
after delivery to a healthy neonate by healthy mother is said to be beneficial for both. All
the authors have advised use of honey and ghrta. Honey is collected from pollens of various
flowers by bees, Pollens.are known antigenic substances, it is possible that this honey might
be containing antigens thus produces non-specific immunity in the child; the ghyta might
be helping in clearing the meconium from bowels. हु

eT आयुर्वेदीय प्रसूतितन्त्र एवं स्त्रीरोग

करके बालक का नामकरण करें। (बालक के) अड्डों में मनोह्दा, आल, रोचना, अगर तथा चन्दन का लेप करके नक्षत्र
(जन्म के नक्षत्र), देवता से युक्त बान्धवों के नाम के सदृश सम अक्षरों वाला नाम रखें।

महर्षि हारीत ने संक्षेप में लिखा है कि बारहवें दिन (ARS कर्म करके) नामकरण-कर्म at

On tenth day after delivery. the woman alongwith her child should take bath with
water medicated with sarvagandha drugs, yellow sarsapa and lodhra; dress herself with
light, intact, clean garments and sacred, desired, light and splendid ornaments. Now she
should touch auspicious objects, worship the god (whom she has always worshipped), fire
and brahmanas possessing tock of hair on crown of their head, having all the body parts
intact and wearing white garments. After having recitations for welfare and prosperity by
brdhmanas and placing the son on pack of intact cloths, she should sit keeping head of the
child towards north or cast. “The child has offered obeisance to diety and brahmanas,’
saying this the father should give him two names i.e. naksatrika (based on the planets of
birth) and abhiprayika (popular to be used daily). The popular name should begin with
ghosa varna (ha, ya, va, ra, la, ha, ma, na, na, jha, bha, gha, dha, dha, ja, ba, ga, da, da),
and end with antastha (ya, va, ra, la) or usmanta (Sa, sa, sa, ha). The name should not have
a letter with vrddha i.e. a, ai, ou, be identical with the names of three generations and be
famous. The naksatrika name should be according to the planet of birth consisting of two
or four letters.

Sugruta says that parents of the child after performing mangala and kautuka worships
(worships with specific rituals) and having recitations for welfare and prosperity should give
two names i.e. abhipreta and naksatra.

Vagbhata I has mentioned that the father of child should perform the naming ceremony
on auspicious period of tenth, twelfth or hundredth day or after completion of one year
according to traditions of one’s family, On the day of ceremony body of the child should
be anointed with manohwa, ala, rocandi, agaru and candana. The name should be venerable,
benedictory, uncommon with the énemies and consists the letters described by Caraka, The
name should not have dusta varna (inauspicious or defective letters) or taddhita varna (an
affix added to primary bases to form derivative or secondary bases from them). The name
of boy should consist even number of letters and end with visarga (a symbol in writing,
representing a hard aspiration and marked by two perpendicular dots). The name of girls
should possess odd number of letters, not be cruel, be distinct in sense or meaning, attrac-
tive, and easy to pronounce. Its last letter should consist dirgha varna (a, 7, i etc.) and
should echo like blessing.

Vagbhata It and Harita have advised the naming ceremony to be held on tenth and
twelfth day respectively.

After naming ceremony, physical examination of the child to assess longevity, stay in
kumdragara (a house or room specifically constructed or maintained for the child), care by
kumaradhara (male attendant to look after the child), detailed description of kumaragdra
(fig. 31) and kuma@radhara and period for leaving the kumdardgara or siutikagdra etc. have
been described by all the authors. Besides, special bed for child, his toys and playground;
upavesana, annaprasana and karnavedhana etc. samskaras (specific rituals performed
while making the child sit for the first time, beginning of cereal feeding and piercing of ear
respectively), have also been elaborated. Specific recipes of gold or other medicine for

. longevity, inkancement of bala (strength), buddhi (intellect) and media (memory), diet
required and diseases inflicting during entire span of childhood have also been described.
Caraka giving short description of the factors responsible for proper growth or diseases of
the new born says that dietetics and other mode of life prescribed for the woman during
antenatal period are congenial to the new born and beneficial for proper growth and devel-
opment. Abnormally used dietetics and mode of life kill the new born in the same way as
a recently planted plant, not possessing strong roots, gets destroyed by wind and heat. Since
the subject comes under the jurisdiction of pediatrician, hence is not being described here.
