i) In the. morning inbetween breast feeding, goat’s urine should be given orally for
cleansing the srotasas (channels).

ii) Bath and massage should not be given.

iii) Following ghrta should be given orally.

Bilvadimila (brhat paficamila), brhaft, and paficakola each one pala, meat of wild
animals and head of rabbit each eight palas should be cooked with sixteen times water,
when half remains, it should be filtered. Now in this deccction, goat's urine, wine, curd and
milk each equal to the quantity of decoction should be mixed, besides finely pestled
vidatiga, rock salt, ajaji, cavika, devadaru, himsra, hingu, laSuna and vyosa each one karsa
should also be mixed. With this mixture, one prastha ghrta should be cooked with standard
procedure. Use of this ghrta cures ulbaka, gulma, hidhma, disorders of vata and vataja
pandu. This also gives strength and nourishment even to a healthy child.

After digestion of food the rasa is formed. Sweet essence part of this rasa circulating
through entire body by the action of vyana vay reaches breasts and is termed as stanya
(breast milk) or in other words the stanya is formed from rasa. It is also upadhatu of rasa.
though Kasyapa, Vagbhata I and Dalhana accept the formation of Stanya from rasa, how-
ever, while describing raktagulma or placenta formation they have mentioned that one part
of rakta or the rakta left over after formation of placenta reaches breasts, gets coloured by
| kapha and forms stanya, after delivery it is increased or formed form rasa. Raja (menstrual
blood) and stanya both are said to be derived from essence part of rasa.

आयुर्वेदीय प्रसूतितन््र एवं स्त्रीरोग

wee 0

Harita says that what-so-ever is ingested by the woman, same travelling through the
 Siras of chest (esophagus) or milk-carrying sirds and getting mixed with pitta reaches
jathara (stomach). There it gets metabolised by digestive fire and then again getting pro-
cessed and metabolised by pitta, reaches Sirs or breasts and is ultimately discharged. This
secretion having association of agni-and soma is knwon as milk. As the blood due to action
of pitta gets suppurated and becomes white, so is the case with milk. In young girls due to
less strength of dhatus and in infertile women due to filling of milk-carrying channels by
vayu, the milk isnot formed. है
Bhela has included milk amongst ten pranayatanas (seats of life).

के ही काल में परिपूर्ण हो प्रथम ws या केलास्ट्रेंम का भी निर्माण हो जाता है, जिसके निर्माण में भी रक्त का योगदान
है। प्रसव के पश्चात्‌ केवल स्तन्य-निर्माण का कार्य होता है जो रस के द्वारा सम्पादित होता है।

Though apparently it looks that there is difference of opinion regarding formation of
stanya, because it is described to be formed from rakta or rasa both. However, careful
scrutiny clarifies it. Formation of stanya trom rakta is described during pregnancy period.
During pregnancy new lactic glands and lactiferous tubules are formed, existent ones grow
and develop. For this growth and development during pregnancy period the rakta (blood)
is essential, first milk secretion or colostrum is also formed during pregnancy from rakta.
After delivery there is no further growth of lactic glands, but their function i.e. formation
of milk is increased, which is accomplished by rasa.

Caraka says that the wet-nurse should be identical in varna (similar in the caste i.e.
for brahmana child the brahmana wet-nurse etc.), young (very young or old woman should
be discarded due to presence of incomplete or decreased dhatus respectively), humble or
modest, free from impatience, not possessing deficient or accessory body parts, non-addict,
beautiful, free from disgust, similar in dega (living place) and jati (sub-caste), neither mean-
minded nor indulging in mean acts, born in high family, affectionate to the child, free from
diseases, having alive male child and good amount of breast-milk, over cautious, not habitu-
ated of sleeping over excrements or used to clean the feces etc. immediately, not married
in low cast, expert in nursing, pious, clean and having hatred from unpiousness or unclean-
liness and possessing good quality of breasts and milk.

Susruta giving almost similar description says that the wet-nurse should be of average
height, middle-aged, free from diseases, well-behaved or urbane, free from fickleness, non-
greedy, neither too thiu nor too obese, possessing milk of good quality, not having too long
or protuberant lips, having neither too short nor too long breasts and other non-addiction etc.
qualities described by Caraka. The wet-nurse should be syama (dark complexioned) because
the women of this complexion possess profuse milk. The wet-nurse is to be appointed for
betterment of health, growth, development and strength of the child.

VagbhataI agreeing with above description adds that wet-nurse should be clever,
chaste or celibate, wear clean garments and keep pious ideas. She should be free from eight
{i. e. too tall or too short in height, over fair or very dark in complexion, having excessive
body hair or their total absence, obese or Jean and thin) physical disorders. Her teats should
be strong but neither too high nor too low. The breast milk of pregnant woman is contra-
indicated because it causes parigarbhika disorder. Indu has clarified that middle aged wom-
an is to be preferred because young woman does not have affection for the child and old
woman can not withstand troubles as well as her milk also is not nutritious to the child.

Vagbhata II has given similar but very short description.

KaSyapa says that wet-nurse should use daily purifying measures (internal and exter-
nal; physical and psychological). Wet-nurse belonging to similar satwa (sdtwika, rajasika
etc. manasika prakytis) to which child belongs is praiseworthy. Belonging to opposite satwa
is forbidden, because she will produce uneasiness and troubles to the child, thus the child
will either not survive or survive with great difficulty. The wet-nurse of identical satwa

When the wet-nurse has sweet milk in sufficient quantity, then after taking bath,
anointing herself and wearing white garments, should tie (on head or any other body part)
all or available drug out of aindri, brahmi, Sctaviryd, sahasravirya, amoghd, avyathtd, Siva,
arista, vatyapuspi and viswaksenakantd (all these are prajasthapana drugs). Now she should
sit facing to the east and give first her right breast to the child.

SuSruta says that on auspicious date the child should be bathed form head to toe,
clothed with new garments and made to sit facing towards north, over the lap of wet-nurse
who is sitting facing east-wards. The wet-nurse after washing the breasts and expressing out
little quantity of milk, should start breast feeding with enchantation of following mantra.

“O fortunate pretty woman ! all the four seas should produce constant flow of milk
from your breasts for increase in strength of the child. O beautiful woman ! as the deities
obtained longevity by consuming nectar, similarly the child should also get longevity by
consuming your milk which is similar to nectar”.

Almost identical description is given by VagbhataI and Bhawaprakasa.

The woman who is hungry, striken with grief, tired, has vitiation of dhdtus, is preg-
nant, suffering from fever, emaciated, obese and has consumed diet likely to produce vidaha
(burning sensation or indigestion) or the edibles opposite in character, should not give

breast-feeds to the child. The child whose recently ingested medicine is not assimilated
should also not be given the feed, because at this stage the force of dosa, ausadhi (drugs)

and mala (excretas) is too much.
Vagbhata I has advised to avoid breast feeding even by the woman who is angry and
Vagbhata II by the woman who has psychological abnormalities or reluctance for feeding.

BAR आयुर्वेदीय प्रसूतितन्र एवं स्त्रीरोग

को-सत्त्व एवं बल की प्राप्ति तथा आरोग्य-लाभ होने के साथ ही उसे रूपवान होने का वर्णन दिया है ।

अन्यत्र दुग्ध के गुणों का वर्णन करते हुए लिखो है कि दुग्ध स्रोतों को शुद्ध करने वाला, बलकारक, दोषनाशक,
fees, वृष्य एवं अग्निवर्धक होता है ।

माधवनिदान एवं योगर्लाकरे' पुस्तकों में सुश्रुत निदानस्थान वर्णित लक्षणों का तथा भावप्रकाश में शर्रीरस्थान वर्णित
लक्षणों का ही उल्लेख है ।

The milk which is normal in colour, smell, taste and touch, and when milked in a pot
filled with water mixes evenly, is known as pure milk. This milk provides nourishment and
good health to the child.

SuSruta says that the pure milk is cold, clean or free from impurities, whitishyellow
or white just like the colour of conch-shell, sweet in taste and free from discolouration,
when put in water, it mixes evenly, neither produces froth nor streaks, neither floats nor
settles down. This type of milk provides good health, growth and development of body as
well as strength to the child. है

Both the Vagbhatas agreeing with above say that it should not be vitiated by dosas.

Kasyapa without mentioning any physical characters says that the pure milk is that

which provides unobstructed, easy and good growth of strength, different body parts, lon-
gevity as well as good health to the child and does not cause any pain or trouble to the child

and wet-nurse.

Harita defining mrduksira as pure milk adds satwa and beauty also in the list which
are achieved by using pure milk. है

MadhavaNidana, Yogaratnakara and Bhawaprakasa have followed Susruta.

i) Except sidhu all other wines.

v) Milk.

वास्तविकता में पुनरुक्ति मात्र ही है, परन्तु पुस्तकों में पृथक्‌ वर्णन के काएण यहाँ भी उसका पृथक्‌ निर्देश कर दिया गया

क्षीरजनन द्र॒व्यों या आहार-विंहारादि का वर्णन किया है, वस्तुतः दोनों में कोई भेद न होने के काएण सभी का एक साथ

ही वर्णन दिया गया है।

Sugruta and Bhavaprakasa while describing clinical features and treatment of ksaya
(decrease) of various dhatus and upadhatus, have included stanya also. In subsequent de-
scription clinical features and treatment of stanyanasa have been described. Actually there
is no difference in both these conditions, however, since in the classics both have been
described separately, hence stanyaksaya and stanyanasa both are recapitulated here also.
Suéruta etc. have described the treatment of stanaynasa after elaborating its etiology, drugs
prescribed are likely to increase the amount of milk. Caraka has prescribed drugs for the
same purpose but without giving the name of disease or its etiology. Since aim of the drugs
prescribed by both is identical, hence all the prescriptions have been recapitulated at one
place.

Suéruta says that milk is the only congenial diet to the child, when mother or wet-nurse

is unable to feed, goat or cow’s milk should be given in appropriate amount. This substitute
feed is to be continued until the mother or wet nurse does not regain sufficient milk or else
till the child can not thrive properly without milk.

Both the Vagbhatas have said that goat or cow’s milk should be given to the child
making-it. similar to the mother’s milk, after medicating it either with decoction of laghu-
paficamila or both sthiras and mixed with sugar.

विमर्श (Comments)

अजा अथवा गौ के दुग्ध में स्त्री-दुग्ध की अपेक्षा प्रोभूजिन की मात्रा किश्चित अधिक तथा शर्करा को कम होती
है। साधन-काल में विभिन्न औषधियों के मिश्रण से सम्भवतः गौ या अजा दुग्ध की प्रोभूजिन की मात्रा कुछ कम एवं
वह सुपाच्य हो जाती हो, सिता का मिश्रण शर्कय की मात्रा की पूर्ति की दृष्टि से किया गया होगा, अत: महर्षि वाग्भट
का वर्णन अधिक युक्तिसंगत प्रतीत होता है।

In comparison to human milk, the milk of cow or goat contains more protein and less
carbohydrate (lactose). Treatment of milk,-with these drugs might be reducing amount of
protein and also converting it to more assimilable form. Mixture of sugar compensates
carbohydrate or in other words these alterations will make the milk of cow or goat more

similar to human milk. दि

This baldtaila cures the disorders of Sakha@ (extremities), kostha (abdomen), asthi
(bones), majja (bone marrow) and sird (veins), and also cures bahiraydma (opisthotonos),
antarayama (emprosthotonos), hanustambha (lock-jaw), sirobhrama (giddiness), ekapaksa-
badha (hemiplegia), fosa (emaciation), mlanaka (wasting), ardita (facial paralysis), gulma,
badhirya (deafness), vepana (tremors), apasmdra (epilepsy), unmdda (insanity), kativedana
(pain in sacral region), karnasitla (earache), SiroSiila (headache), bradhna (hemia),
vatakundalika (retention of urine due to obstruction in the passage), eighty disorders of
vata, twenty yonivydpad (gynec. disorders), Sukra dosas (seminal dise.) and all the graha
disorders. This should also be used in vrddhi (hernias), chronic fever, trtfyaka and
caturthaka fever (tertain and quartan fevers), vaginal pain of the woman having undergone
abnormal labour, Srama (tiredness), different types of atisGra (diarrhoea) and fevers, and all
types of kapha disorders.

It is contraindicated in ajirna (indigestion), krSata (emaciation), miircha (unconscious-
ness) and chardi (vomiting).

If the child (breast fed infant) becomes ill, Sodhana (use of purifying measures)
therapy given to the wet-nurse eradicates diseases of the child. However, if the dosas,
already accumulated in the child, are not removed, he is not cured, his future is destroyed
and his body does not grow properly. When the physician uses purifying measures in both
of them i.e. wet-nurse and child, then the child becomes immediately free from diseases.

As the rivers originate from hills, similarly wet-nurse is source of origin of all the
dosas. The dosas vitiated in the body of wet-nurse, reach of child (through milk) and trouble
him, thus till the Sodhana is not used in both (wet-nurse and child) of them, the diseases
of child are not cured.

स्तन्य एवं धात्री प्रकरण ६७३

महर्षि काश्यप ने वातज, पित्तज एवं कफज स्तन्यदुष्टि के विशिष्ट निदानों का वर्णन किया है जिनका उल्लेख विशिष्ट
शीर्षक के अन्तर्गत किया गया है।

Due to indigestion, consumption of non-congenial, unusual or unfavourable and in-
compatible food and over-eating; use of (excessive) salty, sour, hot, ksdra (alkaline) and
humid or putrified articles; diseases of body and mind, awakening in the night, over worry,
suppression of natural urges and attempt to excrete feces etc, in the absence of their urge;
use of paramanna (a dish made with rice, milk and sugar boiled together), dishes made of
Jaggery, oleo, curd, slowly formed curd or fish. abhisyandi (moisture producing) articles,
meat of wild or aquatic animals or animals frequenting marshy places, sleeping during day
after eating repeatedly, over use of wine, absence of exercise, trauma, anger, other diseases
and emaciation (either due to over use of purging etc. purifying measures or due to other
Causes), the dosas get vitiated. These vitiated dosas moving through kstravaha siras (milk
channels) vitiate the milk and produce eight types of milk disorders.

_ Susruta, Vagbhata I, Madhava Nidana, Bhavaprakaéa and Yogaratnakara etc. have also
given similar causes but in summarized way.

KaSyapa has described specific etiology of vitiation of milk by vata, pitta and kapha,
which is recapitulated under specific headings.

दूषित स्तन्य-पान जन्य सामान्य व्याधियाँ (Diseases caused by use of vitiated milk)

सभी आचार्यो ने स्पष्ट लिखा है कि वातादि दोषों से दूषित स्तन्‍्य का पान करने से, बालकों को उन दोषों से उत्पन्न
अनेकों शारीरिक व्याधियाँ उत्पन्न हो जाती है।

महर्षि काश्यप ने भी उपर्युक्त मत का अनुमोदन किया है।

Due to consumption of milk vitiated by vara etc. dosas, the child suffers from various
physical disorders of the same dosa, by which the milk is vitiated.

The milk vitiated by vayu is blackish brown or pinkish in colour, has kasdya anurasa
(feeling of kasaya or astringent taste aiter sucking the milk or after taste), is visada (pellucida
or non slimy), has indiscernible smell, is ruksa (dry or absence of unctuousness), drava
(liquid), frothy and laghu; does not give satisfaction to the child, produces emaciation and
various disorders of vata.

Susruta says that it has kasdya rasa (astringent taste) and if put in the water, it floats.

Vagbhata I corroborating Caraka has added that it has tikta anurasa also and produces
flatulence, oliguria and constipation, the milk floats in the water in scattered manner.
Vagbhata IE has also given almost similar description.

Kagyapa says that when mother or wet-nurse of the child constantly uses dry mode of
life and dietetics, does retention (suppression of natural urges), observes fasting and in-

The milk vitiated with pitta is black, blue, yellow or coppery in colour, possesses tikta
(bitter), amla (sour) and katu (pungent)anurasa (after taste), smells like blood or dead body
(stinking), is very hot and produces disorders of pitta.

Susruta says that it has amla and katurasa (taste); when put in the water, it produces
yellow streaks. Dalhana has added that it also has tikta rasa and produces blue or red streaks
also. .

Vagbhata I agreeing with Caraka has not described yellow colour but has added for-
mation of yellow streaks in water and vidaha (burning sensation) to the child. Vagbhata II
has also given almost similar description.

Kasyapa says that when wet-nurse becomes helpless by anger, heat of sun and hot
sour, salty and pungent diet, ill-digested food; eats again before digestion of previously
taken food; then her aggravated pitta, being thrown by vayu; following’ the veins (channels)
carrying breast-milk vitiates the breast-milk. Its (breast-milk’s) features are - when splashed

. in water it becomes greenish, reddish or slight blackish in colour. In taste it is pungent, sour,

salty and bitter and in touch it is hot.

By consuming this milk, the child is said to suffer from carmadala (allergic dermatitis)
due to pitta.

MadhavaNidana, Bhavaprakaéa and Yogaratnakara agreeing with above description
have added that the child consuming this milk, suffers from excessive pefspiration, diar-
thoea, kamala (jaundice) and other disorders of pitta. He feels excessive thirst and body

“parts bocome hot. Madhukosa commentary has mentioned that this milk settles down in the

water.

The milk vitiated with kapha is excessivly white and sweet. has lavana anurasa (after
taste), smells like ghrta, oil, fat or marrow, is picchila (slippery), has tantu (thread like
structures), settles down at the bottom when put in the water and produces various disorders
of kapha.

SuSruta says that it is ghana (thick), picchila and settles down in the water.

Vagbhata J has added that it is also vahala (viscous or thick), guru (heavy) and causes
over sleepiness to the child. Vagbhata IT has followed Susruta.

Kagyapa says that the wet-nurse who uses excessively heavy, sour, salty, sweet, mois-
ture producing articles, day-sleeping, indolence and noncongenials, her aggravated Slesma,
being thrown by vdyu, vitiates breast-milk. Its (breast-milk’s) features are—that it settles
down in the water, is thick in appearance and over unctuous, is cold and slimy in touch and
sweet in taste.

MadhavaNidana, Bhavaprakaéa and Yogaratnakara, giving almost similar description,
have added that the child suffers from excessive salivation, various disorders of kapha,
always feels sleepy, is numb or idiot, has swelling of face and eyes and suffers from
vomiting. Bhavaprakasga has mentioned edema and redness of eyes instead of edema of face
and eyes, which does not seem to be proper because redness is the characteristic of pitta
not of kapha.

While describing various pediatric disorders, Vagbhatas and Kasyapa have mentioned
balasosa and phakka alongwith carmadala (allergic dermatitis) respectively due to con-
sumption of milk vitiated with kapha. Since specific pediatric disorders do not come under
perview of this book, hence, are not being described here.

Bra एवं धात्री प्रकरण ६८३

पान से बालक को आम-युक्त, जल के समान (पतला), अनेकों प्रकार के वर्ण तथा वेदनाओं से युक्त तथा आधा बँधा
एवं आधा पतला मल होता है ।

Milk vitiated with all the dosas together exhibits physical characters as well as
symptomatology of all the dosas.

Vagbhata I has described this entity in detail in the treatment of milk-vitiation. He
writes that when wet-nurse consumes the dietetics capable of vitiating ail the dosas, then
these aggravated dosas reach chest and following milk carrying channels vitiate the milk
and produce mixed symptoms. When the mother due to ignorance, absence of constant care
and negligence suckles the child, then the child suffers from disease ksiralasaka having
various symptomatology. Vagbhata II has also mentioned that consumption of this type of
milk produces ksirdlasaka. Since the disease relates to the children, hence is not being
described here.

Child becomes lame, numb and dumb besides suffers from carmadala (allergic
dermatitis) by consuming the milk vitiated with tridosas as per opinion of Kasyapa.

Yogarataakara has mentioned that due to consumption of milk vitiated by tridosas, the
child passes stool which is mixed with dma (mucus), is liquid like water, has various
colours, is associated with different types of pain and is semisolid or half solid and half
liquid.

All these eight disorders are also caused by vata etc. three dosus. However, this
description is based on different physical characters of milk, which, inspite of having
dominance of a particular dosa, produce entirely different symptoms in the child.

These eight disorders are vaivarnya (discolouration) and vaigandhya or daurgandhya
(foul smelling) due to pitta; vairasya (tastelessness), phenasanghata (frothy) and rauksya
(dryness) due to vata and atisneha (excessive unctuous), paicchilya (slimy) and gaurava
(heaviness) due to kapha.

KaSyapa has mentioned only number as eight without any further description.

विमर्श (Comments)

संहिताओं में वर्णित विभिन्न wel एवं वर्णों का प्रत्यक्ष अनुभव के आधार पर निश्चित स्पष्टीकरण सम्भव नहीं है,
फिर भी बालक में होने वाले प्रभावों के आधार पर ऐसा मान सकते हैं कि समस्त वातजन्य स्तन्य-दुष्टियाँ दुग्ध में स्थित
पोषक तत्वों के अभाव को प्रदर्शित करती हैं, जिसके पान से बालक में कृशता आदि लक्षण उत्पन्न होते हैं। श्लेष्म-
जन्य स्तन्य-दुष्टि में सम्भवतः दुग्ध में अपेक्षाकृत वसा की मात्रा अधिक होती है, या कुछ अपचनीय द्रव्य उपस्थित रहते
हैं जिसके पान से बालक को वन तथा अन्य एलेष्प-विकार हो जाते हैं। यह भी सम्भव है कि इस दुग्ध से शिशु को
प्तिजनात्मक क्रिया (एलेंजिक मैनिफ़ेस्टेशेन) होती हो, जिसके कारण मुखशोफ आदि व्याधियाँ एवं वमन हो जाता

कफ के ही समकक्ष लगती है अतः इसे वातकफज मान सकते हैं।

On the basis of practical observations, it is not possible to offer any probable expla-
nation for various colours and tastes of milk described in Gyurvedika classics. However,
considering only clinical manifestations produced in the child, it can be presumed that
probably all the milk disorders produced by vata reflect some deficiency of nutrients in the
milk, naturally the child consuming this milk suffers from emaciation etc. disorders pro-
duced due to under-nourishment. Probably in all the milk disorders caused by kapha the
milk contains relatively more amount of fat or any such thing which child can not digest,
thus vomits the milk or else the child is allergic to this milk, thus, either ejects it or suffers
from edema of face etc. disorders. In milk disorders caused by pitta, probably the milk
carries bacteria or blood or pus from inflammation or abscess of breast. This infection
produces fever etc. in the child. Since the description of Kasyapa Samhita about milk
disorder caused by grahas is very short, hence probable congruence can not be established.

On the basis of physical character of milk explicit by their names and clinical mani-
festation produced, all the five disorders described by Harita can be included under the
disorders caused by dosas, such as alpa dosa may be considered under vatika; ghana dosas
under kaphaja; usna and amla dosas under pittaja disorders. Though the ksara is a property
of vata, however, the symptoms of the child show the features of kapha thus it may be
considered as vatakaphaja.

अष्टाज्जहदयकार ने भी व्याधि एवं दोपानुसार हो कर्म करने का निर्देश दिया है।

महर्षि काश्यप ने लिखा हैं कि कपाय-पात, वमन, विरेचन, पथ्य-भोजन तथा वाजीकरण द्रव्यों से सिद्ध स्तेह के

स्तन्यदोष वमन-योग्य कहे गए हैं. अर्थात्‌ इनमें वमन देना चाहिए।

While managing the vitiation of milk caused by either of the doga, specific attention
should be paid to the peculiarity of dosa i.e its situation in kostha (viscera) or Sakha
(extremities), the intensity of vitiation and also suitability for use of purifying measures.
According to the amount of vitiation of dosa (in excessive aggravation strong or drastic
purification and in slight aggravation mild purification) specific purifying measures i.e.
emesis in kapha, purgation in pitta and asthapana and anuvasana basti (evacuative and
nutritive enemas) in vitiation of vara should be given. Besides dosas, the prakyti (nature)
of wet-nurse should also be taken into account during use of purifying measures. With the
use of these specific purifying measures, the aggravated dosas are suppressed and vitiation
of milk is corrected.

The wet-nurse having already been given snehana (use of oleaginous substances)
should be given sudation followed by emesis. After proper emesis, methodical samsarjana-
krama (use of diet in gradual manner 1.०. first peya or liquid then manda or scum of boiled
rice then vilept or tice-gruel etc.) should be done and then, after readministering snehana,
the virecana (purgative drugs) should be given, giving due consideration to vitiated dosa,
kala (period or time of disease) and bala (strength of the woman). After proper purgation
and reapplication of samsarjana krama, the wise physician should prescribe such diet which
can suppress the dosa left-over after purification.

Suéruta says that to the wet-nurse after giving ghrta, emesis should be induced in the
evening by oral administration of decoction of nimba mixed with honey and mdagadhika.
Next day soup of mudga should be given in diet. In this way emesis should be induced for
three, four or six days. This should follow use of ghrta medicated with triphala. This is
general treatment. Specific treatment should be given on the basis of dosas. Dalhana has
clarified that the ghria to be given before emesis should be prepared with the drugs capable
of suppressing either the kapha or Samana drugs (drugs having properties of suppressing the
dosas). Usual period 1.6. in the morning when sun is red or golden, normally suitable for
administration of ghrta, is exception for wet nurse or is not suitable for her. Naturally, it
is to be given in the noon. After oleation, the sudation should also be given before emesis.
On the day of emesis diet should not be given. Emesis preceded with oleation and sudation
should be continued for three, four or six days till the kapha is completely expelled and
body is fully purified. Once the body is purified, the emesis should be stopped, otherwise

Following are the congenial things to be used in diet or drinks by the woman having

etc. cereals; sprouts of bamboo, tip of vetra and leaves or seeds of kaldya as vegetables after
proper preparation and mixing with fat; mudga (a kind of bean), harenuka (pea), kutlattha
(horse-bean) and masiira (pulse of lentil) for preparation of soup; surd, sauvtraka, maireya
and medaka (different types of wines) etc. wines and lasuna (garlic) and karafija. Soups
cooked with juice or decoction of nimba, tip of vetra, kulaka, vartaka and Gmalaka and
mixed with vyosa and rock salt should be used. Properly medicated meat of rabbit, partridge
and ena (variety of deer) should be given for eating.

sastika, mudga, kulattha, $ali tice, ghrta, milk of goat or cow, timely eating and rock salt
etc. should be used.

Bhavamisra has enumerated only soup of meat and mudga in the list.

परिशिष्ट - एक
(Appendix - I)
मान (Measures)

आयुर्वेदिक संहिताओं में तीन प्रकार के मानों का वर्णन है। पौतव मान (भार मान), द्रुवय मान (आयतन मान)
एवं पाथ्य मान (लम्बाई का मान) | सम्प्रति ग्रन्थ का सम्बन्ध केवल पौतव मान से है।

पौतव मान दो प्रकार का है, मागध एवं कालिज् 1 यद्यपि ame मान ही अधिक मान्य रहा है, परन्तु दाशम्लविक
या मीटरी पद्धति से तुलनात्मक विवरण करने पर कालिड्भ मान अधिक उपयुक्त ग्रतोत होता है, क्योंकि आजकल सामान्य
रूप में १ माष (मासा) को १ ग्राम तथा १ कर्ष को १० ग्राम मान लेते हैं जो कालिज्र मान सदृश (१० माप + १ कर्ष)
है। अत: मानतालिका कालिड्र मान के ही आधार पर वर्णित है ।

In ayurvedika classics three types of measures are described, i.e. pautava mana (mea-
sure of weight), druvaya mana (measure of volume) and payya mana (measure of length).
The present book is concerned only with pautava mana.

This pautava mana is of two types i.e. magadha and kalinga. Though earlier, magadha
was more acceptable to @yurvedika world, however, in attempting to correlate these mea-
sures with today’s prevalent measures of metric system, kdliftga mana is convenient, because
now a days generally one médsa (लव) is taken as one gramme and one fola or karsa as ten
grammes, which is in conformity with kalinga mana (ten masa = 1 karsa). Thus, present
table is given on the basis of kdlitga mana.

classics) system)
